item.description: {"id":"744000137379009","name":"Coordinateur/Coordinatrice de la communication, du Forum et des partenariats","uuid":"e018d928-b856-491c-a9a5-b5bf8d0d65f6","jobId":"55073ed8-ca1a-4916-ba78-3d5dc3d472e1","jobAdId":"5a7073f1-c9d6-4f33-b192-04bda60c8a84","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3049W","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10002602","valueLabel":"WISE"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"7038908","valueLabel":"General Administration"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"GA3","valueLabel":"GA3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-13T07:20:10.063Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000137379009-coordinateur-coordinatrice-de-la-communication-du-forum-et-des-partenariats","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000137379009-coordinateur-coordinatrice-de-la-communication-du-forum-et-des-partenariats?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/e018d928-b856-491c-a9a5-b5bf8d0d65f6?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. Le Centre de l’OCDE sur le bien-être, l’inclusion, la soutenabilité et l’égalité des chances ( WISE ) produit des données et dispense des conseils stratégiques en vue d’améliorer les conditions et la qualité de vie des individus sur les plans économique, social et environnemental. Le Centre WISE s’emploie à concevoir de nouvelles solutions politiques centrées sur la personne au regard de différentes problématiques, des perspectives économiques à la mobilité sociale, en passant par la solitude, le bien-être et la santé mentale. Ses travaux s’inscrivent dans le contexte des priorités d’action et des enjeux mondiaux d’aujourd’hui, notamment la crise du coût de la vie et les transitions démographique et numérique. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Le Centre WISE est à la recherche d’un/une Coordinateur/Coordinatrice de la communication, du Forum et des partenariats qui soit à la fois motivé(e) et créatif(ve), dont la mission consistera à aider la Cheffe de l’engagement et des opérations à optimiser la visibilité et l’impact des produits phares en organisant des activités et des événements promotionnels, en apportant son concours à l’organisation du Forum mondial de l’OCDE sur le bien-être et en contribuant à la préparation et à la coordination des activités de collecte de fonds. Le/La candidat(e) retenu(e) appréciera la perspective stimulante de travailler dans un environnement dynamique, où le rythme est soutenu, et dont l’esprit d’équipe est la composante fondamentale. Il/elle sera doté(e) de solides compétences rédactionnelles, et d’un excellent sens de la communication et des relations humaines ; il/elle saura faire preuve d’initiative et s’appuiera sur une bonne connaissance et une parfaite compréhension du fonctionnement d’une organisation internationale. Il/elle travaillera sous la supervision du/de la Chef/Cheffe des opérations et des partenariats du Centre WISE, et apportera son concours à une nouvelle communauté de pratique sur l’investissement social en coordination avec le/la Chef/Cheffe de projet concerné(e). Responsabilités principales Coordination de la communication En collaboration avec la Direction de la communication de l’OCDE et conformément au plan annuel de communication de l’Organisation, contribuer à l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de plans de communication pour les principaux résultats et événements, notamment en recensant les possibilités de promotion des résultats et en préparant les supports de communication ; préparer les rapports d’impact. Apporter son concours à la mise en application des stratégies relatives aux médias sociaux concernant les principaux résultats et les autres activités de communication, notamment en préparant des contenus et des visuels attrayants et en assurant la liaison avec d’autres directions. Contribuer à la rédaction et à la mise en forme des contenus de communication destinés aux brochures, blogs, podcasts et lettres d’information, en veillant à ce que tous les supports soient conformes aux normes et lignes directrices de l’OCDE en matière de communication telles que définies par COM, notamment s’agissant de la marque et de l’identité visuelle de l’OCDE. Prêter appui à la Coordinatrice des publications et des événements pour actualiser et tenir à jour les pages web de WISE et produire la lettre d’information mensuelle. Coordination des partenariats et relations avec l’extérieur Aider la Cheffe de l’engagement et des opérations à mettre en œuvre la stratégie de collecte de fonds du Centre, en collaboration avec les Chefs d’unité, notamment : en recensant et en recherchant des partenaires potentiels ; en formulant des suggestions pour améliorer la stratégie de relations extérieures du Centre ; en se tenant informé(e) des tendances actuelles en matière de philanthropie et en partageant des informations le cas échéant ; en préparant des supports de communication, des messages destinés aux partenaires et des documents d’information ; en participant à l’organisation de réunions de collecte de fonds ; et en assurant le suivi des partenaires existants et potentiels à l’appui de la gestion des relations et des possibilités de collaboration. Coordination du Forum et des événements Organiser les aspects logistiques et administratifs du Forum mondial de l’OCDE sur le bien-être : préparer un rétroplanning et veiller à ce que les principales échéances soient respectées ; préparer les instructions logistiques et de coordination pour l’organisation de l’événement sur place, y compris l’exposition prévue dans le cadre du Forum ; s’occuper des invitations et confirmations adressées aux intervenants et de la mise à jour du programme ; veiller au respect du protocole ; nouer et entretenir de bonnes relations de travail avec les co-organisateurs dans le pays hôte ; traiter toutes les demandes d’informations logistiques émanant des intervenants et des participants ; et se rendre sur le site du Forum pour assurer la liaison avec l’équipe logistique sur place tout au long de l’événement. Collaborer avec la Coordinatrice des publications et des événements afin de contribuer à l’organisation des événements et des réunions du Groupe de travail sur les statistiques relatives au bien-être. Animation de communauté Contribuer à l’organisation et à la coordination d’une nouvelle communauté de pratique sur l’investissement social en Europe. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire dans un domaine pertinent comme la communication, le marketing, le journalisme, les relations internationales ou tout autre domaine connexe. Expérience professionnelle Au moins deux années d’expérience pertinente de la communication, de l’organisation d’événements à haut niveau et/ou de la collecte de fonds à un niveau de responsabilité comparable, de préférence dans un cadre international. Excellentes compétences en matière de communication écrite : expérience de la conception et de la rédaction de messages à l’intention de différents publics et de la présentation d’informations dans un langage clair, accessible et convaincant. Aptitude avérée à proposer des idées et des solutions pratiques dans le cadre des activités de communication et de relations avec l’extérieur. Bon sens de l’organisation et capacité à produire des résultats de qualité en temps voulu dans des délais serrés. Outils Expérience des systèmes de gestion de contenus Expérience des systèmes d’optimisation, de l’établissement de rapports sur les processus et des tableaux de bord Une excellente connaissance et une grande expérience de la suite Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) et la maîtrise de logiciels tels qu’InDesign et Adobe Express seraient un atout. Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 1) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 1) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 1) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 1). Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. common problems. The International Energy Agency (IEA) is an intergovernmental organisation committed to advancing security of energy supply, economic growth and environmental sustainability through energy policy co-operation. The IEA operates as an autonomous body within the framework of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. Both the OECD and the IEA seek opportunities to work with an increasing number of non-members of growing importance to the world economy. The Agency aims to foster the contribution of the energy sector economic development and environmental sustainability. The IEA seeks to create a talent pool of energy analysts with experience in energy modelling and quantitative analysis to work with the team responsible for the Energy Technology Perspectives report and the State of Energy Innovation to contribute to research, analysis and modelling of regional and sectoral energy technology trends. The successful candidate will have a strong background in energy modelling and quantitative analysis with a focus on one or multiple sectors (transport, buildings, industry, alternative fuels supply, electricity generation). He/she will contribute to the analysis and drafting of IEA flagship and high-profile thematic publications across the whole range of energy technology topics, including but not limited to Energy Technology Perspectives, to the State of Energy Innovation, to sectoral tracking reports (such as the Global EV Outlook and the Global Hydrogen Review ) or to special reports and technology roadmaps. The selected candidates will be part of a team of enthusiastic professionals, reporting to the head of the Technology Innovation Unit, the head of the Hydrogen and Alternative Fuels Unit or the head of the Technology Supply Chains Unit within the Energy Technology Policy Division depending on the specific role. More information about the IEA and its work can be found at www.iea.org "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Energy Analysis and Drafting Assume responsibility for the technology characterization and modelling of one or several sub-sectors within relevant sectoral models of IEA Global Energy and Climate Model. Make significant contributions to quantitative analysis of topical energy technology and innovation issues for inclusion in IEA key publications. Provide intellectual input in developing thought leading analysis of future energy and technology trends. Stay abreast of relevant energy, technology and policy developments in member and non-member countries and with related academic work. Draft reports, working papers, prepare presentations and briefing notes for senior management. Liaison and Outreach Collaborate with other Directorates in the Agency, the OECD and other national and international organisations, the private sector and research bodies in the analysis of the role of energy technology in Member and non-Member countries. Participate in preparations for meetings of IEA standing committees, working parties and other groups as required; participate in relevant meetings of other international organisations; provide support for the development of reports, analyses and information items for these meetings. Work collaboratively with other IEA divisions, ensuring cross-Agency research and analytical projects that require professional input Maintain contacts with members of national delegations, other international organisations, representatives of private sector, and other institutions involved in energy market assessments. Promote the work of the IEA externally to a wide range of audiences through organising and participating in workshops, making presentations and holding bi-lateral meetings. item.title: Intern
item.description: Application Deadline: 31-12-2026 The WTO Secretariat maintains three internship programmes for post-graduate students and recent graduates with an advanced university degree wishing to gain practical experience and deeper knowledge of the multilateral trading system. Only a limited number of such internships is available. Internship selections are based on merit, eligibility criteria, academic qualifications, and expertise. The programmes, listed below, are designed to increase diversity at the WTO, and more information about each may be found in the links provided alongside: (1) The WTO Internship Programme is open to post-graduate students and recent graduates with an advanced university degree from all WTO members and countries or customs territories engaged in accession negotiations - WTO Internship Programme (2) The China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme – Up to ten internships offered under this programme annually, RESERVED FOR POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS OR RECENT GRADUATES WITH AN ADVANCED UNIVERSITY DEGREE FROM DEVELOPING COUNTRIES AND LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES - China's LDCs and Accessions Programme (3) the WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies - RESERVED FOR POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS FROM DEVELOPING COUNTRIES AND LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES WORKING ON THEIR PH.D THESIS - WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies RULES AND PROCEDURES FOR INTERNS (the following may vary, depending on the programme, so it is best to check the above links for information on a particular programme) Eligibility: A candidate must: be a national of a WTO member state or a country or customs territory engaged in accession negotiations have completed his/her undergraduate studies in a relevant discipline; either: be currently enrolled in a master's degree with at least one year completed; or have completed a master's degree programme and be enrolled in a higher-level postgraduate programme (including doctoral studies); or have completed a postgraduate degree (master's degree or PHD) within the past two years at the time of selection; and be at least 21 years at the time of the internship (and no older than 30 years old at the time of the internship for the China WTO Accessions Internship Programme and China General Internship Programme). A roster of suitable candidates is maintained from which interns are selected. In addition to the internship programmes, the need may also arise to recruit interns at short notice for specific tasks. These recruits will also be drawn from the roster. Names will be maintained on the roster for one year and no more. Contractual Terms and Conditions: An agreement will be established between the intern and the Director of the Human Resources Division, specifying the conditions of service and details of any remuneration. Paid interns receive a daily allowance of CHF 60 (including weekends and official holidays falling within the selected period – Except for interns recruited under the China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme who will receive a daily allowance of CHF 90 ). No other remuneration of any kind shall be paid. Internships take place in Geneva, Switzerland. Travel expenses to and from Geneva cannot be paid by the WTO ( Except for the China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme and for the WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies ) , and such travel is not covered by the Organization's insurance. Interns are responsible for their own insurance cover for illness and accidents for the duration of the internship. Please be aware that the cost of living in Geneva is quite high, and the allowance provided is intended as a supplement. It is important to ensure you have sufficient financial resources to support yourself during your time in the area. Internships are for a minimum of three months and up to a maximum of six months in total with no extension, are dependent on the needs of Divisions, and may commence at any time during the year. Depending on Divisional needs, an internship may be split between two Divisions (3 months and no less in each Division and not exceeding six months in total). In this case, the two internship assignments may be carried out at different times and not consecutively, as long as the applicant meets all the requirements for internship as per the "Eligibility" criteria set out above. It is not permissible to return to the programme at a later date after completing a full six-month internship programme, nor is it permissible to move from one programme to another following a six-month stint. An internship does not, in any way, entail the right to a vacancy in another part of the Secretariat. Interns may, nevertheless, apply to external vacancies. While working at the WTO, interns are not considered as officials or staff members, however, they shall be bound by the same duties and obligations as regular staff members. Interns are expected to work full-time and to carry out the duties assigned to them by their supervisor. On commencing the internship, and as applicable, depending on their nationality and any Swiss residence permit they may hold, interns may be issued with a Swiss legitimation card type "H" which serves as a work and residence permit for the duration of their internship. This link explains the responsibilities of holders of such a card and careful note should be taken of the information provided therein. At the end of the internship, the Supervisor responsible for an intern will write an evaluation report, and the intern will also be required to evaluate the internship. Both evaluations will be placed on file. An internship may be terminated by the WTO Secretariat or by the intern with one week's notice.

item.title: Policy Analyst - Economist - Social economy and social innovation
item.description: {"id":"744000139111660","name":"Policy Analyst - Economist - Social economy and social innovation ","uuid":"2b9d64ad-d5b9-4cd3-99fa-1fd4f97a2d65","jobId":"5dc222ae-6489-4ee3-927d-56499e1dbc7f","jobAdId":"6f34dc24-303d-4330-9399-29851033f8e1","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3303G","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000227","valueLabel":"CFE"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL5","valueLabel":"PAL5"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-22T15:58:36.112Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139111660-policy-analyst-economist-social-economy-and-social-innovation-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139111660-policy-analyst-economist-social-economy-and-social-innovation-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/2b9d64ad-d5b9-4cd3-99fa-1fd4f97a2d65?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The Centre for Entrepreneurship, SMEs, Regions and Cities (CFE) provides relevant and timely information, analysis, statistics, and recommendation to support governments’ efforts to improve the domestic and international performance of their policies in the area of entrepreneurs and SMEs, regions and cities, and tourism. It helps local and national actors work together to unleash the potential of entrepreneurs and SMEs, promote inclusive and sustainable regions and cities, boost local job creation, and implement sound tourism policies. It includes the Secretariats serving the Regional Policy Development Committee (RDPC) and its Working Parties, the Committee on SMEs and Entrepreneurship (CSMEE), the Tourism Committee and its Working Party, and the Local Economic and Employment Development (LEED) Directing Committee. The Local Employment and Social Innovation Division (LESI) within CFE focuses on supporting OECD member and partner countries at national, regional and local level to drive local economic development and growth, including through innovative approaches to local job creation, skills development, social inclusion, and place transformation. The division’s work involves analytical and policy-oriented research, conducted in a multicultural environment by a multi-disciplinary team of highly qualified and experienced staff. CFE is looking for an experienced, dynamic Policy Analyst/Economist to join the Local Employment, Skills and Social Innovation Division (LESI) to undertake research and analysis on social economy policies, including social entrepreneurship and social innovation. The selected candidate will undertake deep dives into the nature, contributions, challenges, and opportunities of the social economy in specific sectors (e.g., energy, care, housing), and its potential to generate employment/skills/job creation both as an employer and in its capacity to support public labour market programmes. Additionally, the work will focus on framework conditions such as taxation, legal frameworks, access to markets and finance, impact assessment, and the development of data, evidence and information at both national and sub-national levels. The selected candidate will report directly to the Head of the Social Economy and Innovation Unit. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Research, analysis and drafting Design, lead, and contribute to high-impact analytical and policy-oriented research and case studies on the social economy and social entrepreneurship, including framework conditions, sectoral applications in care, housing, energy, and retail, skills and employment strategies, integration of social economy actors in supply chains, data, digitalisation, AI, productivity and competitiveness. Analyse international evidence and data to inform policy analysis on the Unit’s topics (social economy, social entrepreneurship and social innovation) in OECD member countries and beyond. Draft and edit high-quality evidence-based assessments and tailored recommendations in substantive policy papers, case studies, and chapters in reviews or thematic reports, designed for policymakers and interested audience. Prepare other high-quality documents, including blogs, seminar proceedings, and policy messages based on research and relevant published material. Organise and summarise complex material in a clear manner for specialist and non-specialist audiences. Keep abreast of emerging research, exploratory work and evolving policies on local economic development, emanating from governments, other international organisations, non-governmental organisations, academia and the private sector. Strategic Leadership and Project Management Provide strategic input into the Committee on Local Employment and Economic Developpement (DC LEED), Programme of Work and Budget (PWB), and contribute to its implementation. Conduct and contribute to country level projects involving both qualitative and quantitative research, policy reviews, peer learning activities, and capacity building. Manage staff and consultants, including junior analysts, consultants, and external experts; ensure the delivery of quality outputs on time and within budget. Work collaboratively with other divisions and directorates on horizontal initiatives. Oversee the planning, execution and delivery of meetings and workshops on topics related to social economy and social entrepreneurship. Contribute to and oversee the preparation of presentations, speeches, briefings, press releases and other communication materials. Project management and fundraising Contribute actively to the management of projects, including ensuring the timely delivery of high-quality outputs. Actively support the Division’s and CFE’s fundraising efforts, including drafting project proposals and strengthening networks and engagement with potential donors as required. Supervise the work of junior staff, including interns, external and internal consultants as needed. Co-ordination, representation and liaison Support the activities of the Social Economy Unit, including organising webinars and in-person events, as well as contributing content to the social-economy online toolkit . Organise other project-related meetings and events, such as seminars, roundtables and workshops, as needed. Establish and maintain contacts with high-level representatives in relevant ministries and government agencies, as well as intergovernmental organisations and relevant stakeholders. Represent the OECD Secretariat at international conferences and contribute to raising the profile and disseminating LEED and CFE work at local, national and international levels. Collaborate with other Divisions and OECD directorates actively contributing to horizontal and multidisciplinary projects and outputs as needed. Other duties Provide general support to the activities of the Division as required, in particular as requested by LESI management and the Director’s office. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background An advanced university degree in a relevant area such as economics, public policy, social sciences, or a related field. Professional Background A minimum of three, but preferably at least five years of professional experience, acquired in an international organisation, a national or subnational government, or in a university or related research institution. Good knowledge of the OECD’s substantive work, especially related to the social economy. Excellent policy research and analytical skills proven by prior substantive contributions. Proven ability to draft analytical and policy-relevant reports and papers. Proven experience in dealing with stakeholders, including representatives of local or national governments. Ability to make and deliver effective presentations to policymakers, expert and non-expert audiences. Tools Strong knowledge of MS Office. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 2); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 2); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 2); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2). There are three possible levels for each competency. The level for each competency is determined according to the specific needs of each job role and its associated grade. To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies

item.description: {"id":"744000139113722","name":"Analyste des politiques - Économiste – Économie sociale et innovation sociale","uuid":"17bf5832-07b4-42bf-b0e3-365f9ffd6a35","jobId":"5dc222ae-6489-4ee3-927d-56499e1dbc7f","jobAdId":"21a4a997-f368-48df-bf7d-983f51fd3aed","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3303G","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000227","valueLabel":"CFE"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL5","valueLabel":"PAL5"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-22T15:58:59.659Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139113722-analyste-des-politiques-economiste-economie-sociale-et-innovation-sociale","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139113722-analyste-des-politiques-economiste-economie-sociale-et-innovation-sociale?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/17bf5832-07b4-42bf-b0e3-365f9ffd6a35?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. Le Centre pour l’Entrepreneuriat, les PME, les Régions et les Villes (CFE) fournit des données, des analyses, des statistiques et des recommandations pour soutenir les efforts des gouvernements visant à améliorer la performance nationale et internationale de leurs politiques dans les domaines de l’entrepreneuriat et des PME, des régions et des villes, ainsi que du tourisme. Il aide les acteurs locaux et nationaux à collaborer pour libérer le potentiel des entrepreneurs et des PME, promouvoir des régions et villes inclusives et durables, stimuler la création d’emplois locaux et mettre en œuvre des politiques touristiques solides. Il comprend les secrétariats servant le Comité de développement des politiques régionales (RDPC) et ses groupes de travail, le Comité des PME et de l’entrepreneuriat (CSMEE), le Comité du tourisme et son groupe de travail, ainsi que le Comité de pilotage du développement économique local et de l’emploi (LEED). La Division de l’emploi local et de l’innovation sociale (LESI), au sein du CFE, appuie les pays membres et partenaires de l’OCDE à l’échelle nationale, régionale et locale pour stimuler le développement économique local et la croissance, notamment par des approches innovantes en matière de création d’emplois locaux, de développement des compétences, d’inclusion sociale et de transformation des territoires. Le travail de la division implique des recherches analytiques et politiques, menées dans un environnement multiculturel par une équipe pluridisciplinaire composée de personnel hautement qualifié et expérimenté. Le CFE cherche un(e) analyste des politiques/économiste expérimenté(e) et dynamique pour rejoindre la Division de l’emploi local, des compétences et de l’innovation sociale (LESI), afin de réaliser des recherches et des analyses sur les politiques de l’économie sociale, y compris l’entrepreneuriat social et l’innovation sociale. Le/la candidat(e) sélectionné(e) approfondira l’analyse de la nature, les contributions, les défis et les opportunités de l’économie sociale dans des secteurs spécifiques (par exemple, énergie, soins, logement), ainsi que son potentiel à générer des emplois, des compétences et de la création d’emplois, tant en tant qu’employeur qu’en tant que soutien aux programmes publics du marché du travail. De plus, le travail portera sur les conditions-cadres nécessaires à l’économie sociale telles que la fiscalité, les cadres juridiques, l’accès aux marchés et au financement, l’évaluation de l’impact et le développement de données, de preuves et d’informations à l’échelle nationale et infranationale. Le/la candidat(e) sélectionné(e) travaillera directement sous la responsabilité du Chef de l’unité de l’économie sociale et de l’innovation. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Recherche, analyse et rédaction Concevoir, diriger et contribuer à des recherches analytiques et politiques à fort impact, ainsi qu’à des études de cas sur l’économie sociale et l’entrepreneuriat social, incluant les conditions cadres, les applications sectorielles dans les domaines du soin, du logement, de l’énergie et du commerce de détail, les stratégies de compétences et d’emploi, l’intégration des acteurs de l’économie sociale dans les chaînes de valeur, les données, la digitalisation, l’IA, la productivité et la compétitivité. Analyser les données internationales pour éclairer l’analyse des politiques sur les thèmes de l’Unité (économie sociale, entrepreneuriat social et innovation sociale) dans les pays membres de l’OCDE et au-delà. Rédiger et éditer des évaluations basées sur des preuves de haute qualité et des recommandations adaptées dans des documents politiques, des études de cas et des chapitres de revues ou de rapports thématiques, destinés aux décideurs et à un public intéressé. Préparer d’autres documents de qualité, tels que des blogs, des comptes rendus de séminaires et des messages politiques, basés sur la recherche et les publications pertinentes. Organiser et résumer des matériaux complexes de manière claire pour un public spécialisé et non spécialisé. Se tenir au courant des recherches émergentes, des travaux exploratoires et des politiques évolutives sur le développement économique local, émanant des gouvernements, d’autres organisations internationales, d’ONG, du monde universitaire et du secteur privé. Leadership stratégique et gestion de projets Contribuer au Comité de l’emploi local et le développement économique (DC LEED), au Programme de travail et au Budget (PWB), et à leur mise en œuvre. Mener et contribuer à des projets au niveau national impliquant des recherches qualitatives et quantitatives, des revues de politiques, des activités d’apprentissage par les pairs et le renforcement des capacités. Gérer le personnel et les consultants, y compris les analystes juniors, consultants et experts externes ; assurer la livraison de résultats de qualité dans les délais et dans le respect du budget. Collaborer avec d’autres divisions et directions sur des initiatives transversales. Superviser la planification, l’organisation et la réalisation de réunions et d’ateliers sur des thèmes liés à l’économie sociale et à l’entrepreneuriat social. Contribuer à la préparation et superviser la réalisation de présentations, discours, briefings, communiqués de presse et autres supports de communication. Gestion de projets et collecte de fonds Contribuer activement à la gestion des projets, en veillant à la livraison en temps voulu de résultats de haute qualité. Soutenir activement les efforts de fundraising de la Division et du CFE, notamment en rédigeant des propositions et en renforçant les réseaux et l’engagement avec les donateurs potentiels, selon les besoins. Superviser le travail du personnel junior, y compris les stagiaires, consultants externes et internes, selon les besoins. Coordination, représentation et liaison Appuyer les activités de l’Unité économie sociale et innovation, notamment en organisant des webinaires et des événements en présentiel, ainsi qu’en contribuant au contenu de la boîte à outils en ligne sur l’économie sociale . Organiser d’autres réunions et événements liés aux projets, tels que des séminaires, tables rondes et ateliers, selon les besoins. Établir et maintenir des contacts avec des représentants de haut niveau dans les ministères, agences gouvernementales, organisations intergouvernementales et parties prenantes pertinentes. Représenter le Secrétariat de l’OCDE lors de conférences internationales et contribuer à accroître la visibilité et la diffusion des travaux du LEED et du CFE à l’échelle locale, nationale et internationale. Collaborer activement avec d’autres divisions et directions de l’OCDE pour contribuer à des projets et résultats transversaux et pluridisciplinaires selon les besoins. Autres tâches Fournir un soutien général aux activités de la Division selon les besoins, en particulier à la demande de la direction de LESI et du bureau du Directeur. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil du/de la candidat(e) idéal(e) Formation Un diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur dans un domaine pertinent tel que l’économie, la politique publique, les sciences sociales

item.description: {"id":"744000139254149","name":"Product Engineer","uuid":"fdc9a26c-c655-465b-b433-fdbbf15d80e3","jobId":"46e3ae0c-cb4b-405c-a94f-3a2e0f607ee6","jobAdId":"d9bd9c2b-7c99-459e-9758-42f9b52ebaf9","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3281I","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":true,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10001129","valueLabel":"RPS"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"7038891","valueLabel":"Corporate Functions"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"CF4","valueLabel":"CF4"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-23T10:26:02.285Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139254149-product-engineer","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139254149-product-engineer?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/fdc9a26c-c655-465b-b433-fdbbf15d80e3?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The International Service for Remunerations and Pensions The International Service for Remunerations and Pensions (ISRP) delivers specialised services to international organisations, covering salary studies, statistical analysis, surveys, remuneration and pension management, legal advisory services and fund management. The ISRP is administratively attached to the OECD. Within the ISRP, the IT Services Unit (ITS) develops, maintains and modernises a portfolio of digital services that support the Service’s operational activities. These services include web applications used for pension administration, compensation and benefits, surveys, legal and document services, and related business processes. The Unit works across product design, software engineering, operations and continuous improvement to deliver reliable, secure and user-centred digital services. The ISRP is looking for a Product Engineer to strengthen the evolution of its digital services within its IT Services Unit (ITS), with a focus on the Service’s web applications portfolio. The selected candidate will take features from business needs to delivered software by leading product discovery with stakeholders, authoring functional specifications, designing accessible user experiences, and building and shipping web applications on a modern TypeScript stack. The selected candidate will contribute to the day-to-day operational running of ISRP digital services on the basis of documented procedures, and will play a central role in strengthening knowledge management and shared practices across the Service’s IT activities. Depending on the strengths of the selected candidate, the role may be weighted further towards engineering depth or towards product and portfolio ownership. The selected candidate will report to the ISRP Technical Lead Manager, under the general supervision of the Head of the IT Services Unit (ITS). "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Product discovery and functional design Lead product discovery with ISRP business units and stakeholders by facilitating workshops, conducting structured requirements gathering and modelling user journeys for core business applications in areas such as pension administration, compensation and benefits, surveys, and legal and document services. Author functional specifications and acceptance criteria, and drive them through to stakeholder sign-off and user acceptance testing. Analyse existing and legacy applications to recover and document business rules in preparation for their progressive replacement, and lead as a first priority the functional design of the rebuild of the IFI portal (International Financial Institutions). Maintain a structured and transparent product backlog informed by user feedback and business priorities, facilitate the intake and prioritisation of development requests across the Unit’s portfolio, and support fellow developers in structuring and managing their backlogs. Design, development and delivery Design and deliver user-centred and accessible interfaces for ISRP web applications and future digital services, in line with recognised accessibility standards. Develop, test and ship full-stack web applications on a modern TypeScript stack, in line with OECD security requirements, controls and development standards. Contribute to the progressive modernisation of the application portfolio through the replacement of end-of-life applications, with further rebuild projects to follow. Co-ordinate with internal and external service providers on integrations, environment provisioning and handovers. Operations, knowledge and continuous improvement Participate in the operational running of ISRP digital services on the basis of documented operating procedures, including scheduled application releases, monthly updates of application data and content, yearly campaigns to gather pension-related information and documents, and responses to user service requests. Continuously improve and automate these operating procedures to strengthen service reliability, repeatability and operational resilience. Establish and maintain the team’s knowledge infrastructure, including documentation standards, a central knowledge base, operating procedures and onboarding paths, to support auditability, service continuity and effective cross-coverage. Define, measure and report service and product key performance indicators, and prepare analyses and presentation materials to support management reporting and decision-making. Identify and propose improvements to workflows and tooling, and champion shared practices across the Service’s IT activities to contribute to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge-sharing. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Academic Background University degree in computer science, information technology, human-computer interaction or a closely related discipline, or equivalent professional experience demonstrating expertise in the field. Professional Background A minimum of three years’ proven professional experience building, shipping and operating web applications in production, ideally in a product-oriented role. Demonstrated experience leading product discovery with non-technical stakeholders, and authoring functional specifications and acceptance criteria through to sign-off. Experience designing accessible and user-centred interfaces, with familiarity with prototyping and user research practices. Demonstrated experience establishing or maintaining documentation and knowledge-management practices, including knowledge bases, standards and onboarding materials, supported by excellent written communication skills. Experience analysing legacy systems to recover business rules and specify their replacement would be an advantage. Experience in an international and cross-cultural setting would be preferable. Tools Strong proficiency in TypeScript and React, with production experience of Next.js or a comparable React framework, and working knowledge of Node.js back-end development, REST APIs and relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL. Proficiency with prototyping and design tools such as Figma, and with recognised web accessibility standards including WCAG and/or RGAA. Familiarity with source control and continuous integration and delivery tools such as GitLab, Azure DevOps or GitHub. Comfort working in Linux environments, including application deployment, reading logs and diagnostics, and command-line usage. Familiarity with collaboration and documentation platforms such as Confluence and Jira, and with Microsoft 365. Knowledge of PHP and Symfony would be a strong asset. Knowledge of automated testing practices such as Vitest, Jest or Playwright, or of Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, would be an asset. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Additional Information","text":" Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 2); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 3); Achieve Results (Level 3); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 3). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies . Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. Closing Date This vacancy should be filled as soon as possible, and applications should reach us no later than midnight 30 August 2026 (Paris time). Contract Duration 24 month fixed-term appointment, with the possibility of renewal to a maxim

item.description: {"id":"744000139251661","name":"Ingénieur(e) web orienté(e) produit","uuid":"27617bf2-6f2f-4017-ab14-d25b0e37409f","jobId":"46e3ae0c-cb4b-405c-a94f-3a2e0f607ee6","jobAdId":"5f017317-a337-47b9-ba81-f7a3d0755f81","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3281I","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":true,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10001129","valueLabel":"RPS"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"7038891","valueLabel":"Corporate Functions"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"CF4","valueLabel":"CF4"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-23T10:26:29.267Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139251661-ingenieur-e-web-oriente-e-produit","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139251661-ingenieur-e-web-oriente-e-produit?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/27617bf2-6f2f-4017-ab14-d25b0e37409f?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. Le Service international des rémunérations et des pensions (SIRP) fournit des services spécialisés aux Organisations coordonnées et aux Organisations associées, couvrant les études salariales, les analyses statistiques, les enquêtes, la gestion des rémunérations et des pensions, les services de conseil juridique et la gestion de fonds. Le SIRP est administrativement rattaché à l’OCDE. Au sein du SIRP, l’Unité des services informatiques (ITS) développe, maintient et modernise un portefeuille de services numériques soutenant les activités opérationnelles du Service. Ces services comprennent des applications web utilisées pour l’administration des pensions, la gestion des rémunérations et avantages sociaux, les enquêtes, les services juridiques et documentaires, ainsi que les processus métier associés. L’Unité intervient dans la conception de produits, l’ingénierie logicielle, les opérations et l’amélioration continue afin de fournir des services numériques fiables, sécurisés et centrés sur les utilisateurs. Le SIRP recherche un(e) Ingénieur(e) web orienté(e) produit afin de d’accompagner l’évolution de ses services numériques au sein de l’Unité des services informatiques (ITS), avec une attention particulière portée au portefeuille d’applications web du Service. La personne retenue transformera les besoins métier en solutions logicielles déployées, en pilotant la découverte produit avec les parties prenantes, en rédigeant les spécifications fonctionnelles, en concevant des interfaces utilisateur accessibles et en développant puis déployant des applications web sur une pile technologique moderne fondée sur TypeScript. Elle contribuera également à l’exploitation quotidienne des services numériques du SIRP conformément aux procédures documentées et jouera un rôle central dans le renforcement de la gestion des connaissances et des pratiques partagées au sein des activités informatiques du Service. Selon son profil, le poste pourra être davantage orienté vers l’expertise technique ou vers la gestion du produit et portefeuille applicatif . La personne retenue sera placée sous l’autorité du Responsable technique du SIRP, sous la supervision générale du Chef de l’Unité des services informatiques. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Découverte produit et conception fonctionnelle Piloter les activités de découverte produit avec les unités métier et les parties prenantes du SIRP en animant des ateliers, en recueillant les besoins de manière structurée et en modélisant les parcours utilisateurs pour les applications métier essentielles, notamment dans les domaines de l’administration des pensions, des rémunérations et avantages, des enquêtes et des services juridiques et documentaires. Rédiger les spécifications fonctionnelles et les critères d’acceptation, puis les conduire jusqu’à leur validation par les parties prenantes et aux tests d’acceptation utilisateurs. Analyser les applications existantes afin de reconstituer et documenter les règles métier en vue de leur remplacement progressif, et conduire en priorité la conception fonctionnelle de la refonte du portail IFI (Institutions financières internationales). Maintenir un backlog produit structuré et transparent fondé sur les retours utilisateurs et les priorités métier, faciliter la réception et la priorisation des demandes de développement au sein du portefeuille de l’Unité et accompagner les autres développeurs dans la gestion de leurs backlogs. Conception, développement et livraison Concevoir et livrer des interfaces accessibles et centrées sur l’utilisateur pour les applications web du SIRP et les futurs services numériques, conformément aux normes reconnues d’accessibilité. Développer, tester et mettre en production, du front-end au back-end, des applications web full stack sur une pile technologique moderne fondée sur TypeScript. dans le respect des exigences de sécurité, des contrôles et des standards de développement de l’OCDE. Contribuer à la modernisation progressive du portefeuille applicatif en remplaçant les applications arrivées en fin de vie, d’autres projets de refonte devant suivre. Coordonner les activités avec les prestataires internes et externes concernant les intégrations, la mise à disposition des environnements et les transferts de responsabilité. Exploitation, gestion des connaissances et amélioration continue Participer à l’exploitation des services numériques du SIRP conformément aux procédures documentées, notamment les mises en production planifiées, les mises à jour mensuelles des données et contenus applicatifs, les campagnes annuelles de collecte d’informations et de documents relatifs aux pensions, ainsi que le traitement des demandes de support utilisateurs. Améliorer et automatiser en permanence ces procédures opérationnelles afin de renforcer la fiabilité, la reproductibilité et la résilience des services. Mettre en place et maintenir l’infrastructure de gestion des connaissances de l’équipe, notamment les normes documentaires, une base de connaissances centralisée, les procédures d’exploitation et les parcours d’intégration, afin de garantir la traçabilité, la continuité des services et la polyvalence des équipes. Définir, mesurer et communiquer les indicateurs clés de performance des services et produits, et préparer des analyses et présentations à l’appui du reporting et de la prise de décision. Identifier et proposer des améliorations des processus et des outils, et promouvoir les bonnes pratiques communes au sein des activités informatiques du Service afin de favoriser une culture d’apprentissage continu et de partage des connaissances. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Formation Diplôme universitaire en informatique, technologies de l’information, interaction humain-machine ou dans une discipline étroitement liée, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente démontrant une expertise dans le domaine. Expérience professionnelle Au moins trois années d’expérience professionnelle confirmée dans le développement, le déploiement et l’exploitation d’applications web en production, idéalement dans un rôle orienté produit. Expérience démontrée dans l’animation des activités de découverte produit avec des parties prenantes non techniques ainsi que dans la rédaction de spécifications fonctionnelles et de critères d’acceptation jusqu’à leur validation. Expérience dans la conception d’interfaces accessibles et centrées sur l’utilisateur, avec une bonne connaissance du prototypage et des méthodes de recherche utilisateur. Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place ou la gestion de pratiques documentaires et de gestion des connaissances, notamment de bases de connaissances, de standards documentaires et de supports d’intégration, appuyée par d’excellentes compétences rédactionnelles. Une expérience dans l’analyse de systèmes hérités afin de reconstituer les règles métier et spécifier leur remplacement constituerait un avantage. Une expérience dans un environnement international et multiculturel serait appréciée. Outils et technologies Excellente maîtrise de TypeScript et React, avec une expérience de production sur Next.js ou un framework React comparable, ainsi qu’une bonne connaissance du développement back-end Node.js, des API REST et des bases de données relationnelles telles que PostgreSQL ou MySQL. item.title: E T Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, www.worldbank.org E astern and Southern Africa Regional Context The Eastern and Southern Africa (AFE) region is diverse, spanning low-income and lower-middle-income countries and a number of upper-middle-income borrowers, with wide variation in health outcomes, fiscal space, and institutional capacity. Many countries face a high and evolving burden of disease alongside persistent inequities in access and quality, while also managing recurrent shocks, including climate-related hazards, epidemics, and food and fuel price volatility. In this context, the World Bank supports governments through analytics, policy dialogue, and financing to strengthen human capital and build more resilient health systems and essential public health functions. Through its Health, Nutrition, and Population (HNP) Global Practice, the World Bank supports countries’ efforts towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and providing quality, affordable, equity-focused health services to everyone regardless of their ability to pay by strengthening primary health care systems and reducing the financial risks associated with ill-health. Some of the ongoing health and nutrition challenges in the AFE region include: • Triple burden of disease and epidemiological transition: a continuing burden of communicable diseases (including HIV, TB, malaria and outbreaks), persistently high maternal, newborn and child mortality in many settings, and a rapidly growing burden of NCDs and injuries—often coexisting within the same populations and health systems. • Health system constraints and inequities: persistent gaps in access to quality essential services, especially for rural, remote, and vulnerable populations, driven by constraints in the health workforce, medicines and supply chains, service readiness, governance and accountability, and limited fiscal space and financial protection for households. • Nutrition and food insecurity: high levels of child stunting and micronutrient deficiencies in several countries, alongside rising overweight/obesity, compounded by food price shocks and climate variability that affect diets and worsen vulnerability throughout the life course. Summary of Botswana and Southern Africa Health Portfolio The World Bank’s health portfolio in Botswana combines investment financing with targeted technical assistance (TA) and analytics to advance the Government’s priorities on UHC, primary health care revitalization, and health security. The portfolio is anchored by the Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPRR) Project, which supports preparedness and response; strengthened surveillance, laboratory, and emergency management systems; and investments in core enablers, including digital public health infrastructure and availability of quality data. In parallel, the World Bank provides TA supporting sector planning and governance such as development of the Health Sector Strategic Plan, digital health and data use (interoperability, registries, and routine data quality and use), and improvements in supply chain performance and regulatory systems for health products. This work is complemented by analytics to inform reforms and investments, including on health financing and efficiency, equity, and service delivery performance to strengthen human capital and system resilience. Across southern Africa, the World Bank’s health engagement in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho combines investment lending with analytical and advisory services to strengthen primary health care, improve quality of care, and build more resilient health systems. In Lesotho, the portfolio includes an active health and nutrition system strengthening project focused on expanding coverage and improving the quality of essential maternal and child health, nutrition, and NCD services, alongside reforms to strengthen stewardship and service delivery readiness. There are opportunities to support the preparation of new operations and enhance the scope of TA and advisory work in southern Africa. In South Africa and Namibia, support is anchored in policy dialogue and analytics, including public expenditure and efficiency work, to inform reforms that expand effective coverage, reduce inequities, and improve the sustainability of health financing. Objectives and Scope of Work In light of the growing health portfolio, the HAEH2 team seeks an Extended-Term Consultant (ETC) with experience as a Health Specialist/Economist to provide day-to-day technical and operational support to HNP task teams and Government counterparts, primarily in Botswana and, as needed, across the southern Africa portfolio. The scope of work includes: • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in Botswana. The ETC will support implementation of the Botswana health portfolio (including the HEPRR project) by monitoring progress against the results framework (including support to M E, data quality, and results reporting) and follow-up on agreed actions; supporting planning and delivery of implementation support missions; and contributing to key operational deliverables (aide memoires, management briefs, and client-facing communications). The ETC will help convene consultations with the Ministry of Health and other stakeholders, monitor progress, and coordinate with fiduciary, safeguards, and technical colleagues to ensure timely, integrated support. • Help ensure close coordination with government, development partners, and the CMU and World Bank teams across other sectors in Botswana. The ETC will facilitate coordination and information flow across the Ministry of Health and other relevant agencies, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the Country Management Unit and colleagues in other sectors) to align priorities, timelines, and implementation support. The ETC will play a pivotal role in providing strategic sectoral guidance to the CMU and provide key inputs into country management reviews and documents. • Support policy dialogue with the Ministry of Health, relevant national institutions, and other stakeholders. The ETC will support policy dialogue by preparing briefs, talking points, and presentations, synthesizing implementation experience, sector analytics, and international lessons. The ETC will help translate discussions into clear decisions and follow-up actions to inform priority reforms in primary health care, health security, health financing, and other system strengthening areas. • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in southern Africa, as needed. The ETC will support task teams in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho, including assistance with preparation and follow-up of missions and key deliverables, and contributions to selected analytical and advisory work (e.g., service delivery performance, health financing and efficiency, and health security). Duties and Accountabilities: The ETC’s key tasks and activities will include but are not limited to: • Support implementation support for HEPRR and other Botswana portfolio activities, including monitoring implementation and results; consolidating inputs across technical, fiduciary and ESF colleagues; and proactively following up with counterparts on agreed actions. • Contribute to the planning, preparation, and follow-up of missions, technical consultations, and key portfolio engagements, including drafting agenda/talking points, preparing briefing packages, and drafting aide memoires and progress reports, and management updates as requested by Task Team Leaders. • Support monitoring and evaluation (M E) and results reporting for the portfolio, including maintaining an M E implementation plan, supporting updates to the results framework and indicator definitions as needed, compiling and quality-checking data and narrative inputs for progress reporting. • Provide technical inputs to project implementation, including review of technical specifications and Terms of References for goods and services (e.g., medical and laboratory equipment, digital systems, and technical assistance), and advise on alignment with good practice, user requirements, and World Bank procurement principles (in coordination with procurement specialists). • Support stakeholder coordination across Government, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the CMU and other sectors) by preparing coordination notes, documenting decisions, and escalating issues requiring management attention. • Contribute to selected analytical and advisory activities (ASA), including literature and data review, drafting sections of technical notes and reports, and supporting quality assurance to ensure analytical rigor and consistency of messaging. • As needed, provide operational and analytical support to the southern Africa health portfolio (South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho). • Maintain well-organized records of key documents and correspondence; support timely sharing of information within task teams; and contribute to knowledge management by capturing lessons learned and good practices.

item.title: Economist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/home Global practice for Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) The Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) Department leads the World Bank Group’s policy dialogue and engagement with countries to strengthen macro-fiscal foundations, including debt sustainability, debt management, public expenditure, and domestic resource mobilization, trade and investment and to accelerate job creation and inclusive growth. FPG links the macroeconomic dialogue with programs focused on expanding the role of the private sector in economic development. In its day-to-day engagement, FPG supports Ministries of Finance, Planning, Economy, Industry and Trade, and Production in pursuing reform agendas that strengthen job creation through inclusive, private sector-led growth. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/topic/fiscal-policy-and-growth Background and general description The FPG unit for Southern Africa and East Africa (EAEM2) is looking for a local economist to be based in Maputo, Mozambique. The selected candidate will contribute substantially to analytical work and lending operations. She or he will report to the FPG Practice Manager covering the EAEM2 unit, which comprises 14 countries across three Country Management Units: AECS1 (South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia), AECS2 (Mozambique, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles), and AECC2 (Angola, Democratic Republic of Congo, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Burundi). The unit has a strong focus on prudent macro-fiscal policies, structural reforms, inclusive growth, and job creation. The World Bank’s FPG engagement in Mozambique supports the country’s efforts to strengthen macroeconomic stability, fiscal and debt sustainability, domestic resource mobilization, and the management of natural-resource revenues, while fostering a more diversified, productive, and job-rich economy. The work program combines policy dialogue, financing operations, technical assistance, and analytical work, including macroeconomic monitoring, Macro Poverty Outlooks, economic updates, public finance analysis, and work on growth and jobs. Particular attention is given to translating Mozambique’s natural-resource potential into broad-based development outcomes, strengthening institutions and fiscal frameworks, and supporting private-sector development and economic resilience. As an Economist for EAEM2, you will contribute to the country team covering Mozambique and, as needed, to the regional FPG team working on other countries. The Economist will be based in Maputo and work closely with the Division Director, Senior Country Economist, Lead Economist, and other members of the country team, and will report to the FPG Practice Manager. The position requires strong analytical capability, sound judgment, close engagement with government counterparts and development partners, and the ability to deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines. The Country Economist will: • Contribute to FPG Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA) in macroeconomic and fiscal management, macroeconomic modelling, data analysis, public finance, growth, jobs, and private-sector development; • Collect, analyze, validate, and maintain economic, fiscal, debt, external-sector, financial, and socioeconomic data related to Mozambique, and communicate findings clearly through tables, charts, briefs, presentations, and analytical notes; • Maintain macroeconomic databases and regularly prepare updated medium-term macroeconomic projections, using economic and financial models and World Bank toolkits; • Contribute to the preparation of Macro Poverty Outlooks, economic updates, public finance and growth diagnostics, Debt Sustainability Analysis, Country Policy and Institutional Assessments, policy notes, and other country and regional knowledge products; • Contribute to the design and implementation of financing operations, including Development Policy Financing, to the design and implementation of SDFP Performance and Policy Actions, and to technical assistance supporting the Government’s reform program; • Serve as a task leader or team member for country-specific financing operations and/or analytical and advisory services, commensurate with experience; • Support the Country Management Unit in implementing the World Bank program in Mozambique and contribute to cross-practice collaboration around country priorities; • Contribute to policy dialogue with government counterparts on macro-fiscal policy, debt, domestic revenue mobilization, natural-resource revenue management, structural transformation, productivity, and job creation; • Establish and strengthen partnerships with bilateral and multilateral agencies, research institutions, academia, civil society, and other stakeholders, helping leverage knowledge and resources; • Contribute to the dissemination of World Bank knowledge products to government, development partners, civil society, academia, the private sector, and other key audiences; and • Contribute to regional and cross-country analytical and operational work within EAEM2 as business needs require.
