Unit Context The Enterprise Architecture (ITSET) unit enables strategy execution by connecting business goals with technology investments, frameworks, and delivery models. ITSET ensures coherence, interoperability, and business value realization through standards, reference architecture, and governance. The unit drives portfolio alignment, process optimization, and adoption of data-driven practices across the WBG. Duties and accountabilities: The Associate Senior Enterprise Architect • Defines and governs portfolio architectures and product architectures to enable as well as accelerate solution delivery with the ITS portfolio by leveraging enterprise architecture frameworks, accelerators, guidelines and best practices while ensuring compliance with enterprise guardrails and architectural standards. • Drives enterprise-wide adoption and optimization of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), AI/ML and Agentic AI capabilities — including services such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Azure AI Foundry, Azure AI Agent Service, and Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — and modern integration patterns to enable secure, scalable, and intelligent solutions across the organization. • Translates organizational strategy, business priorities, and digital transformation goals into coherent, actionable enterprise architecture direction and technology roadmaps — including strategies for multi-agent orchestration, autonomous workflows, and AI-augmented business processes. • Evaluates and applies industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices — including agentic AI orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, Microsoft Agent Framework (converging AutoGen and Semantic Kernel), Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), Strands Agents SDK, and OpenAI Agents SDK pragmatically to advance the World Bank Group's digital transformation and modernization objectives. • Produces high-quality, traceable architecture artifacts — including reference architectures, design patterns, solution guides, decision frameworks, and agentic AI governance models — that enable delivery teams to execute effectively and consistently across cloud-native and multi-agent environments. • Collaborates effectively with business leaders, solution architects, platform engineers, and Agile teams to co-create solutions — including AI agent workflows, RAG pipelines, multi-agent systems, and human-in-the-loop designs — that balance innovation, feasibility, and enterprise alignment. • Acts as an enterprise enabler and trusted advisor, aligning diverse stakeholders around shared architectural standards, patterns, and governance practices — including agent lifecycle governance, agent identity and access management, and responsible AI guardrails. • Demonstrates openness to feedback, fosters inclusive decision-making, and integrates diverse technical and business perspectives into architectural recommendations. • Balances innovation with risk management, regulatory compliance, security, and operational stability — including AI content safety guardrails, agent policy enforcement, FinOps for AI workloads, and agent observability — in all architectural decisions and guidance. • Architects and governs enterprise integration strategies leveraging API management platforms (Azure API Management, AWS API Gateway, MuleSoft, Apigee), integration Platform-as-a-Service (iPaaS) solutions (Azure Logic Apps, Azure Integration Services, AWS Step Functions, Workato), and enterprise service buses to enable seamless, secure, and governed connectivity across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. • Designs and enforces event-driven architectures (EDA) using cloud-native messaging and streaming services — including Amazon EventBridge, Amazon Kinesis, Azure Event Grid, Azure Service Bus, Google Pub/Sub, and Apache Kafka — to enable real-time, loosely coupled, and resilient enterprise integrations at scale. • Leads the definition and governance of API-led connectivity patterns — including experience APIs, process APIs, and system APIs — establishing API lifecycle management standards, versioning strategies, contract-first design, and developer portal governance to promote reusability and interoperability across enterprise systems. • Drives cloud integration architecture for multi-cloud and hybrid environments, defining patterns for cross-cloud data synchronization, identity federation (Entra ID, AWS IAM Identity Center, GCP Identity), network interconnectivity (ExpressRoute, Direct Connect, Cloud Interconnect), and workload portability to ensure operational resilience and vendor risk mitigation. • Defines enterprise integration standards for data interoperability and exchange, including master data management (MDM) integration, ETL/ELT pipeline architectures (Azure Data Factory, AWS Glue, dbt), real-time data streaming, and canonical data models to ensure data consistency, quality, and traceability across enterprise systems and analytics platforms. • Governs the adoption and architectural alignment of low-code/no-code integration platforms (Power Automate, Power Platform, Copilot Studio) and RPA tools within enterprise workflows, ensuring they comply with security, data governance, and architectural standards while accelerating citizen-led automation and business process digitization. • Establishes and enforces integration security and governance standards — including OAuth 2.0, mTLS, API key management, rate limiting, payload encryption, and zero-trust network access — to ensure all enterprise integrations meet organizational security policies, data protection requirements, and regulatory compliance mandates. Enterprise Architecture Development • Leads the development, evolution, and continuous improvement of enterprise architecture frameworks, reference architectures, design patterns, and governance guidelines to ensure technology initiatives are strategically aligned with business objectives. • Oversees the creation and maintenance of comprehensive architecture documentation — including standards, blueprints, decision records, and solution guides — to promote knowledge sharing, institutional learning, and consistent adoption across teams. • Establishes and maintains an enterprise architecture artifacts catalog encompassing reference architectures, best practices, guardrails, and reusable patterns to strengthen the EA foundation and enable enforceable governance. Architecture Analysis Innovation • Guides the assessment and rationalization of existing IT infrastructure, platforms, and applications to identify opportunities for modernization, optimization, and cost efficiency. • Manages and conducts architectural reviews and Well-Architected Framework assessments, ensuring adherence to enterprise standards, security requirements, and organizational goals. • Monitors industry trends, emerging technologies — including Agentic AI, cloud-native architectures, and advanced integration paradigms — to proactively identify opportunities for innovation, capability enhancement, and competitive advantage. • Evaluates vendor solutions, platforms, and tools through structured decision frameworks and comparative analyses to inform enterprise technology selection and adoption strategies. Stakeholder Engagement • Communicates architectural strategies, trade-offs, and recommendations to executive leadership and stakeholders with clarity, ensuring alignment and informed decision-making across the organization. • Manages collaboration with business leaders and program teams to elicit, analyze, and translate business requirements and strategic priorities into actionable technical specifications and architecture direction. • Oversees partnership with Agile and SAFe teams to ensure architectural alignment, scalability, technical guidance, and governance ac

The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context: ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context: The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) provides digital support for global and country-specific products, aiding thousands of task teams and country management units in better planning, tracking, and managing their operations, thereby improving country engagement. Additionally, ITSCE enables geospatial capabilities through self-service tools and analytics, allowing teams to monitor project preparation and implementation from anywhere. The Geospatial Solutions team is responsible for the delivery, evolution, and adoption of enterprise geospatial products and services that support operational, analytical, and decision-support needs across the World Bank Group. The team develops and manages platforms that integrate geospatial, statistical, and development data to generate location-based insights supporting country programs, project design and implementation, infrastructure planning, climate resilience, disaster risk management, results monitoring, and other operational priorities. The ITSCE unit is seeking a Product Manager who is passionate about geospatial technologies and committed to maximizing business value through technology delivery. The role will lead business engagement and product strategy for the Geospatial Solutions portfolio, working closely with operational stakeholders, Country Management Units, Global Practices, regional teams, and technology partners to identify opportunities, shape demand, and ensure geospatial investments deliver measurable operational impact. The Product Manager will play a key role in connecting development and operational needs with innovative geospatial capabilities while ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and technology strategy. Duties and responsibilities • Leads the product portfolio for Geospatial Solutions, working with agile team and Country Management Units, Global Practices, Regional teams, and operational stakeholders to identify high-value opportunities where geospatial solutions can improve development outcomes, operational efficiency, decision-making, and project delivery. • Deep understanding of business and operational priorities across regions and sectors, and translates these needs into geospatial product strategies, roadmaps, and investment priorities. • Defines and communicates a clear, scalable product vision and roadmap for Geospatial solutions that balances operational demand, delivery capacity, organizational priorities, and long-term sustainability. • Builds strategic relationships across the WBG and with external partner organizations to advance the adoption and impact of geospatial solutions. • Promotes the use of geospatial intelligence and spatial analytics in support of country programs, project implementation, climate resilience, disaster response, infrastructure planning, and monitoring and evaluation activities. • Provides leadership across agile teams, ensuring alignment, coordination, and execution so that development cycles translate into timely, high-quality product releases and operational value. • Facilitates continuous stakeholder engagement and feedback, identifies emerging opportunities, and evolves the product roadmap to maximize adoption and business impact across operational teams. • Designs governance structures and operating models for geospatial products, ensuring compliance with WBG policies, technology standards, and data management requirements while maintaining agility and innovation. • Oversees vendor and partner relationships, ensuring timely access to specialized geospatial expertise, technical capabilities, and delivery support. • Evaluates and recommends strategic investments that accelerate product development, improve scalability, enable replication across regions and business units, and effectively manage technical debt. • Monitors product-level financials and investment performance, ensuring resources are utilized effectively and aligned with business value and operational outcomes. • Leads complex, cross-functional initiatives involving software engineers, data scientists, GIS specialists, solution architects, business stakeholders, and operational teams to deliver impactful geospatial capabilities. • Identifies systemic challenges and cross-cutting opportunities across sectors and regions, applying structured analysis and strategic thinking to accelerate the adoption of geospatial solutions throughout the World Bank Group. • Represents the Geospatial Solutions portfolio in strategic discussions and governance forums, advocating for investments and priorities that support operational effectiveness and development impact.

Unit Context The Technology Platforms Team (ITSPL) is anchored in the Chief Technology Officer (ITSTO) division in ITS. ITS Technology Office (ITSTO) drives technology-enabled innovation and delivers the digital backbone for WBG's mission. It develops future-ready technology strategy, modernizes infrastructure, manages innovation, and fosters agility. The unit collaborates across the organization to leverage technology as a force multiplier, accelerating development impact and digital transformation globally. ITSPL delivers secure, cloud-first IT platforms with automation, self-service, and Platform Engineering (IaC). It manages databases, integrations, cloud ops to ensure reliable, scalable, cost-effective alignment with enterprise standards. The primary programs that the ITSTO unit is responsible for is providing a wide range of technical infrastructure services to meet the institution's computing needs, from mid-range servers, large scale servers, and the respective system, network, and supporting software on those platforms. It provides engineering, integration, and system administration services for Server Administration, Server Security, Backup/Restore, Storage, Virtual infrastructure (on premise and in cloud) and Data Center Management. Duties and accountabilities: The role will work as part of the Developer Experience (DevEx) team within the Shared Services Platform Engineering team in ITSPL. The role is responsible for designing and evolving developer-facing platforms that reduce cognitive load, minimize delivery friction, and provide consistent self-service experience for application teams. The role focuses on platform product engineering, including the Internal Developer Portal (IDP), standards, and golden paths, rather than operational execution or production support. The role requires a hands-on approach in a multicultural environment which supports diversity, continuous learning, enhancing skillsets and collaboration. The ideal candidate must demonstrate excellent communication skills as the position requires frequent interaction with multiple cross-functional teams. The candidate must possess a strong sense of curiosity, adaptability, and the drive to learn and innovate. We provide a meaningful, open, and collaborative environment. We have many interesting problems to solve, providing you an opportunity to develop your skills while contributing to the mission of the bank. We value teamwork, openness, curiosity, and persistence. Key Responsibilities: • Design, engineer, and evolve developer-facing platform services that improve developer experience by reducing cognitive load and unnecessary complexity. • Identify friction points across the application delivery lifecycle and translate them into platform capabilities, abstractions, and self-service workflows. • Define and maintain golden paths, templates, and standards that guide developers toward secure, compliant, and efficient delivery patterns. • Design and operate an Internal Developer Portal (IDP) that serves as the primary interface for platform capabilities, documentation, and workflows. • Build and maintain shared platform services using Infrastructure as Code and reusable automation components. • Design platform-level CI/CD capabilities as standardized services rather than application-specific implementations. • Implement governance-by-design through automated guardrails, policy-as-code, and embedded controls that do not burden developers. • Partner with cloud, security, architecture, and observability teams to ensure platform services are cohesive and aligned with enterprise standards. Continuously evaluate platform adoption, usability, and effectiveness, refining services to reduce bespoke engagement and manual coordination.

item.title: Underwriter
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . In February 2024, the World Bank Group announced a major upgrade to its guarantees business, by establishing as of July 1 2024, the Guarantee Platform (Platform) housed at MIGA. The Platform will deliver improved guarantee access through a unified team of guarantee specialists as well as innovative new guarantee solutions. These new reforms will help position the Platform/MIGA to achieve the goal of tripling annual guarantee issuance to $20 billion by 2030. MIGA’s Operations Department (MIGOP) leads MIGA’s guarantee business development and origination activities, structures transactions, leads projects through the underwriting and approval process, and manages guarantees portfolio. Within MIGOP, the Global Transaction Team (GTT) is a dedicated team of Analysts, Underwriters, and Senior Underwriters with a focus on underwriting MIGA’s guarantee transactions. MIGOP is seeking a highly experienced, motivated, and proactive Underwriter with strong project finance, public sector finance, political risk insurance, trade finance and/or structured finance underwriting skills, as well as client and new business origination skills, preferably gained in the energy and general infrastructure or financial sectors. While reporting to the Manager for GTT, the day to day activities of the Underwriter will focus mainly on leading transaction teams (comprised of individuals from across the Agency/Platform) and underwriting guarantee transactions as the transaction lead. Depending on experience, the activities may also include supporting business origination and transaction structuring activities. Through this role, the underwriter will develop a broad knowledge of the Platform’s guarantee activities by working on transactions across the Platform’s full product line and across regions and sectors (energy and extractives industries, infrastructure, financial institutions, capital markets, manufacturing, agriculture, services, etc.). Note that this is initially a Washington, DC-based position, however given the regionalization agenda, there is a strong possibility of this position being selected for decentralization. If shortlisted, this will be discussed with you at interview. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES • Lead a multi-disciplinary transaction team (sector, legal, environment and social, climate finance, reinsurance, gender, integrity, risk, development impact, etc.) through the transaction underwriting and approval process, which includes the organization and coordination of due diligence meetings and missions. • Conduct sector and project risk assessments, including contractual risk allocation and the technical and commercial viability of the investment project • Prepare and use complex financial models to, amongst others, analyze the financial viability of the investment project or support credit analysis for credit enhancement transactions • Work together with the risk management officers to analyze country/sub-sovereign project risks and mitigants and with the credit risk officers to support the analysis of state-owned enterprises (credit profile, institutional capacity, legal status and relationship with the government) • Collaborate with risk management officers and the transaction team to conduct development impact analyses of investment projects, including assessing the contribution to the host country's development, the broader impact on the industry and the private sector, and the benefits delivered to both direct and indirect stakeholders • Develop, together with the transaction team, recommendations for the contract of guarantee terms and conditions, including recommendations on appropriate guarantee structures and risk mitigants • Lead the negotiation of new contracts of guarantee with prospective guarantee holders and/or their advisors, in close coordination with the relevant Team Lead/Sector Manager and MIGA’s Legal Department • Engage closely with MIGA’s clients, conduct in-country and virtual due diligence meetings with host country government officials, and collaborate with partners (e.g., World Bank, IFC, and other development finance partners) • Prepare high quality guarantee proposal documents and present them for consideration to MIGA’s Senior Management and Board of Executive Directors • In close coordination with MIGA Senior/Sector Underwriters, Sector Managers, and Regional Heads, support MIGA’s new business origination and client management efforts aimed at generating a robust pipeline of business • As required, create and deliver new business origination-focused presentations to sponsors, government officials, state-owned enterprises, financial institutions, specialist industry groups, and forums

item.title: Investment Officer - Transaction Advisory
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit: https://www.ifc.org IFC’s Transaction Advisory Services Department (CPNPA) is housed in the IFC Cross-Cutting Solutions Vice Presidency (CCSVPU). CPNPA offers transaction advisory services to governments to assist them in partnering with the private sector in sustainable long-term infrastructure projects through designing and structuring PPP transactions able to provide high-quality, affordable, and efficient public and social services. The main sectors of activity are electricity, water, transportation, telecommunications, and social services, such as health and education. CPNPA also collaborates closely with the Corporate Finance Services Department (CFS) which offers three key main products: (1) M A Advisory: advising on buy-side / sell-side transactions; (2) Equity Mobilization Program (EMP): supporting third-party equity mobilization alongside IFC investment; (3) Asset monetization involving listed or listing public entities CPNPA mobilized $4.7B of private investment in FY24, representing about 25% of the IFC’s total core mobilization. Drawing on over 30 years of experience and with over 120 staff across the globe, CPNPA currently manages over 100 active client engagements. Africa has 30 staff distributed in five regional hubs located in Johannesburg, Nairobi, Abidjan, Cairo, and Abuja. The CPNPA department is expected to continue playing a leading role in mobilizing private capital on behalf of the WBG, the FY25 target being fixed at $5.9B. PPP Transaction Advisory is seeking a Investment Officer (IO)/ Senior Investment Officer (SIO) with significant market and industry experience to integrate the Western Africa CPNPA team based in Abidjan, Ivory Coast, with the main objective of developing the presence of IFC in PPP business in the Western Africa sub-region that includes 16 countries: Senegal, Ivory Coast, Cape Vert, Mauritania, Benin, Burkina Faso, Togo, Gambia, Mali, Guinee, Chad, Guinee-Bissau, Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia and Niger. The PPP team focuses on advising governments and government entities on the following types of transactions across all infrastructure sectors: • Public-Private Partnerships e.g. BOT type concessions. • Restructuring and privatization of state-owned enterprises. • Corporate Finance type activities (equity raising, M A, pre-IPO support). The IO will be strongly engaged in business development and execution of mandates. Both origination activities and the preparation work of complex PPP transactions may require close collaboration within the World Bank Group to ensure consistency with the countries’ strategy, access to expertise in institutional and sector reforms, and the development of legal and regulatory frameworks (tariff structures, and others), as may be necessary. The work of the IO will be carried out under the supervision of and in close collaboration with the Western Africa Hub Leader. Further to the activities developed in the Western Africa region, the IO could also be required to work across the broader Africa region, depending on business needs. The position is based in Abidjan, Ivory Coast and the IO will report to the Western Africa Hub Leader based in Abidjan. Role Responsibilities: The IO’s work will involve business development and the implementation of advisory mandates of a variety of PPP types. These activities require, among others, strong interactions with government clients aimed at signing new mandates and execution of the same. Duties will include, but will not be limited to: • Actively contribute to the business targets for the Hub, in terms of increase of pipeline of projects, closings and yearly mobilization targets. • Develop client relationships and project leads in the Western Africa region and carry marketing activities with out of the box thinking in assigned countries/strategic infrastructure sectors. • In developing marketing activities, the IO will collaborate with other WB/IFC teams to identify opportunities based on country strategies and market creation potential. • Lead in the negotiation of the mandates with clients and ensure supervision of the preparation of commercial proposals, etc. • When appropriate, undertake project scoping to assess the feasibility of potential projects. • Prepare/review memos and documentation for internal approval and consultant procurement processes and manage the projects’ budget. • Foster strong relationships with World Bank Group counterparts to identify collaboration opportunities while enhancing business delivery at the country level. • Understand the political, legal, and regulatory impediments permitting private sector participation in the working countries and work closely with the other parts of the WBG to overcome these. • Lead the day-to-day management of project preparation, leading teams working on sell-side PPP mandates, including managing legal, technical, environmental, and other consultants; review the consultants’ outputs, reports, analysis, financial models, etc. • Demonstrate mastery of financial modeling and project finance related analyses to assess bankability of potential projects and be able to supervise teams / juniors undertake financial analyses to support structuring of projects. • Develop transaction structure options for the PPP projects being implemented providing innovative and practical solutions to address the client’s problems, while ensuring the Projects’ bankability and long-term sustainability. Present and negotiate the proposed project structure with the Client after obtaining IFC approval. • Assist in the organization and management of the tendering process of projects, including marketing of projects, participating in road shows, and preparation of Prequalification and Request for Proposals documents. Assist during the selection and project award processes and final negotiation of project agreements leading to deal closing. Strong negotiation skills to develop solutions and overcome impasses in transactions is paramount. • Participate/lead meetings with government clients and investors. • In the preparation of the Projects, coordinate closely with other parts of IFC including environmental, social, legal, or other advice, and if appropriate, investment and World Bank colleagues to provide bespoke solutions to ensure Projects achieve expected sustainable development impact. • Develop, coach, motivate, and manage junior members of the team. • As appropriate, participate in the development and implementation of upstream activities in line with IFC 2030 to create, deepen, and expand markets with the regional and global teams from across IFC and the WBG. • As appropriate, contribute to the elaboration of the sub-regional strategy. • Support Corporate Finance mandates, both in terms of origination and execution that may include the preparation and delivery of pitch presentations to companies, reviewing and advising on corporate structure, balance sheet structure, valuation, prospectus review, corporate governance, etc. • As requested, participate in the preparation of the regional strategy for the PPP advisory business, with a focus on strategic priorities, mobilization of private investment, and development of climate-friendly and high-impact projects. • Support knowledge management by helping to disseminate PPP and CFS knowledge and experience and, • Assist in other PPP projects across the larger region or strategy-related activities, as the need may arise.

item.title: Project Manager, Real Estate
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 175 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit www.worldbank.org . Global Corporate Solutions and Corporate Real Estate The World Bank Group’s Real Estate Team (WBGRE) plays a crucial role in supporting the World Bank Group legal entities (IBRD, IFC, IDA, MIGA, and ICSID) by developing and operating their real estate assets worldwide. WBGRE’s primary purpose is to provide safe, cost effective, sustainable, and functional real estate solutions, enabling business units to perform their work program in line with the WBG’s mission to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. To achieve its purpose, WBGRE led by the Senior Manager is structured into 3 divisions: (i) HQ Real Estate Development Management and (ii) Global Real Estate Development Management and (iii) Global Strategy and Planning or Center of Excellent. WBGRE also acts as the Secretariat for the WBG’s Real Estate Governance Framework, including supporting the WBG Real Estate Governance process. WBGRE comprises 80+ staff, leverages over 500 contractors, and manages an annual capital investment plan of about $160 million globally. WBGRE works closely with the Bank’s regions managing more than 175 country offices. Job Description The Project Manager reports to the Manager, Real Estate (GCSF1) and handles major components of facilities projects, comprising acquisition, design, and construction of Bank’s offices in the Real Estate (Africa) region - GCSF1. He or She delivers the work program under the direction of the Senior Project Manager working closely with managers at all levels at Headquarters and Country Offices, internal business units and service providers, attorneys, real estate brokers, landlords, furniture, and equipment manufacturers, architectural, engineering and project management firms, and construction contractors. The position is based in Nairobi, Kenya Duties and accountabilities include but are not limited to: • Delivers the work program under the direction of the Senior Project Manager and as required, by the Manager. • Responsible for providing technical support towards the design and construction of the World Bank Office Premises including but not limited to active new office development projects in Nairobi as well as monitoring other World Bank construction works as assigned. The technical support includes support to project and contract management, as well as monitoring of construction works on site. The incumbent collaborates closely with the different stakeholders and provides local knowledge and expertise to help meet the needs of the project. • Develops project program with the client. • Resolves scope of required resources and mobilize them from within/outside the Bank. • Supports technical interaction with the internal real estate group lease or purchase formation and negotiations. • Conducts review of terms and conditions of lease proposals and assists in formulating strategy for lease transactions. • Sets the project budget and schedule, and leads the planning, design, and construction process, coordinating inputs from Bank units and outside firms on all aspects of the project from inception through final completion. • Identifies, inspects, and evaluates alternative sites and buildings, and determines their suitability for the Bank’s requirements and needs. • Coordinates and directs all implementation activities and resources. Analyzes needs, identifies potential issues, and develops optimal solutions considering user requirements, technical constraints, resource availability, Bank policies, standards, and guidelines. • Supports the selection of design supervision consultants, contractors, and specialty consultants for projects. • Manages the preparation of construction plans, specifications, and contract documents. • Manages the preparations of project presentations to staff, Senior Management, and governance oversight teams. • Monitors the project budget and schedule and takes appropriate corrective action when needed to adhere to the pre-established budget and schedule. • Assures the final completion and timely occupancy of projects in a cost-effective manner. • Prepares for requisitions and approves invoices submitted by vendors/contacts and prepares the required documentation for payments. • Prepares timely project reporting for clients and SR management. • Manages 3rd party review and testing and commissioning • Manages accurate projects documents filing. • Oversees and monitors post-occupancy activities. This position was previously posted as req37444 (Project Manager, International Real Estate) as an international recruitment. Following a change in business needs, the position has been converted to a local recruitment. The selected candidate will be eligible for the applicable local compensation package and benefits associated with the duty station.

item.title: Operations Analyst
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . In February 2024, the World Bank Group announced a major upgrade to its guarantees business that will deliver improved guarantee access through a unified team at MIGA as well as innovative new guarantee solutions. These new reforms will help position MIGA to achieve the goal of tripling annual guarantee issuance to $20 billion by 2030. MIGA’s Operations Department (MIGOP) leads MIGA’s guarantee business development and origination activities, structures transactions, and leads projects through the underwriting and approval process, and manages our guarantees portfolio. Within MIGOP, the Global Transaction Team (GTT) is a dedicated team of Operations Analysts, Underwriters, and Senior Underwriters with a focus on underwriting MIGA’s guarantee transactions. MIGOP is seeking a highly experienced, motivated, and proactive Operations Analyst with strong project finance, public sector finance, and/or political risk insurance underwriting skills, as well as client and new business origination skills, preferably gained in the energy and general infrastructure sectors. While reporting to the Manager for GTT, the Operations Analyst will work closely with Transaction Team Leads (Underwriters and Senior Underwriters) on underwriting guarantee transactions. Depending on experience, the activities may also include supporting business origination and transaction structuring activities. Through this role, the Operations Analyst will develop a broad knowledge of MIGA’s guarantee activities by working on transactions across the Platform’s full product line (including, PRI including Capital Optimization, Non-Honoring for both the real and financial sectors, and trade finance guarantees) and across regions and sectors (energy and extractives industries, infrastructure, financial institutions, capital markets, manufacturing, agriculture, services, etc.). Note that this is initially a Washington, DC-based position, however given the regionalization agenda, there is a strong possibility of this position being selected for decentralization. If shortlisted, this will be discussed with you at interview. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES • Work on multi-disciplinary transaction teams within MIGA (legal, environment and social, climate finance, reinsurance, gender, integrity, risk, development impact, etc.) throughout the transaction lifecycle including underwriting, approvals and guarantee negotiation • Conduct independent research and analysis on various topics including the transaction investor and sector and support analysis on the technical and commercial viability of the investment project • Prepare and use complex financial models to, amongst others, analyze the financial viability of the investment project or support credit analysis for credit enhancement transactions • Engage with MIGA’s clients, conduct in-country and virtual due diligence meetings with host country government officials, and collaborate with partners (e.g. World Bank, IFC, and other development finance partners) • Prepare guarantee pricing estimates for clients • Contribute to preparation of high-quality guarantee proposal documents and participate in presentations to MIGA’s Senior Management • In close coordination with MIGA Senior/Sector Underwriters, Sector Managers, and Regional Heads, support MIGA’s new business origination and client management efforts and, as required, conduct industry and client research • As required, prepare talking points and presentations for new business origination-focused activities with project sponsors, government officials, state-owned enterprises, financial institutions, specialist industry groups, and forums • As required, collaborate with the portfolio team to provide analytical support in respect of portfolio management activities • As required, conduct integrity searches on potential clients, project participants and stakeholders.

item.title: E T Consultant - Operations Officer
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . The IFC Country Office in Guinea is seeking a qualified Extended Term Consultant - Operations Officer to join its team in Guinea. Reporting to the World Bank Group Country Manager, the Operations Officer will conduct a wide variety of corporate and project finance activities including projects generation and supervision. This involves the preparation of presentations and pitch books for IFC’s participation in workshops, conferences, and high-level meetings; intensive relationship management with government and business representatives; contribution to strategy formulation, as well as data management and knowledge dissemination. Role Responsibilities: • Proactively develop a strong pipeline of good quality investment opportunities through origination and business development anticipating market trends and employing sector/country knowledge. Coordinate closely with WB and MIGA teams. • Develop market knowledge to ensure that IFC is working with the development partners and sponsors. • Take accountability for client selection and conduct the integrity due diligence of potential sponsors. Develop and maintain relationships with potential clients and identify business opportunities, while considering IFC’s strategy, priorities, and products. • Demonstrate or quickly acquire a thorough understanding of the countries, provide market intelligence and analysis, and develop strong business networks. • Build and maintain strong relationships with portfolio clients, in coordination with the Country Officer, global and regional private businesses (in financial and real sectors), multilateral partners, and government officials to further develop investment opportunities in economic sectors with high developmental impact. • Strategy formulation in collaboration with the WBG Country Manager and maintain collaborative working relationships across the WBG. • Monitoring portfolio projects in collaboration with the country Officer and Industries teams. • Develop a strong understanding, and actively market and utilize IFC’s Advisory Services’ offering (AS). • Prepare relevant strategy papers, briefs, summaries, working papers, reports, and promotional materials for internal and external users, in support of country and industry priorities, in coordination with the Country Officer and the Communications Team. • Facilitate information flow from Managers, Country Officers to the WBG Country Manager ensure consistent resolution of administrative issues. • Support office administration as needed. • Provide in-country support, and subsequent follow-up to IFC visiting missions as needed. • Perform other such duties as may be required from time to time to meet emerging, ad-hoc corporate requirements, and/or respond to internal or external requests.

item.title: Lead Economist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. https://ww.worldbank.org . East Asia and the Pacific (EAP) Region EAP is a large and diverse region. Despite substantial economic growth and poverty reduction, the EAP region faces huge development challenges. Growth has been uneven across and within countries, institutions still need strengthening, and most countries are heavily affected by climate change. The Bank plays a significant role on global public goods, including climate, biodiversity, water pollution, and health. The COVID pandemic, and more recently food and energy price increases are compounding the impact of the global economic slowdown. The World Bank Group is seen as a premier development institution in the Region, with a leadership role on analytical and advisory services as well as financing. East Asia and the Pacific Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/ea The World Bank's Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) Global Practice supports client countries in achieving sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth through macroeconomic and fiscal policy advice, analytical work, and lending operations. The East Asia and Pacific (EAP) region encompasses some of the world's most dynamic economies, including the Philippines, Malaysia, and Brunei Darussalam — each at a distinct stage of development but sharing common challenges around fiscal sustainability, private sector-led growth, and job creation. The Philippines is one of the region's fastest-growing economies, yet faces persistent structural constraints including limited fiscal space, infrastructure gaps, and labor market informality. Malaysia, an upper-middle-income economy, is actively pursuing high-income status and requires continued reform of its fiscal framework and growth model. Brunei, a high-income hydrocarbon-dependent economy, is navigating an ambitious economic diversification agenda. The World Bank is seeking a Lead Economist to provide intellectual leadership and strategic oversight of its economic and policy engagement across these three countries. The Lead Economist will serve as the primary economic interlocutor for the Philippines and support FPG teams in Malaysia and Brunei, leading the Bank's analytical and advisory work on macroeconomic policy, growth, and fiscal and structural reform. The role combines high-quality economic research, policy dialogue at the highest levels of government, and cross-country knowledge synthesis to generate impact on development outcomes. The Lead Economist will report to the Practice Manager for Fiscal Policy and Growth in the East Asia and Pacific region. Job duties and accountabilities 1. Intellectual Leadership and Economic Analysis Lead and oversee the preparation of flagship analytical products, including core economic diagnostics. Develop and apply rigorous quantitative and qualitative analytical frameworks to assess macroeconomic trends, fiscal sustainability, structural transformation, and productivity dynamics. Synthesize cross-country lessons and global knowledge to inform country-level policy recommendations. Contribute to regional and global knowledge products, including the EAP Economic Update and FPG flagship publications. 2. Policy Dialogue and Client Engagement Serve as the Bank's primary economic spokesperson and trusted advisor to senior government counterparts, including Ministries of Finance, central banks, and planning agencies. Lead high-level policy dialogue on fiscal reform, growth strategy, and job creation, translating analytical findings into actionable policy recommendations. Represent the World Bank in senior-level forums, including meetings with policy makers, technical counterparts, and international conferences. Build and maintain strong relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, including government, the private sector, academia, civil society, and development partners. 3. Operational Support and Program Development Provide economic leadership and quality assurance for lending operations, including Development Policy Loans, Investment Project Financing, and Program-for-Results instruments, ensuring that operations are grounded in robust macroeconomic and fiscal analysis. Contribute to Country Partnership Frameworks and Systematic Country Diagnostics by providing high-quality economic inputs and strategic direction. Support the design and implementation of technical assistance and capacity-building programs in fiscal policy, economic statistics, and growth analytics. 4. Team Leadership and Mentoring Lead and manage a team of economists and researchers, providing strategic direction, quality oversight, and professional mentoring. Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performance team culture. Contribute to the recruitment, onboarding, and professional development of junior staff. 5. Knowledge Management and External Visibility Disseminate research findings through publications, policy briefs, blogs, and public events to maximize development impact. Engage proactively with media, think tanks, and the broader research community to raise the visibility of the Bank's analytical work in the three countries. Contribute to MTI and EAP knowledge-sharing platforms and communities of practice.

item.title: ET Consultant - Investment Accounting
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . The Policy Implementation - Investment Accounting sub team (CTRPI- IA) within the WBG Controllers (CTR) has overall responsibility for the accounting analysis, evaluation and implementation for IFC’s complex loan, equity and guarantee transactions, working extensively with IFC’s investment officers and other staff in CTR. This position reports directly to and assists the CTRPI-Investment Accounting Supervisor. CTRPI- IA is seeking an ET Consultant (ETC) staff for one year to support and contribute the teams work program which includes: the accounting implementation of complex loan, equity and guarantee transactions and work extensively with Investment Officers and CTR staff. The individual will identify transactions to be scoped in for review by the unit on a daily basis and allocate scope in transactions to the team. The individual will also assemble documents and information on projects selected for accounting review, document the fact pattern summarizing the project and investment structure and, for simple investment transactions, compare the legal agreement to the accounting standards and provide accounting conclusions relative to the applicable accounting treatment of the investment. The individual will be required to perform these duties leveraging on the A.I. tools used by the team. The individual will have basic technical accounting knowledge of US GAAP and/or IFRS guidance for loan/equity/guarantee investments, particularly with respect to Consolidation and / or identification of Derivatives. A self-starter, the candidate will be a highly disciplined individual with excellent accounting/auditing and strong interpersonal skills. S/he must be able to gain the cooperation of technical and business staff at all levels and across departmental boundaries. In addition, the individual must have a keen interest in technology and leveraging on A.I. to complete the tasks assigned to them Roles and Responsibilities The individual’s responsibilities will include: • Leverage on A.I tools to identify transactions to be scoped in for review and assign these reviews to members of the unit. • On an ongoing basis, prepare and document the investment structures and background facts for scoped-in transactions and perform accounting analyses for simple investment transactions. This task should leverage use of A.I tools as much as possible. • Undertake frequent discussions with Investment Officers and Investment Accounting team members to clarify information or obtain additional information. • Participate in the continuous process improvement and efficiencies. Document and update the Investment Accounting procedures for monitoring and assessing significant influence factors, Consolidation, Debt Securities, and other related accounting areas. • Regularly share key information on processes, timelines, responsibilities, expectations and potential problems with supervisors and team members and seek their input. • Assist in various compliance testing and other compliance activities as assigned. • Perform other duties as assigned from time to time.

Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTORATE (EXD) The Executive Directorate (EXD) is the steward of OECD resources, on behalf of the Secretary-General. Our focus is on people and their wellbeing; the effective and efficient management of the budget; the safety and security of staff, Delegations, visitors, and of the OECD’s data; maintaining and sustaining physical and digital infrastructure; and enabling the convening power of the OECD through conferences, meetings and events, whether virtual, physical or hybrid. As well as providing corporate services, functions and management support to our staff and Members, we provide integrated, strategic and expert advice on corporate policies and management issues to the Secretary-General, to Council and to Standing Committees, to which we regularly report on corporate matters. We also provide risk management functions (for management areas under our purview). Ours is a fast-paced environment focused on delivering management excellence across all of our functions. THE HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT SERVICE (EXD/HRM) Within the OECD’s Executive Directorate (EXD), the Human Resource Management Service (HRM) is responsible for providing stewardship of the Organisation’s human capital on behalf of the Secretary-General. Overseeing three divisions (HR Operations, the Client Services Group and the Talent Management and Analytics Group), EXD/HRM’s Head Office provides strategic HR direction, leadership in corporate and legal matters and oversight and co-ordination for the Organisation at large. HRM/HRO is looking for a Staff Administration Team Lead who will oversee an operational team responsible for corporate on-boarding and departure formalities as well as processing all administrative actions related to the employment of the staff and support a portfolio of client directorates. item.description: {"id":"744000140715019","name":"Head of Division – Monitoring and Peer Review ","uuid":"529618dd-df8d-4d7c-8b21-892e08b3e2fd","jobId":"84d48e5d-cd17-4a1a-a192-262a8b16eb82","jobAdId":"a25145f6-c6c1-4aed-ab34-94b5aed2b425","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3302V","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000271","valueLabel":"CTP"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6104231","valueLabel":"Executive Leadership"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"EL1","valueLabel":"EL1"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-30T15:04:01.937Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140715019-head-of-division-monitoring-and-peer-review-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140715019-head-of-division-monitoring-and-peer-review-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/529618dd-df8d-4d7c-8b21-892e08b3e2fd?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" THE OECD – Who we are, what we do The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. THE GLOBAL FORUM The Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes (the Global Forum), whose Secretariat is hosted by the OECD’s Centre for Tax Policy and Administration (CTPA), plays a central role in promoting and monitoring the implementation of international standards on transparency and exchange of information (EOI). With over 170 members ( www.oecd.org/tax/transparency ) participating on an equal footing, the Global Forum supports the fight against tax evasion and avoidance by conducting peer reviews and monitoring activities and delivering capacity building to help them implement and benefit from these standards. Its work covers tax transparency standards, such as the Transparency and Exchange of Information on Request (EOIR), the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) for automatic exchange of financial accounts information, the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), and the associated confidentiality and data safeguards (CDS) requirements. THE POSITION The Global Forum is looking for a dynamic Head of Division to provide leadership and strategic direction. As a key member of its Senior Management team, s/he will lead the Monitoring and Peer Review Division, overseeing the monitoring and peer review the implementation of the transparency and exchange of information standards, promoting their effective implementation and supporting reforms to ensure they remain effective tools against tax avoidance and evasion. The Division also supports the Global Forum’s work to establish partnerships with stakeholders in the tax and development community. The successful candidate will work closely with, and report to, the Head of the Global Forum Secretariat. The scope and the complexity of the Global Forum’s work require an experienced senior executive with expertise in tax policy and administration, international development and political processes. The ideal candidate will be a strategic thinker with political acumen, experienced in delivering a complex Programme of Work and Budget, leading international teams and maintaining a professional network. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Leadership Support the implementation of the Global Forum’s Programme of Work and Budget (PWB) and the advancement of its strategic outcomes, with a focus on monitoring and peer review of the standards in transparency and exchange of information for tax purposes. Support the Office of the Secretary-General, the OECD Sherpa, and their respective teams on targeted policy advice and on the OECD’s contributions in the area of tax and development, including to the G20 and G7. Lead on the design and management of the Global Forum’s monitoring and peer review programmes, ensuring the effectiveness of the standards and promoting the necessary reforms to meet the needs of all member jurisdictions. Lead on ensuring the quality and consistency of the implementation of the Global Forum’s monitoring and peer review processes, managing key stakeholders and ensuring consistency and coherence across outputs. Ensure the Global Forum’s work reflects the needs of all its member jurisdictions, and promotes effective standards, including by leading the Global Forum’s engagement across the OECD and with member jurisdictions to deliver the Common Transmission System. Foster cross-organisational collaboration, particularly with the OECD Development Cluster, on tax and development issues. Contribute to strengthening the OECD and the Global Forum’s standing as authoritative reference centres for analysis and guidance on tax policy and administration among member jurisdictions and relevant stakeholders. Support the effective global reach of the OECD and the Global Forum’s work on tax transparency and exchange of information, including through rigorous public reporting and sustained engagement with key partners, in alignment with the OECD’s global relations strategy. Representation and Liaison Represent the Global Forum Secretariat and the OECD in internal and external meetings. Establish and maintain strong networks with international organisations, national authorities, academia, and research institutions. Actively contribute to the effective dissemination of the Global Forum’s work through the media, professional networks, academia and other communities. Prepare timely and accurate responses to briefing requests from the Secretary-General’s Office and other parts of the Organisation. Develop strategic relationships with key international and regional organisations active in tax transparency. Management and Co-ordination Ensure effective coordination and collaboration across the Organisation, including with the Office of the Secretary-General and policy directorates, to support corporate initiatives and horizontal projects. Lead and manage Division staff by setting clear objectives, providing direction and feedback, supporting professional development, and promoting effective project management and internal communication. Build and lead a cohesive, diverse, and inclusive team, fostering excellence and a collaborative work environment. Uphold and promote the OECD’s highest professional standards and ethical principles, ensuring a supportive and respectful workplace. Oversee the organisation and smooth delivery of all meetings under the Division’s responsibility. Effectively manage human and financial resources to deliver the programme of work and budget and fulfil the Division’s commitments. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. THE GLOBAL FORUM The Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes (the Global Forum) whose Secretariat is hosted by the OECD’s Centre for Tax Policy and Administration (CTPA), plays a central role in promoting and monitoring the implementation of international standards on transparency and exchange of information (EOI). With over 170 members ( www.oecd.org/tax/transparency ) participating on an equal footing, the Global Forum supports the fight against tax evasion and avoidance by conducting peer reviews and monitoring activities and delivering capacity building to help them implement and benefit from these standards. Its work covers tax transparency standards, such as the Transparency and Exchange of Information on Request (EOIR), the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) for automatic exchange of financial accounts information, the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), and the associated confidentiality and data safeguards (CDS) requirements. THE POSITION The Global Forum is looking for a dynamic and visionary Head of Division to provide leadership and strategic direction. As a key member of its Senior Management team, s/he will lead the Capacity Building and Outreach Division , which ensures all members have a voice in shaping the international tax transparency work and receive effective support to implement international tax transparency standards and mobilise domestic resources. The Division Head also fosters partnership with stakeholders in the tax and development community and works closely with the Head of the Global Forum Secretariat. The scope and the complexity of the Global Forum’s work require an experienced senior executive with strong expertise in tax policy and administration, international development and political processes. The ideal candidate will be a strategic thinker with political acumen, experienced in managing and delivering a complex Programme of Work and Budget, leading diverse international teams, while maintaining a wide and effective professional network. item.title: Regional Industry Director, Europe, Infrastructure & Natural Resources (INR)
item.description: IFC — a member of the World Bank Group — is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. Our mission is to leverage the power of the private sector to end extreme poverty and promote shared prosperity in a sustainable way. For more information, visit www.ifc.org IFC has embarked on an ambitious new growth strategy (IFC 3.0) to stimulate more investment activity. This strategy calls for generating our opportunities by proactively working “Upstream” to create, deepen, and expand markets and imagine, design, and implement investment projects. It requires taking a systematic approach to understanding the regulatory and sector bottlenecks that prevent the flow of private capital into productive investment in our member countries and addressing these bottlenecks through World Bank Group engagement on policy reforms and programmatic interventions at the country and sector level. This strategy also calls for working with Governments and IBRD/IDA and MIGA colleagues first to seek private sector solutions to address development challenges - where such solutions are advisable and can be effective - and reserve public financing for projects only when other options are suboptimal. This approach is called the “Cascade.” The Infrastructure and Natural Resources (INR) Industry is one of IFC’s key strategic priorities. The team delivers financial and technical support to clients in the power, transport, municipal environmental infrastructure, telecommunications, oil and gas, and mining sectors, from IFC’s own Balance Sheet and through the mobilization of other capital. The Department also seeks to maintain IFC, as part of the World Bank Group at the cutting edge of helping member countries find solutions to new and emerging infrastructure and natural resource issues. IFC's priorities in Europe: (i) grow business in the Regions, achieving strong development impact, additionality, and financial sustainability; (ii) build new and nurture existing client relationships; (iii) manage a portfolio of assets for strong profitability and impact; (iv) work closely with the regional management team to strengthen our value proposition and delivery in the regions, including by developing joint ventures with other industry teams; (vi) catalyze and mobilize private capital and develop client and sector solutions that can be scaled and replicated; (vii) work closely with the global industry and treasury teams to introduce best international practices, global knowledge, and new financial products; (viii) foster strong relationships with other IBRD/IDA to identify collaboration opportunities and enhance client delivery and country-level outcomes. IFC is seeking a Regional Industry Director (RID) for INR, based in Vienna, who will be primarily responsible for INR activities in Europe. This key leadership role requires significant and demonstrated leadership and management skills. Duties and Accountabilities The roles and responsibilities of the position will include but not be limited to: Business Responsibility • Develop and implement the INR strategy and priorities in the Region in partnership with the Regional Directors, the Country Managers, the INR Management team, and other Regional Industry Directors, focusing on growing our business and achieving a strong development impact with high additionality and sustainable profitability. • Lead and grow the overall INR business in the Regions and be responsible for delivering financially sound, profitable, and developmental new business and portfolio management. • Strategically position the INR business in Europe, working closely with the Regional Vice President, other Industry Regional Directors, and Regional Directors by developing the Country Strategies. • Chair and/or manage Investment Review Meetings and make decisions on IFC investments in Europe. • Be responsible for Upstream and Advisory engagements for INR in the Regions. • In collaboration with Senior Management of the INR Global Industry, contribute to the delivery and execution of INR’S regional strategy. • Partner with the IBRD/IDA and MIGA to develop regional sector strategies. • Work closely with the Global Industry, Client Relationship Managers, and Treasury teams to ensure the implementation of best international practices and innovative solutions. Client and stakeholder responsibility • Lead, in coordination with the regional leadership team, the design and implementation of the strategy for business development and ensure proactive and comprehensive client and INR portfolio management in the Region. • Represent IFC to key clients and Region stakeholders; build and maintain excellent long-term relationships with key stakeholders, including public sector relevant institutions, MDBs, Donors, and investors. • Partner with other INRD/IDA and MIGA and other industries in the Region to seek opportunities for joint ventures, mobilization of resources/partners/collaboration, and knowledge transfer among the institutions to benefit clients. Resource Responsibility • Act as Primary Supervisor for INR Managers and Reviewing Officials for other INR staff dedicated to the Region. • Implement agreed corporate initiatives for enhancing efficiency and client service. Recommend INR resource allocation for the Region. Reporting Lines • The RID will directly report to the Regional Vice President of LAC and Europe. • The RID will be part of the Core Leadership Team of the LAC and Europe Vice Presidency, and the INR global management team.

item.title: Data Analyst
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context: WBG Budget and Procurement supports the World Bank Group’s strategic priorities by providing budget, planning, procurement, systems, reporting, analytics, and shared services across the institution. The WBG Centers of Excellence department brings together core budget functions to build a more integrated, data-driven, and client-focused budget function. The department supports One WBG integration, budget reforms, modernized systems, automation, and stronger decision support for senior management and client teams. Unit Context: The Budget Solutions unit leads WBG-wide budget systems, data, reporting, knowledge, and technology-enabled solutions. The unit supports the Integrated Planning Solution, ERP transition, budget reporting, analytics, automation, and client-facing digital products. The Systems, Data and Reporting team will help strengthen data governance, reporting quality, self-service analytics, process automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve decision-making and service delivery across WBP and its clients. Duties and accountabilities • Support business stakeholders and technical teams in identifying data needs, reporting gaps, and opportunities to improve budget analytics and client service delivery. • Extract, clean, validate, and organize structured and unstructured datasets from relevant WBP systems and data sources, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and timeliness. • Conduct exploratory data analysis and prepare clear summaries, visualizations, dashboards, and recurring reports using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Python, or R. • Contribute to the development, testing, and documentation of predictive models, reporting tools, mobile applications, and AI-enabled solutions under the direction of senior colleagues. • Maintain and update standard reports, dashboards, datasets, and model outputs, escalating data quality issues and supporting routine validation and troubleshooting. • Assist with user testing, documentation, and knowledge sharing to help business users interpret reports and apply data insights in day-to-day decision-making.
