item.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prospering and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . At COP27 and CMA4, the Conference of the Parties (COP) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Conference of the Parties serving as the Meeting of the Parties to the Paris Agreement (CMA) established funding arrangements to assist developing countries particularly vulnerable to climate change. This decision included the creation of the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), with a focus on providing support to affected nations. At COP28 and CMA5, the COP/CMA formally approved the Fund’s Governing Instrument, designating it as part of the UNFCCC’s financial mechanism and placing it under the guidance of both COP and CMA. The decision authorized the FRLD’s Board to secure a hosting arrangement with the World Bank as an interim trustee for four years, which includes hosting the Fund’s secretariat. The World Bank has agreed to act as trustee and administer the Trust Fund in line with the COP/CMA’s stipulations. The FRLD Secretariat, hosted by the World Bank in Washington, D.C., supports FRLD governing bodies, manages institutional relations, aids in strategy, policy, and program development, and oversees management systems. The FRLD Secretariat, led by the Executive Director (ED), coordinates FRLD’s strategic activities across its governing bodies, including the Board, and the World Bank (as Trustee and Secretariat host), and other stakeholders. It also drives thought leadership, manages portfolio risk, and develops initiatives to mobilize resources. The Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will contribute to the design and implementation of results frameworks and M E systems to support FRLD’s operations, including annual results reporting. A strong emphasis is placed on knowledge management and organizational learning through dissemination of tools, guidelines, and lessons learned. The M E Specialist will report directly to the Results, Evaluation and Learning (REAL) team Program Manager and collaborate closely with the Secretariat staff and external stakeholders, including governments, access entities, multilateral development banks, UN agencies, vertical climate funds, donor organizations, and civil society. The position is based in Washington, D.C. and involves frequent travel. Duties and Responsibilities: 1. Results Frameworks, Systems Reporting • Contribute to the implementation of the FRLD results measurement framework, RMF handbook, MEL Policy, Strategic Learning Framework, Knowledge Management, Evaluation System and Approach - and related guidance documents, as needed. • Coordinate the design, development, and continuous improvement of a web-based results management system to support data-driven decision-making and institutional learning (in coordination with the portfolio management system). • Contribute to the results reports that synthesize achievements, lessons learned, and areas for improvement across projects and programs. 2. Knowledge Management and Learning • Coordinate the development and dissemination of M E and knowledge products, including tools, templates, guidelines, and case studies that promote institutional learning and good practices. • Promote a learning-oriented culture by designing and facilitating knowledge-sharing events, learning reviews, and reflection workshops. • Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to generate, curate, and disseminate knowledge products on emerging topics related to loss and damage. 3. Strategic Technical Support to Programs and Countries • Provide M E guidance to access agencies and client countries to strengthen results orientation in funding requests and projects. •Oversee the review of funding requests of projects and programs to ensure the technical robustness of M E requirements, including completeness, methodological soundness, and full compliance with the Fund’s Results Framework and related policies. • Work closely with FRLD REAL team program manager to ensure M E frameworks and learning objectives are consistently integrated across all levels of programming. Support country-level capacity to design, manage, and use M E systems for planning, implementation, and adaptive management. 4. Strategic Communication and Dissemination • Develop and implement a dissemination strategy for evaluation and learning products tailored to multiple audiences. • Prepare briefs, results narratives, impact stories, presentations, and knowledge summaries etc. for FRLD leadership and stakeholders to inform decision-making and strategic planning. • Provide logistical and substantive support in organizing results related workshops, consultations, and knowledge-sharing sessions with stakeholders.

item.title: Finance & Budget Officer
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prospering and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . At COP27 and CMA4, the Conference of the Parties (COP) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Conference of the Parties serving as the Meeting of the Parties to the Paris Agreement (CMA) established funding arrangements to assist developing countries particularly vulnerable to climate change. This decision included the creation of the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD), with a focus on providing support to affected nations. At COP28 and CMA5, the COP/CMA formally approved the Fund’s Governing Instrument, designating it as part of the UNFCCC’s financial mechanism and placing it under the guidance of both COP and CMA. The decision authorized the FRLD’s Board to secure a hosting arrangement with the World Bank as an interim trustee for four years, which includes hosting the Fund’s secretariat. The World Bank has agreed to act as trustee and administer the Trust Fund in line with the COP/CMA’s stipulations. The FRLD Secretariat, hosted by the World Bank in Washington, D.C., supports FRLD governing bodies, manages institutional relations, aids in strategy, policy, and program development, and oversees management systems. The FRLD Secretariat, led by the Executive Director (ED), coordinates FRLD’s strategic activities across its governing bodies, including the Board, and the World Bank (as Trustee and Secretariat host), and other stakeholders. It also drives thought leadership, manages portfolio risk, and develops initiatives to mobilize resources. The Finance and Budget Officer will report directly to the Program Manager – Budget and Financial Management and will work under his day-to-day supervision. He/She will collaborate closely with the Secretariat staff and external stakeholders, including Board members, members of the Budget Committee, the World Bank Trustee, and civil society. The position is based in Washington, D.C., USA, and may involve occasional travel. Duties and Responsibilities: 1. Budgeting, Financial Reporting, and Monitoring: • Collect, consolidate, and reconcile budget inputs from across Secretariat units. Prepare comprehensive draft budgets for review by the Program Manager. • Support the drafting of the Secretariat’s Workplan in alignment with the Administrative budget. • Prepare periodic financial reports and statements — including monthly and periodic budget execution reports for the Board, the Budget Committee, and other stakeholders. • Track variances against approved budgets, flag deviations, and maintain up-to-date financial records. • Support the design, development, and regular updating of financial and budget dashboards, compiling key performance metrics and budget utilization trends to support data-driven decision-making. 2. Trust Fund Financial Management and Systems: • Support the Program Manager and the DED as TTL of the Administrative Trust Funds, in the setup and maintenance of FRLD Trust Fund financial systems governed by World Bank policies and procedures, including the implementation of financial monitoring frameworks. • Provide day-to-day operational support on financial management of FRLD-managed trust funds, including cost planning, fund allocation tracking, performance monitoring, and the preparation of financial analyses for the Board and stakeholders. 3. Policy Compliance and Process Optimization: • Provide operational support on financial and fiduciary management matters in compliance with World Bank policies and procedures, including quality assurance efforts and ensuring best practices in financial planning, risk mitigation, and reporting. • Contribute to the evaluation and improvement of financial management processes related to FRLD trust funds to enhance operational efficiency and support alignment with resource mobilization and allocation strategies. 4. Stakeholder Coordination and Board Support: • Support the Program Manager in liaising with World Bank units (e.g., DFi, LEG, WFA, TRE, BPS), the Trustee, the Secretariat divisions, the Budget Committee, and other key stakeholders to facilitate coordination on all trust fund and financial management matters. • Support the preparation of Board and Budget Committee documentation on financial planning and budget-related matters, including drafting papers, preparing presentations, and conducting technical briefings as requested. • Coordinate with the Governance and Board Affairs team on decision-making processes, including drafting decision text.

item.title: E T Temporary - Communications Assistant
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. About the Compliance Advisor Ombudsman (CAO) The Office of the Compliance Advisor Ombudsman (CAO) is the independent accountability mechanism for the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), members of the World Bank Group, reporting directly to the IFC and MIGA Boards. CAO’s mandate is to facilitate the resolution of complaints from people affected by IFC and MIGA projects, enhance environmental and social project outcomes, and foster public accountability and learning to enhance IFC’s and MIGA’s performance. Position Overview Communication and outreach are integral activities that support CAO’s work and strategic engagement with internal and external stakeholders. The CAO Communications Team is looking for a Communications Assistant to support day-to-day communications and outreach activities. The successful candidate will assist with content development for digital and social channels; support event logistics; maintain communications databases; and work closely with teams across CAO. Responsibilities Deliverables • Develop and draft content, including the creation of visual materials such as infographics and information brochures or slides on CAO processes and a range of accountability-related topics. • Contribute to CAO’s internal and external newsletters by developing content and sourcing information. • Post content to CAO’s website, social media, and other communications channels. • Coordinate the production of the news clipping. • Provide logistics support for external meetings and events. • Develop and maintain communications’ databases and listservs. • Reorganize and maintain CAO’s photo library and archives • Support CAO case data tracking and disclosure activities. • Liaise with vendors including designers, editors, printers, and photographers as needed.

item.title: Program Assistant, Administrative Support, Bogota Office
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. The Regional Office for Colombia (CCMCO), is based in Bogotá and is part of IFC’s Latin America and Caribbean (LAC) Department. CCMCO plays a central role in the functioning of IFC’s matrix organization to bring regional information and perspective to IFC decision-making. CCMCO is responsible for (a) leading the formulation of IFC’s regional strategy; (b) monitoring and communicating IFC’s project pipeline, portfolio performance, and strategy implementation in these four countries; (c) monitoring political, macro-economic, sectoral, and financial market developments, and keeping senior management informed of these developments and potential impact on IFC’s activities and strategies; (d) maintaining dialogue with governments, locally based stakeholders, and other parts of the World Bank, (e) coordinating the investment services (IS) and advisory services (AS) program in the region in collaboration with Regional Industry Departments; and (f) contributing substantially to business development. To fulfill this role, CCMCO seeks a Program Assistant based in Bogotá, Colombia. As part of the Administrative and Client Support (ACS) team the candidate will: Duties and Accountabilities • Provide a wide range of office support to the IFC Colombia team and management to make a significant contribution to the achievement of the unit work program. • Provide specialized support for database management, task management, major event planning and logistics, travel arrangements, editorial assistance, etc. • Coordinate team schedules taking priorities into account, monitoring changes, and communicating the information to appropriate staff, including officials or clients outside the World Bank Group. • Independently undertake diverse and complex work assignments, interpreting existing procedures and processes and application to assist with the implementation of the unit work program. • Handle incoming and outgoing written verbal communications with clients and Government partners. • Exercise quality enhancement for projects and documents ensuring adherence to departmental, VPU and institutional guidelines. • Draft, edit and translate routine correspondence applying effective proofreading and grammar skills in English with high quality and writing standards. • Maintain accurate and efficient filing (paper and electronic) • Back-up of administrative team colleagues when necessary • Back up for reception in coordination with the rotation schedule • Support the elaboration of reports related to business development and transaction processing, putting together industry and market research, comparable data, market trends, etc. • Assist client relationship management, managing and updating the tool for all the industries on a regular basis • Support financial analysis of portfolio clients (enter information in IRP, etc.) • Support the team in processing transactions: help prepare decision books, review information received from clients, perform IDDs, etc. • Prepare documentation for IFC internal processes. • Help the team update pitch books for clients in different sectors.

item.description: {"id":"744000140893729","name":"Policy Analyst - Health, Employment, Skills and Social Affairs","uuid":"4f43d229-8f1e-4fd5-ad40-594d0213ce37","jobId":"8b796c62-39ac-4d9c-b935-db1d9a92099a","jobAdId":"dc94513a-9d84-4c95-bb52-3ce65c3eb1d2","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3304A","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000512","valueLabel":"ELS"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL6","valueLabel":"PAL6"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-31T12:10:55.228Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140893729-policy-analyst-health-employment-skills-and-social-affairs","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140893729-policy-analyst-health-employment-skills-and-social-affairs?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/4f43d229-8f1e-4fd5-ad40-594d0213ce37?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. In line with the strategic objectives of the Secretary-General, the Directorate for Employment, Labour and Social Affairs (ELS) is the focal point for OECD work on building more cohesive and healthier societies through policy advice related to quality jobs, continuous investment in human capital, reduction in poverty and exclusion, improving quality and outcomes of healthcare and public health, effective use of pharmaceuticals and medical devices, effective and efficient health-care systems and good management of migration flows. ELS is looking for several Policy Analyst(s) with a proven track record working in the areas of Health and Employment, Skills and Social Affairs. Successful applicants will work on various projects in a dynamic team of economists, policy experts and statisticians to develop policy advice on at least one of the following areas: Improving the performance of health systems, through work on one or more of the following topics: Measuring health systems performance; Healthcare Quality and outcomes; Public health and prevention policies; Health financing, health system resilience and value for money; Human resources for health; Digital health, data governance and artificial intelligence; Pharmaceutical policies and genomics; Long-term care and integrated care. Employment, Skills and Social Affairs \nImproving the performance of labour markets, employment services, social and migration policy and skills systemsthrough work on one or more of the following topics: the design, implementation and evaluation of employment, skills, migration and integration policies; the analysis of sickness and disability policies; research on adult skills and evolving labour market needs; the future of work, social policy and AI; as well as work on social protection systems and financing, family and youth policies and other social policy topics. Candidates should have a strong background in applying economic concepts to one or more of the following: health systems, and employment, skills and social policies. Experience in managing projects, and a proven ability to plan and deliver work effectively. They will be expected to work both independently and collaboratively with colleagues across their Division and Directorate. They will work on a number of projects, reflecting country policy interests and the programme of work of the Directorate. Successful candidates will work in teams within the relevant Division, and will be supervised by a Senior Policy Analyst. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Research, analysis and drafting: Carry out high quality economic and policy analysis in the respective areas, including supporting cross-disciplinary and comparative analysis and the development of policy recommendations, reports, policy briefs and other deliverables. Contribute to the preparation of reports, flagship publications and country reviews, including contributing to the development of data sources and of new comparative indicators, and ensuring high-quality outputs. Prepare other high-quality documents, including working papers, policy briefs, policy papers, blogs, seminar proceedings, and policy messages based on research and relevant published material. Contribute to the development of practical tools, including policy toolkits to support the implementation of OECD recommendations, and facilitate the sharing and dissemination of information through innovative ways. Conduct statistical analysis to explain key differences in outcomes across countries. For some positions, advanced data analysis skills will be required. Seek innovative approaches to address policy challenges in the labour market and society. Oversee the work of more junior staff, provide feedback and guidance, as applicable to each project. Co-ordination, representation and liaison: Participate, as required, in horizontal and multidisciplinary projects and activities of the relevant Division and the OECD. Liaise with other OECD Directorates and with experts. Contribute to the organisation of, and participate in, meetings of national government delegates, as well as experts from the private sector, civil society, global community and academia in connection with the Organisation’s work programme in the above areas. Establish new networks and strengthen existing collaboration with policy makers, working parties, delegations and outside experts and international institutions to create synergies and increase the impact of the Directorate’s work. Support the external visibility of the Directorate and its products, including through communication activies and by organising, participating and presenting work at high-level meeting, conferences, workshops and webinars, and co-ordinate high-level missions to OECD and non-OECD member countries as needed. Stay abreast of policy issues in the areas of health, employment, social and skills policies and ensure, as appropriate, the Directorate’s involvement in OECD-wide initiatives. Provide general support to the activities of the relevant Division as required, including preparation of presentations, speeches and briefings for senior leadership. Actively support the Division’s fundraising efforts, including drafting project proposals and strengthening networks and engagement with potential donors as required. Carry out other tasks as assigned. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background An advanced university degree in economics, health economics, labour economics, social policy or other relevant discipline. Excellent understanding of the range of issues that impact one or more of the following: health, labour markets, employment, social and skills systems in various country contexts and experience in working on these issues in different countries. Sound knowledge of and experience in economic, public policy analysis and social research quantitative and qualitative tools such as economic modelling, public policy evaluation methods, analysis of micro administrative and survey data, designing and implementing of pilots, applied to one or more of the following: health, employment, skills and social policies. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 2); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 2); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 2); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies . item.title: Analyste des politiques – Santé, emploi, compétences et affaires sociales
item.description: {"id":"744000140894082","name":"Analyste des politiques – Santé, emploi, compétences et affaires sociales ","uuid":"5b163aa9-2dbd-4745-80f7-57059dcca550","jobId":"8b796c62-39ac-4d9c-b935-db1d9a92099a","jobAdId":"6e068e80-0ef8-45cb-903e-02fc3d67a6a6","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3304A","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000512","valueLabel":"ELS"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL6","valueLabel":"PAL6"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-31T12:13:45.754Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140894082-analyste-des-politiques-sante-emploi-competences-et-affaires-sociales-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140894082-analyste-des-politiques-sante-emploi-competences-et-affaires-sociales-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/5b163aa9-2dbd-4745-80f7-57059dcca550?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. Conformément aux objectifs stratégiques du Secrétaire général, la Direction de l’emploi, du travail et des affaires sociales (ELS) coordonne les travaux que mène l’OCDE en vue de bâtir des sociétés plus solidaires et en meilleure santé, en prodiguant des conseils stratégiques relatifs à la promotion d’emplois de qualité, à l’investissement continu dans le capital humain, à la réduction de la pauvreté et de l’exclusion, à l’amélioration de la qualité et des résultats de santé et de santé publique, à l’utilisation efficace des dispositifs médicaux et pharmaceutiques, à l’amélioration des systèmes de santé et à la bonne gestion des flux migratoires. ELS est à la recherche de plusieurs analystes des politiques ayant une expérience avérée dans les domaines de la santé, de l’emploi, des compétences et des affaires sociales. Les personnes retenues seront amenées à travailler sur divers projets au sein d’une équipe dynamique d’économistes, de spécialistes de l’action publique et de statisticiens, afin de formuler des recommandations stratégiques relatives à l’un au moins des domaines suivants : Améliorer les performances des systèmes de santé par des travaux consacrés à l'un ou à plusieurs des thèmes suivants : Mesure de la performance des systèmes de santé ; Qualité et résultats des soins de santé ; Politiques de santé publique et de prévention ; Financement de la santé, résilience des systèmes de santé et optimisation des ressources ; Ressources humaines dans le secteur de la santé ; Santé numérique, gouvernance des données et intelligence artificielle ; Politiques pharmaceutiques et génomique ; Soins de longue durée et soins intégrés. Emploi, compétences et affaires sociales Améliorer les performances des marchés du travail, des services de l’emploi, des politiques sociales et migratoires et des systèmes de compétences par des travaux consacrés à l'un ou à plusieurs des thèmes suivants : Conception, mise en application et évaluation des politiques en matière d’emploi, de compétences, de migration et d’intégration ; Analyse des politiques en matière de maladie et d’invalidité ; Recherches sur les compétences des adultes et l’évolution des besoins du marché du travail ; Avenir du travail, politiques sociales et IA ; ainsi que par des travaux sur les systèmes de protection sociale, les politiques de financement, les politiques familiales et de la jeunesse, et d’autres sujets relatifs aux politiques sociales. Les personnes qui présentent leur candidature doivent avoir une expérience solide de l’application de concepts économiques à l’un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : les systèmes de santé, les politiques sociales, les politiques de l’emploi et les politiques des compétences. Elles doivent avoir une expérience de la gestion de projets, et une capacité avérée à planifier et exécuter leur travail de manière efficace. Elles travailleront aussi bien en autonomie qu’en collaboration avec des collègues de leur division et de leur direction. Les analystes travailleront à différents projets, définis en fonction des intérêts des responsables de l’action publique et du programme de travail de la Direction. Les personnes retenues travailleront dans des équipes relevant de la division correspondant à leur domaine de compétences et seront encadrées par un ou une analyste principal des politiques. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Recherche, analyse et rédaction Réaliser des analyses des politiques et des analyses économiques de grande qualité dans ses domaines d'attribution, notamment en contribuant à des analyses interdisciplinaires et comparatives ainsi qu’à l’élaboration de recommandations stratégiques, de rapports, de synthèses et d’autres produits. Participer à la préparation de rapports, de publications phares et d’examens par pays, notamment en contribuant à l’élaboration de sources de données et de nouveaux indicateurs comparatifs, et en veillant à produire des résultats de qualité. Préparer d’autres documents de grande qualité, y compris des documents de travail, des synthèses, des documents d’orientation, des billets de blog, des comptes rendus de séminaire et des messages à l’intention des pouvoirs publics, en s’appuyant sur des travaux de recherche et des publications pertinentes. Contribuer à l’élaboration d’outils concrets, notamment de boîtes à outils destinées à soutenir la mise en œuvre des recommandations de l’OCDE, et faciliter le partage et la diffusion de l’information par des moyens innovants. Conduire des analyses statistiques afin d’expliquer les principaux écarts de résultat entre les pays. Pour certains postes, des compétences approfondies en matière d’analyse de données seront requises. Rechercher des approches innovantes pour relever les défis dans le domaine des politiques sociales et du marché du travail. Superviser le travail d’agents moins expérimentés, fournir des retours et des conseils selon les projets. Coordination, représentation et liaison Participer, selon la demande, aux activités et projets horizontaux et pluridisciplinaires de la Division concernée et de l’OCDE. Assurer la liaison avec les autres directions de l’Organisation ainsi que des experts. Prêter son concours à l’organisation de réunions de délégués des gouvernements nationaux et d’experts du secteur privé, de la société civile, de la communauté mondiale et des milieux universitaires en lien avec le programme de travail de l’Organisation dans les domaines susmentionnés, et y participer. Créer de nouveaux réseaux et renforcer la collaboration existante avec les décideurs, les groupes de travail, les délégations, les experts extérieurs et les institutions internationales afin de créer des synergies et de renforcer l’impact des travaux de la Direction. Contribuer à la visibilité extérieure de la Direction et de ses produits, notamment en menant des activités de communication et en organisant des réunions à haut niveau, des conférences, des ateliers et des webinaires, en y participant et en y présentant des travaux, et coordonner des missions à haut niveau dans des pays Membres et non Membres de l’OCDE, selon les besoins. Se tenir informé(e) des enjeux propres aux domaines de la santé, des politiques sociales, de l’emploi et des compétences et veiller, le cas échéant, à ce que la Direction soit associée à des initiatives entreprises à l’échelle de l’Organisation. Apporter globalement son soutien aux activités de la Division autant que de besoin, notamment en préparant des exposés, des discours et des notes d’information à l’intention des responsables. Soutenir activement les efforts de collecte de fonds de la Division, notamment en rédigeant des propositions de projets et en consolidant les réseaux et la collaboration avec les donateurs potentiels, le cas échéant. S’acquitter de toute autre tâche attribuée. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur en économie, économie de la santé, économie du travail, politique sociale ou dans une autre discipline pertinente. Expérience professionnelle Cinq à sept années d’expérience de la recherche et de l’analyse appliquées aux politiques sociales, aux politiques de santé,

item.description: {"id":"744000140968972","name":"Chercheur/chercheuse en politiques publiques (Économie) – Économie numérique ","uuid":"897cf3e3-7020-4086-9b0c-4d20e7d2be8a","jobId":"79d570f7-9f45-415e-819a-e605f5fba2c0","jobAdId":"2c27795e-834c-41c5-bd8b-fb85a0a26aff","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3305C","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10001210","valueLabel":"STI"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL3","valueLabel":"PAL3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-31T17:37:18.598Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140968972-chercheur-chercheuse-en-politiques-publiques-economie-economie-numerique-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000140968972-chercheur-chercheuse-en-politiques-publiques-economie-economie-numerique-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/897cf3e3-7020-4086-9b0c-4d20e7d2be8a?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. Conformément aux objectifs stratégiques du Secrétaire général, la Direction de la science, de la technologie et de l’innovation (STI) aide les pays Membres de l’OCDE et d’autres grandes économies à bâtir un environnement propice aux innovations issues de la science, de la technologie et des connaissances, en vue de créer une valeur ajoutée économique et sociale. La Division de la connectivité, de l’économie et de la société numériques (DCES), rattachée à la Direction STI, est chargée de produire des données factuelles, des analyses et des recommandations stratégiques sur des sujets fondamentaux essentiels pour la formulation de politiques du numérique, de la sûreté en ligne à la sécurité numérique, en passant par le bien-être numérique, la connectivité et les infrastructures, les technologies critiques (à l’instar des semi-conducteurs), ou encore la mesure de la transformation numérique. STI/DCES est à la recherche d’un chercheur/d’une chercheuse en politiques publiques motivé·e et inventif·ve ayant une expérience dans le domaine de l’économie pour apporter un soutien au Groupe de travail sur l’économie, la mesure et l’analyse du numérique (GTEMAN) au sein du Comité de la politique du numérique (CPN) et contribuer aux travaux de la DCES sur la mesure de la transformation numérique. La personne retenue aura une bonne connaissance des concepts économiques fondamentaux, sera experte dans l’utilisation des techniques statistiques ou économétriques et aura une bonne connaissance de la programmation. De plus, elle possèdera une aptitude avérée à communiquer des résultats complexes. Elle devra faire preuve d’autonomie, mais aussi collaborer avec d’autres membres de l’équipe. Elle travaillera sous la direction d’un membre de haut rang de l’équipe et de la Cheffe de la DCES au sein de STI. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Recherche économique et travaux relatifs à la science des données Contribuer aux projets de recherche économique menés sous l’égide du GTEMAN qui portent sur la diffusion des technologies numériques et leurs répercussions sur les résultats économiques clés (par exemple en ce qui concerne la concurrence, les marchés du travail et la productivité). Employer des approches faisant appel à l’économétrie et l’apprentissage automatique, mais aussi potentiellement à l’analyse géospatiale et/ou au traitement automatique du langage naturel. Prêter son concours à la rédaction de documents, notamment de documents de travail et de présentations, contenant des analyses quantitatives et des modélisations. Soutenir les travaux du GTEMAN visant à élaborer des normes et définitions statistiques pour la transformation numérique, et contribuer à la mise en œuvre de la Feuille de route sur la mesure de la transformation numérique. Communication et liaison Nouer de bonnes relations de travail avec les collègues au sein de STI et dans l’ensemble de l’OCDE, ainsi qu’avec les économistes et statisticiens des administrations nationales et d’autres organisations internationales. Participer aux réunions et ateliers du GTEMAN ainsi qu’à des réunions et ateliers connexes. Aider à l’élaboration de documents et d’outils méthodologiques. Contribuer à la visibilité externe de la DCES, notamment en prenant part à des ateliers, des conférences, etc., et en y présentant des travaux. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur en économie, statistique, ou mathématiques, ou dans une discipline connexe. Expérience professionnelle Au moins deux ans d’expérience pertinente en analyse économique et un vif intérêt pour la production et/ou l’utilisation de méthodologies quantitatives avancées. La connaissance de la manière de concevoir une enquête statistique, des méthodes expérimentales de collecte de données et du traitement des sources de données non conventionnelles, constituerait un avantage. Bonne aptitude à communiquer des résultats complexes. Expérience de la gestion de projets et de la participation à des projets pluridisciplinaires. Outils Connaissance de logiciels de base de données ; une connaissance pratique des principales bases de données sur les TIC en usage à l’OCDE et/ou dans d’autres organismes internationaux ou nationaux constituerait un avantage. Connaissance d’au moins un logiciel utilisé aux fins de l’analyse quantitative (Stata, R, GAMS ou SAS, par exemple). La connaissance de Python constituerait un avantage. Bonne connaissance de Git aux fins de la gestion des versions, ou volonté d’apprendre à l’utiliser. Langues Parfaite maîtrise d’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE (le français et l’anglais) et connaissance de l’autre langue, que la personne retenue s’engage à porter à un bon niveau. Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 1) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 1) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 1) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE . "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Durée du contrat Durée déterminée de 13 mois, avec possibilité de renouvellement jusqu’à un maximum de 36 mois. Date de clôture Les fonctions décrites ci-dessus devront être pourvues dès que possible, et les candidatures devront nous parvenir au plus tard à 23h59 le 13 septembre 2026 (heure de Paris). Veuillez noter que, conformément aux Statut et Règlement applicables aux agents de l’Organisation, l’âge de départ obligatoire à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. Ce qu’offre l’OCDE Le salaire mensuel minimum s’élève à 5.279 EUR, plus allocations/indemnités en fonction d’éligibilité, la rémunération globale étant exonérée d’impôt sur le revenu en France. Cliquez ici pour consulter les Statut, règlement et instructions applicables aux agents de l’OCDE. Veuillez noter que toute personne nommée agent·e à compter du 1er juillet 2025 sera engagée conformément aux nouvelles modalités contractuelles de l’OCDE . Cliquez ici pour en savoir plus sur ce que propose l’OCDE et sur son environnement de travail exceptionnel. Cliquez ici pour feuilleter en ligne notre Guide de gestion du personnel afin d’en savoir plus sur tous les aspects touchant aux ressources humaines de l’Organisation, à notre environnement de travail et aux nombreuses autres mesures destinées à faciliter le quotidien des agents. Veuillez noter que la personne retenue pourra être engagée à un grade inférieur, en fonction de ses qualifications et de son expérience professionnelle. La présente offre d’emploi pourrait servir à la constitution d’un vivier de candidat·es jugé·es aptes à exercer des fonctions comparables dans le cadre d’un engagement de durée indéterminée ou déterminée. item.title: E T Consultant - Flood Risk Modeling & Management
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org . Infrastructure Vice Presidency Globally, one billion people live more than 2 kilometers from all-weather roads, 685 million people lack electricity, and nearly 4 billion people lack internet access. Access to basic infrastructure services is critical for creating economic opportunities for the poor. The Infrastructure (INF) Vice Presidency within the World Bank is charged with developing sustainable solutions to help close infrastructure gaps in developing and emerging economies. It consists of four global departments: Energy Extractives (EEX); Transport (TRA); Resilient Tourism; Urban, Resilience and Land (URL), and Global Infrastructure Finance Department. It oversees the Bank's work across energy and transport sectors, urban development, as well as efforts to promote energy transition, low-carbon transportation, livable cities, disaster risk resilience, land management, and quality infrastructure services through public-private partnerships. Infrastructure represents around $110 billion of the Bank’s portfolio. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure The Global Knowledge Unit for Disaster Management, Solutions Impact (KIUSD) supports low and middle-income countries to understand, manage, and reduce their risks from natural hazards and climate change. Within KIUSD, the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) umbrella trust fund is a global partnership that helps low- and middle-income countries better understand and reduce their vulnerability to natural hazards and climate change. KIUSD has 14 Global Thematic Areas, which provide grant financing, analytics, and technical assistance to the most vulnerable countries and communities where it will have the greatest positive impact. As a donor-funded program, GFDRR consults regularly with donors and actively strives to maintain and develop new partnerships for increased impact. For more information: https://www.gfdrr.org/en Please note this position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. Job Duties and Responsibilities: KIUSD is seeking a qualified and motivated professional to form a critical part of the disaster risk analytical work and contribute to teams within the unit and beyond, for the implementation of activities under the Disaster Risk Analytics thematic area. Tasks include providing expert technical inputs and operational expert support on disaster risk analytics to Task Teams and World Bank clients (advice on technical studies for project design and implementation, post disaster damage assessments, developing disaster risk financing strategies, joining field missions and virtual meetings with client governments). The E T consultant will work the Disaster Risk Analytics team and will be expected to contribute or lead knowledge products related to risk analytics, and climate and disaster risk management under other KIUSD Global Technical thematic areas. The E T Consultant will work closely with the Task Team Leaders and core staff of the Global Knowledge Unit for Disaster Management, Solutions Impact (KIUSD) under managerial supervision of the Practice Manager of KIUSD: • Under the supervision of the TTL, support the development and implementation of flood risk analytics that input into post-disaster damage tools and applications including Global Rapid post-disaster Damage Estimation (GRADE) remote assessments. • Engage with regional TTLs and government counterparts on the risk analytics methodologies and results. • Develop the risk analytics capabilities with the TTL and team through the development and improvement of flood risk modelling products, innovations, coding, and tools to support Bank operations and client engagements. • Support the implementation and procurement of flood and climate related risk reduction, preparedness and climate adaptation technical activities to be carried out by client or other experts and ensure integration of disaster risks management into broader multi-hazard risk reduction strategies and response plans. • Where necessary, discuss and define with the task teams the technical requirements for activities in Flood Risk Management Technical Assistance, and identify terms of reference, international experts or institutions that can support the activity. • Cultivate and advance partnerships with firms, consultants, external institutions, and internal World Bank teams for the co-development of new products, support to operational Task Teams, and advancement of the field of flood risk management. • Illustrate Program advancements and contributions in the form of blogs, peer-reviewed papers, conference contributions, etc. • Contribute to programmatic outputs including results monitoring, reporting, budgeting, and branding. • Contribute to the work of KIUSD teams, facilitating team building, learning and knowledge sharing and collaboration. • Carry out other tasks relevant to support the overall objective of the position.

item.title: Business Process Analyst
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit www.worldbank.org . The mandate of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) is to foster increased flows of international investment by providing an impartial and effective international forum for the resolution of disputes between host governments and foreign investors. Further information about ICSID can be found on its website at www.worldbank.org/icsid . Role Responsibilities: General duties include: • Work with users to assess business operations, document business needs, and identify areas for improvement. • Identify system simplification and automation opportunities leading to optimization of internal processes and efficiencies. • Help formulate and define project scopes and objectives based on institutional requirements and user needs. • Help document business requirements and identify opportunities to design or redesign systems to meet operational needs. • Participate substantively in testing the functionality of systems being developed to determine whether requirements are being met. • Provide business insights and clarifications of requirements to support the delivery of effective technical solutions. • Provide direct support to ICSID users on new technical solutions by providing training and answering questions as needed. • Prepare user guides on new systems and applications. • Proactively identify opportunities for integration across systems and functions. • Help maintain ICSID case data in new applications, ensuring that information is entered accurately and kept up to date. • Serve as a member of the ICSID intake team, supporting the intake and processing of all requests, including requests for arbitration, conciliation, mediation, post-award remedies, appointing authority matters, and arbitrator challenges. Specific duties include, but may not be limited to: Data review and clean-up: • Work with data owners and ITS teams to identify and collect datasets from various sources. • Perform clean-up and data reconciliation based on the logic provided by the respective data owners. This would be an iterative task, with each successive iteration creating datasets of relatively higher quality. • Document reconciliation issues and contact the responsible data owner to define the clean-up strategy. • Help data owners maintain “delta” sets after the clean-up phase and through deployment to production. Creation of test plans: • Work with data owners and system users to understand business functionalities required from new applications and reports. • Document lists of test cases required for validating the functionality of the applications and reports. • Seek approval of test plans from the respective application owners. User Acceptance Testing (UAT): • Perform iterative UAT against the approved list of test cases. Work with ITS to resolve functional issues identified. • Work with data owners and ITS to find and resolve data gaps and issues. • Document and summarize test results for review and sign-off by various stakeholders.

item.title: E T Consultant, Investment Analyst, Financial Institutions Group, Peru
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. The FIG’s Latin America and the Caribbean team (FIG LAC) is based across the LAC region with main hubs and locations in Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, and Sao Paulo. The team members work on both new business development and processing, and portfolio management across the region. FIG is seeking to hire an ET Consultant to be based in Lima, Peru. The ET Consultant will be integrated into the team that develops new business, completes transactions, and supervises a portfolio of loans, quasi-equity and equity investments in FIG’s LAC region. The candidate is required to know and effectively use fundamental business concepts and practices and to provide analytical, research and other professional support to professional level Investment Officers. The work program is varied and may be somewhat complex requiring evaluation, original thinking, and various written outputs. Duties and Accountabilities • Create financial analysis models. • Support structuring of new investments. • Analyze historical and projected financial statements and prepare periodic portfolio reports. • Conduct industry and market research and assist in IFC’s business development efforts. • Monitor operational and financial performance of client companies to evaluate risk and recommend active portfolio management actions. • Prepare documentation for IFC internal processes and monitor compliance with IFC financial, environmental and legal requirements. • Establish and maintain quality client relationships to ensure responsive client service and to enhance new business opportunities. • Participate in investments negotiations. • Liaise with colleagues across departments and the region and at the head office in Washington DC. • Participate in the monitoring of investments in portfolio companies.

item.title: ETC - Disaster Risk Finance /Insurance and Modeling Expert
item.description: Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty on a livable planet, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . Prosperity Vice Presidency The WBG Prosperity Vice Presidency is responsible for getting the right public and private sector solutions to our operational teams and to our clients, and to produce scalable impact. It l eads the WBG’s key global engagements in support of: Growth and jobs (including supporting teams across the WBG on the jobs agenda); debt sustainability and debt management; improved domestic resource mobilization and expenditure efficiency; a resilient and inclusive financial sector; business-enabling policies and regulations; trade policy and facilitation; and transparent, effective, and accountable government institutions world-wide. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission. Financial Services Sector (FSS) I Department The FSS Global Department is comprised of two directorates: FSS I covers financial resilience and integrity, financial inclusion, capital market development and disaster risk finance, while FSS II covers SME finance, Banking, Housing, Leasing and Insurance, as well as Sustainable Finance. Disaster Risk Finance Unit The Disaster Risk Finance (DRF) team in FSS1 helps client governments strengthen financial resilience to disaster shocks. Through the Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program (DRFIP), the team delivers technical assistance, analytical work, and advisory support, drawing on the World Bank’s crisis preparedness and response toolkit and other financial instruments. It works closely with regional and country teams, government counterparts, private sector, development partners to design and implement solutions tailored to each country’s risk profile and institutional context. The DRF team also contributes to global efforts to close insurance protection gaps, including through engagement with the G7, G20, the International Association of Insurance Supervisors, and the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), among others. Against this background, the DRF team seeks an Extended Term Consultant (ETC) to provide senior-level technical advice and engagement support for the Unit’s work program on DRFI, insurance market development, and risk modeling. The position is based in London, United Kingdom, and requires frequent travel. Duties and Responsibilities The ETC will be responsible for the following: • Lead the delivery of disaster risk finance instruments and mechanisms in countries, including sovereign risk transfer products such as parametric insurance, catastrophe bonds, and risk pooling arrangements, as well as contingent financing facilities, disaster reserve funds, and risk-based public financial management frameworks. • Provide ad hoc actuarial and quantitative analysis to support client engagement, policy dialogue, and internal decision-making, including identifying options to strengthen financial protection across risk layers undertaking value for money analysis. • Review and quality-assure technical outputs prepared by others, including diagnostic reports, strategy documents, financial models, and presentations. • Curate and share knowledge on insurance market development, including key bottlenecks, global trends, insurance technology, the integration of insurance into climate risk management, relevant case studies, and financial innovations for client countries. This may include co-authoring policy and research notes, preparing internal guidance, developing policy and industry toolkits, and organizing seminars and workshops. • Collaborate with internal stakeholders such as IFC, MIGA, Treasury, and external stakeholders, including the Insurance Development Forum (IDF). • Represent the CDRFI team in stakeholder consultations, interagency coordination forums, workshops, and donor dialogues, as needed. • Perform other duties and tasks assigned by the Unit Manager. The initial appointment will be for one year, with possible renewal for up to two additional years, subject to business needs, funding availability, and satisfactory performance. Under World Bank Group policy, Extended Term appointments are limited to a lifetime maximum of three years.

It leads the WBG’s key global engagements in support of: Growth and jobs (including supporting teams across the WBG on the jobs agenda); debt sustainability and debt management; improved domestic resource mobilization and expenditure efficiency; a resilient and inclusive financial sector; business-enabling policies and regulations; trade policy and facilitation; and transparent, effective, and accountable government institutions world-wide. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission. Financial Services Sector (FSS) I Department The FSS Global Department is comprised of two directorates: FSS I covers financial resilience and integrity, financial inclusion, capital market development and disaster risk finance, while FSS II covers SME finance, Banking, Housing, Leasing and Insurance, as well as Sustainable Finance. Disaster Risk Finance Unit The Disaster Risk Finance (DRF) team in FSS1 helps client governments strengthen financial resilience to disaster shocks. Through the Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program (DRFIP), the team delivers technical assistance, analytical work, and advisory support, drawing on the World Bank’s crisis preparedness and response toolkit and other financial instruments. It works closely with regional and country teams, government counterparts, private sector, development partners to design and implement solutions tailored to each country’s risk profile and institutional context. The DRF team also contributes to international regulatory discussions through the G7, G20, the International Association of Insurance Supervisors, and the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS). In this context, the team is seeking an Extended Term Consultant (ETC) to provide senior-level technical advice and engagement in support of the Unit’s work on insurance regulatory and supervisory approaches and insurance market development. The position is based in London, UK, and requires frequent travel. Duties Responsibilities: The ETC will be responsible for the following: • Lead or contribute to work on insurance regulatory, supervisory, and market practices, including supporting or leading country-level engagements through relevant financing operations and advisory and knowledge activities; • Develop, curate, and share knowledge on insurance market development, including key bottlenecks, emerging global trends, the integration of insurance into climate risk management, insurance technology, relevant case studies, and financial innovations for client countries. This may include co-authoring policy and research notes, preparing internal guidance, developing policy and industry toolkits, and organizing seminars and workshops; • Participate in Financial Sector Assessment Programs (FSAPs) and prepare Insurance Core Principle (ICP) reviews, technical notes, and other policy notes as needed; • Collaborate with international insurance organizations, including the International Association of Insurance Supervisors (IAIS), Sustainable Insurance Forum (SIF), European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA), Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Insurance Development Forum (IDF), and others; • Represent the CDRFI team in stakeholder consultations, interagency coordination forums, workshops, and donor dialogues, as needed. • Perform other duties and tasks assigned by the unit manager. The initial appointment will be for one year, with the possibility of renewal for up to an additional two years, subject to business needs, funding availability, and satisfactory performance. As per World Bank Group policy, Extended Term appointments are subject to a lifetime maximum of three (3) years.

item.title: Analyste de la sécurité et des réseaux électriques
item.description: {"id":"744000141302924","name":"Analyste de la sécurité et des réseaux électriques","uuid":"6ce1fc74-96e7-44d6-ac3d-2569690427f7","jobId":"95140137-15e3-49d4-a9e8-415e9e9c7dcf","jobAdId":"d8cc7ab4-681b-4b13-a3d1-829f05d0f2b9","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3341X","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"5a9445ef-058b-4346-8dca-ef49c8638ded","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL6","valueLabel":"PAL6"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-03T15:59:10.562Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141302924-analyste-de-la-securite-et-des-reseaux-electriques","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141302924-analyste-de-la-securite-et-des-reseaux-electriques?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/6ce1fc74-96e7-44d6-ac3d-2569690427f7?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. L’ Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est une organisation intergouvernementale qui œuvre en faveur de la sécurité des approvisionnements énergétiques, de la croissance économique et de la durabilité environnementale en promouvant la coopération dans le domaine des politiques énergétiques. L’AIE fonctionne en tant qu’organe autonome au sein de l’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques. L’AIE recherche des analystes de la sécurité et des réseaux électriques pour contribuer à ses travaux d’analyse des réseaux et de l’électrification menés au sein de sa Division des systèmes et marchés de l’électricité (ESM). Les personnes retenues prendront part aux travaux de la Division sur la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité et, en particulier, la modernisation des réseaux de transport et de distribution. Il s’agira d’analyser et de modéliser les systèmes électriques sous l’angle physique et techno-économique, et d’élaborer des projets axés sur les réseaux. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Modélisation, analyse et rédaction Piloter les travaux techniques, d’analyse et de modélisation de la Division consacrés aux systèmes électriques, à la modernisation des réseaux (transport et distribution) et à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité. Conduire des travaux d’analyse portant sur les moyens d’intégrer au système les nouvelles sources de production d’électricité et les nouvelles formes de demande, en mettant l’accent sur la sécurité d’exploitation, la fiabilité et la résilience. Analyser les évolutions de la gestion de la congestion, des processus de raccordement au réseau et de la planification stratégique des réseaux sur les principaux marchés de l’électricité. Suivre les innovations et les pratiques opérationnelles visant à permettre une utilisation plus efficiente des réseaux, notamment les technologies d’amélioration des réseaux, les solutions numériques et les cadres de réglementation. Contribuer à l’exécution du programme de l’AIE relatif à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité, et prendre part à la rédaction de contenus relatifs au réseau pour le rapport de l’AIE sur l’électricité et d’autres publications pertinentes de la Division des systèmes et marchés de l’électricité. Collaboration et relations avec l’extérieur Échanger avec les principales parties prenantes du secteur ; prêter son concours, en tant que de besoin, aux préparatifs des réunions des comités permanents, des groupes de travail et, si nécessaire, d’autres groupes de l’AIE ; participer aux réunions pertinentes d’autres organisations internationales ; concourir à l’établissement des rapports, analyses et éléments d’information destinés à ces réunions. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur ou doctorat en génie électrique, génie énergétique, génie des systèmes énergétiques, économie de l’énergie, physique ou dans une discipline connexe. Expérience professionnelle Au moins cinq à sept ans d’expérience directement acquise sur les systèmes électriques dans une entreprise du secteur de l’électricité, une société de conseil économique, une entreprise axée sur les technologies de réseau ou une autorité de réglementation de l’électricité, en travaillant sur les réseaux de transport ou de distribution, l’exploitation des systèmes, la gestion de l’énergie ou un domaine connexe. Solide connaissance technique des systèmes électriques et compréhension approfondie des concepts liés à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité, des fondamentaux du marché de l’électricité et de l’interaction entre l’exploitation du système et les incitations du marché. Solide connaissance des réseaux de distribution de moyenne et de basse tension, avec une bonne compréhension des cadres régissant les processus de raccordement et l’intégration des ressources énergétiques décentralisées. Une expérience de la planification du réseau et des pratiques opérationnelles visant à améliorer l’efficience et l’utilisation des infrastructures existantes est souhaitable. Une expérience de la modélisation des systèmes électriques, notamment la modélisation des réseaux en régime stationnaire, en régime dynamique ou en stabilité transitoire, ou de l’étude de la planification ou de l’extension du réseau constituerait un avantage. Capacités d’analyse avérées et excellente compétence rédactionnelle, confirmées par les produits de travaux antérieurs (rapports analytiques, analyses quantitatives, modèles opératoires et/ou textes publiés). Outils Excellente maîtrise des applications Microsoft Office, en particulier d’Excel. Une expérience de SQL ou Power Query constituerait un atout. Solide connaissance de langages de programmation pertinents (Python par exemple). Une expérience de logiciels de modélisation de réseau pertinents (PowerFactory, PSS, PSCAD, par exemple) constituerait un avantage. Langues Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral, avec des compétences rédactionnelles et éditoriales. La connaissance d’une ou de plusieurs autres langues constituerait un atout. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 2) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE . Durée du contrat Durée déterminée de deux ans, avec possibilité de renouvellement. Veuillez noter que, conformément aux Statut et Règlement applicables aux agents de l’Organisation, l’âge de départ obligatoire à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. Ce qu’offre l’OCDE Le salaire mensuel minimum s’élève à 8 098.36 EUR, plus allocations/indemnités en fonction de la situation personnelle, la rémunération globale étant exonérée d’impôt sur le revenu en France. Cliquez ici pour consulter les Statut, règlement et instructions applicables aux agents de l’OCDE. Veuillez noter que toute personne nommée agent·e à compter du 1er juillet 2025 sera engagée conformément aux nouvelles modalités contractuelles de l’OCDE . Cliquez ici pour en savoir plus sur ce que propose l’OCDE et sur son environnement de travail exceptionnel. Cliquez ici pour feuilleter en ligne notre Guide de gestion du personnel afin d’en savoir plus sur tous les aspects touchant aux ressources humaines de l’Organisation, à notre environnement de travail et aux nombreuses autres mesures destinées à faciliter le quotidien des agents. Veuillez noter que la personne retenue pourra être engagée à un grade inférieur, en fonction de ses qualifications et de son expérience professionnelle. La présente offre d’emploi servira à la constitution d’un vivier de candidat·es jugé·es aptes à exercer des fonctions compar
