item.title: Senior Economist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/home VPU Context: The South Asia Region (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka) is at a crucial stage of development. Rapid economic growth, driven by urbanization and demographic dividend, has brought down poverty rates, but severe forms of exclusion and disparities based on ethnicity, caste, and gender remain. Rapid growth has also come with congestion and pollution in cities. South Asia is more than other regions affected by changes in temperature and extreme weather event. Additional challenges are that South Asia is underperforming in exports, has large informal sectors and low female labor force participation rates. All these challenges must be addressed to secure rapid growth in coming decades. Private sector led growth, focused on investments in infrastructure, energy, logistics and cities are essential to generate the jobs needed to employ South Asia’s sizeable youth population. At the same time, the region needs to continue building human capital so that South Asia’s population is well equipped for the jobs of the future. The World Bank in South Asia: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/region/sar Unit Context: The Finance, Competitiveness and Investment (FCI) Global Practice of the World Bank combines expertise in the financial sector with expertise in private sector development to foster private-sector led growth and help create markets in client countries. FCI’s core lines of business are: (a) Financial Stability Integrity; (b) Financial Inclusion, Infrastructure Access; (c) Firm Capabilities Innovation; (d) Long-Term Finance; (e) Climate Risk Management; (f) Markets and Technology; and (g) Investment and Competition. For more information, please visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/unit/fci SAR FCI unit is seeking a Senior Economist for a locally recruited, 3-year term appointment based in New Delhi, India, to support our growing portfolio of advisory and lending projects focused on private sector development. The selected candidate will contribute to financing and lending operations, analytical and advisory services (ASA), and policy dialogue related to financial sector development. Duties and accountabilities: • Provide intellectual and technical leadership on financial sector development issues in India. Engage in strategic dialogue with senior government counterparts (e.g. Ministry of Finance and financial regulators) and private sector stakeholders to identify challenges and opportunities in the financial sector. Offer policy advice and technical input on reforms related to financial stability and development. • Lead / co-lead the development of lending operations aimed at mobilizing private capital. Structure innovative financing solutions, including blended finance instruments, to leverage private sector resources for development projects. This includes conceptualizing project design, preparing project documentation, and coordinating across teams to align operations with the new World Bank’s country strategy. • Drive the creation of high-quality analytical work on financial sector topics. This entails leading economic and sector work that address key development challenges in India’s financial sector. Ensure analytical outputs are rigorous, relevant, and actionable, communicating complex financial concepts in clear terms for policymakers. • Work in close collaboration with colleagues across the FCI Global Practice and other Global Practices to deliver integrated solutions. Coordinate with the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), and other World Bank Group teams to harness synergies and ensure a unified approach in engagements with clients. • Champion private capital mobilization as a cross-cutting priority across all dimensions of the engagement, whether policy advocacy, the design of lending operations, analytical work, or collaboration with other Global Practices and sister organizations. Embed private capital solutions systematically into the team's work program, ensuring that opportunities to crowd in private finance are identified and pursued consistently rather than treated in isolation. • Serve as a key point of contact for financial sector engagements in India, maintaining strong client relationships built on trust and technical expertise. Represent the World Bank in meetings, workshops, and conferences related to the financial sector. Proactively identify client needs and emerging issues, and respond with relevant World Bank support or knowledge offerings. • Mentor and guide junior staff and team members, fostering a positive and inclusive team environment. Share knowledge and best practices within the team and across the Global Practice. Demonstrate a collaborative team spirit, working effectively in multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams.

item.title: Senior External Relations Officer
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org. Communications and External Relations (CER) The mission of Communications and external relations (CER) is to help deliver financial and political support for the World Bank Group, strengthen the Bank Group’s role as a global thought leader in development by enhancing and safeguarding its reputation, and supporting operational teams to achieve country outcomes. CER manages corporate communications and global engagement with key stakeholders, including media, civil society, foundations, private sector, donor countries, and international organizations, as well as employee engagement. CER also manages strategic communications for the World Bank Group’s Regions and technical units and leads the management of reputation risk. Regional Stakeholder Engagement in CER (CERRS) The Regional Stakeholder Engagement team manages strategic communications across the seven regions of the World Bank Group driving engagement across regions and country offices to align local efforts with our global strategy. The work aims to build support and understanding for World Bank Group (WBG) priorities across a range of stakeholders; enhance and protect the reputation of the WBG as a leading development organization; support operational effectiveness and social accountability by sharing development progress, knowledge, and results. Recognizing that economic and social contexts evolve rapidly, and that communications technologies have revolutionized the ways that information travels, we are building a team of dynamic and innovative professionals prepared to use innovative engagement strategies, traditional and digital tools, including social media and artificial intelligence to shape the debate on development priorities and tradeoffs. East Asia and Pacific East Asia and Pacific (EAP) is among the world’s fastest‑growing, most dynamic regions. The World Bank partners with countries across EAP to promote economic growth and job creation, strengthen human capital, and advance sustainable energy, water, and agriculture for a resilient and prosperous future for all. Over the past two decades, EAP has sustained strong growth, lifting hundreds of millions of people out of poverty and transforming economies and lives. Many countries have reached upper‑middle‑income status and are aiming for high‑income status. Poverty rates continue to fall, with 24 million people in the region projected to escape poverty between 2024 and 2025 (based on the upper‑middle‑income poverty line). Despite this progress, major challenges remain. About 320 million people will reach working age over the next decade, while only around 110 million new jobs are projected—making job creation an urgent priority. Widening inequality within and across countries underscores the need to expand access to education, healthcare, and social safety nets, particularly for the urban poor and rural communities. Rapid urbanization increases demand for transport connectivity, water and sanitation, and pollution management. Meeting rising electricity needs at affordable cost—without sharply increasing greenhouse gas emissions—requires accelerating the energy transition. Adaptation and resilience to extreme weather and natural disasters are critical in a region that includes 13 of the world’s 30 most climate‑vulnerable countries. Since 2000, EAP has experienced 70 percent of the world’s natural disasters, affecting more than 1.6 billion people. East Asia and Pacific Regional Stakeholder Engagement Team (CEREA) The East Asia and Pacific (EAP) Regional Stakeholder Engagement team (CEREA) manages strategic communications and external relations in support of the WBG strategic priorities in EAP. It includes communications and external relations professionals both in Washington, D.C. and WBG EAP Country Offices. CEREA’s goal is to connect and engage with diverse stakeholders across EAP to communicate about the WBG mission to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet, promote an informed, evidence-based debate about development in the region, and enhance the WBG’s reputation as an effective development partner for the countries of East Asia and Pacific. CEREA’s key audiences include government officials, think tanks and researchers, business leaders and associations, investors, development partners, civil society organizations, and journalists. Recognizing that economic and social contexts evolve rapidly, and that communications technologies have revolutionized the ways that information travels, we are building a team of dynamic and innovative professionals prepared to use innovative engagement strategies, traditional and digital tools, including social media and artificial intelligence to shape the debate on development priorities and tradeoffs. Senior Communications and External Affairs Officer The Senior External Affairs Officer is a senior member of the EAP (CEREA) Regional Stakeholder Engagement team and serves as a strategic advisor to regional management on stakeholder engagement, communications, advocacy, and reputational risk management. The position plays a key role in advancing the World Bank Group's regional stakeholder engagement agenda and driving delivery across CER's four business lines: Stakeholder Engagement, Strategic Business Marketing, Advocacy Campaigns, and Risk Issue Management. The role requires strong strategic judgment, political awareness, and the ability to anticipate risks, influence stakeholders, shape narratives, and mobilize support for development priorities. Working closely with regional and country management, operational teams, and colleagues across IBRD, IDA, IFC, and MIGA, the Senior Communications and External Affairs Officer helps advance a coordinated One World Bank Group approach to external affairs. The position combines strategic advisory responsibilities with hands-on delivery and is expected to lead complex assignments, support priority initiatives, and contribute directly to execution across the regional portfolio. The Senior Communications External Relations Officer position is based in Washington, D.C. and reports to CER Manager, EAP. Key Responsibilities Stakeholder Engagement • Lead stakeholder engagement strategies that advance World Bank Group priorities, support country outcomes, and strengthen the institution's influence across the region. • Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including government officials, development partners, private sector leaders, civil society organizations, media, academia, and other influential actors. • Lead stakeholder intelligence efforts, including stakeholder mapping, analysis, and monitoring of actors, coalitions, and trends that may affect World Bank Group priorities, reform efforts, or reputation. • Advise management and operational teams on stakeholder dynamics, political economy considerations, coalition-building opportunities, and engagement approaches. • Ensure stakeholder insights and external perspectives are incorporated into communications strategies, advocacy efforts, risk management, and operational decision-making. Strategic Business Marketing • Position the World Bank Group as a trusted development partner by articulating the value of integrated public-private solutions and the One World Bank Group approach. • Develop strategic narratives, engagement approaches, and communications products that support regional priorities, operational objectives, and client engagement. • Identify and elevate flagship operations, reform milestones, knowledge products, and success stories that demonstrate impact and generate demand for World Bank Group engagement. • Identify opportunities to strengthen visibility and understanding of the World Bank Group's work among governments, investors, private sector partners, foundations, and development stakeholders. Advocacy Campaigns • Lead advocacy and communications campaigns that support development priorities, reform efforts, and institutional objectives. • Develop compelling messaging and narratives that translate complex development issues into clear, accessible, and persuasive communications. • Coordinate regional contributions to corporate and global campaigns, adapting messages and approaches to regional and country contexts. • Oversee the development of speeches, op-eds, press releases, talking points, digital content, and other communications products for senior management and key stakeholders. • Help ensure consistent, targeted, and effective messaging across communications, stakeholder engagement, digital, and media channels. Risk Issue Management • Serve as a senior advisor on reputational risk and issue management, helping management anticipate, assess, and respond to developments that could affect World Bank Group operations, stakeholder relationships, or reputation. • Lead or coordinate risk assessments, stakeholder analyses, issue management efforts, and mitigation strategies for sensitive operations, reforms, and institutional priorities. • Advise management and operational teams on positioning, stakeholder considerations, and communications approaches related to complex or high-profile issues. • Develop issue briefs, risk assessments, scenario plans, leadership briefing materials, and response strate

item.title: Industry Specialist
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. We are seeking an Industry Specialist, based in Washington D.C. Role Overview The Industry Specialist will operate at the intersection of technical due diligence, commercial viability, and policy/regulatory frameworks, with the objective of enhancing project bankability and enabling private capital participation. Key Responsibilities Technical Due Diligence and support • Define, lead and challenge technical due diligence across transport projects (design, capex, opex, implementation risks), including ToR drafting, consultant selection, appraisal trips/site visits to identify potential issues, validate assumptions, and test operational readiness. • Translate technical findings into clear implications for financial viability, risk allocation, and structuring. • Assess whether project design is aligned with demand realities and operational efficiency requirements. • Identify key technical risks and define practical mitigation measures compatible with private sector expectations. • Review contractual frameworks (EPC, O M, concession agreements) with a focus on lender/investor requirements. • Ensure alignment between technical assumptions and financial models (capex, opex, ramp-up). • Support preparation of investment materials with a clear articulation of risks, mitigants, and value drivers. • Provide a commercial perspective on market dynamics • Support pipeline development by screening opportunities, identifying risks and solutions, engaging with governments, clients, sponsors, operators, and internal teams when required to shape commercially viable and bankable pathways to private financing. • Support portfolio supervision by monitoring technical and operational performance, identifying emerging risks, advising on corrective actions, and feeding lessons learned into new origination. Policy Regulation – Bridging Public and Private • Work closely with regional teams to ensure policy and regulatory frameworks are aligned with private sector participation requirements. • Translate regulatory and institutional constraints into concrete implications for project bankability. • Advise public sector counterparts on how to design projects and frameworks that can attract private capital (tariffs, risk allocation, contractual structures). • Identify key bottlenecks (regulatory, institutional, technical) and propose targeted, practical reforms. • Contribute to ensuring consistency between upstream policy work and downstream investment execution. Knowledge Replicability • Capture lessons learned across projects to inform repeatable models for private capital mobilization. • Contributes to the development of practical guidance, tools, and templates for teams across regions. • Support dissemination of best practices linking policy frameworks, technical design, and investment outcomes.

item.title: E T Temporary - Program Assistant
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . In July2024, the World Bank Group launched the WBG Guarantee Platform (WB GP) a major upgrade to its guarantees business, that will deliver improved guarantee access through a unified team at MIGA as well as innovative new guarantee solutions. These new reforms will help position MIGA to achieve the goal of tripling annual guarantee issuance to $20 billion by 2030. MIGA’s Eastern Europe Regional Office (ECA) is recruiting a one-year Extended Term Temporary (ETT) to provide high-quality administrative, operational, and coordination support to the regional team, contributing to the efficient functioning of business development activities, office operations, information management, and stakeholder coordination. The selected candidate will report to the MIGA Regional Head based in Vienna, Austria, and will work closely with the regional team and relevant World Bank Group stakeholders. Duties and Accountabilities A. Business Development Support • Utilize digital solutions efficiently to support administrative and operational tasks. • Coordinate schedules and calendars, taking priorities into account, and communicate updates to relevant internal and external stakeholders. • Draft routine correspondence and format business documents and presentations. • Coordinate logistics for meetings, workshops, conferences, and events, including invitations, venue arrangements, catering, and related administrative support. • Coordinate mission travel for staff to the region, particularly senior management missions, as well as general staff travel arrangements. • Support the organization of conferences and business development events, including preparation of marketing materials and coordination of meeting facilities. • Establish and maintain lists and databases of clients, partners, and stakeholders. • Contribute to the preparation of marketing and business development materials, particularly PowerPoint presentations and pipeline reports. • Under the guidance of the Regional Head and senior staff, prepare monthly business development activity reports, including retrieval, analysis, and presentation of relevant data. B. Information Management • Maintain and update internal shared resources, databases, and filing systems. • Assist in preparing background materials for meetings and events. • Compile, organize, and distribute documents to relevant participants and stakeholders. • Prepare presentation materials and produce complex texts, reports, figures, charts, and graphs. C. Office Administration and Operations • Manage general office administration, including: o Office inventories and asset tracking o Filing and records management o Courier services and urgent mail delivery o Coordination with vendors and service providers • Process vendor invoices, purchase orders, and non-staff reimbursements through the ePayables Portal. • Work with a high level of professionalism, discretion, and diplomacy in managing priorities and workflow. • Perform ad hoc administrative and operational assignments as required. • Provide backup support to colleagues when necessary. D. HR and Staff Support Coordination • Serve as the regional office coordinator for the Leave and Attendance Record System (LARS). • Coordinate with local HR representatives on administrative HR matters, including: o Staff and dependent visa renewals and expirations o UNLP documentation o Local employment permits and exemptions o Related follow-up actions and documentation support 4. Required Competencies and Skills • Strong organizational and multitasking skills • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Russian • High level of attention to detail and professionalism • Ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office applications • Experience with MIGA or WBG internal systems, business processes is a must • Familiarity with AI-enabled productivity tools and digital collaboration platforms • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multicultural environment • Strong interpersonal skills and client-oriented approach • Ability to handle confidential information with discretion

item.title: Driver
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit www.worldbank.org . Regional Context The Middle East and North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan (MENAAP) Region serves twenty two countries across different income groups, of which fourteen are active/potentially active IBRD/IDA borrowers (Afghanistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Pakistan, Syria, West Bank and Gaza, Tunisia, and Yemen), with a total of 251 projects and over $51 bn in total commitment. Eight are users of the Region's non-lending services, mostly on a reimbursable basis (Bahrain, Kuwait, Libya, Malta, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates). The mission of the region is to foster sustainable growth with a focus on job creation and poverty reduction, economic and social inclusion, and good governance. The region attaches importance to creating a supportive work environment based on the values of teamwork, transparency, trust, and client service, underlined by professional excellence. The region places high value on diversity. The region is organized into seven Country Departments (CMUs), the Office of the Regional Chief Economist, and the Development Effectiveness Unit (MNADE). With an expanded regional strategy, the World Bank aims to help the region weather the current crises, move from stabilization to transformation, unlock its vast economic potential of youth and women, develop its human capital to adapt to global megatrends, and foster innovation (https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/mena). The World Bank Group in Saudi Arabia The partnership between the World Bank (WB) and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) goes back almost 70 years and continues to grow. In 2025, the World Bank Group placed its Regional Hub office for the MENAAP Region in Riyadh. The growing office houses the Regional Vice President, the Regional Practice Directors, Regional Hub Office Manager, as well as close to 100 senior specialist and support staff. The WB engagement in KSA focuses on partnerships, knowledge, and technical advisory support. The World Bank’ s Reimbursable Advisory Services (RAS) engagements are directed towards strengthening institutional capacity within the government entities and assisting in developing legislation and policies that advance the Kingdom’s development goals. The WB engagement in KSA supports the realization of the Vision 2030 and includes work on the investment and business climate, education, health, labor markets, transport, energy, water, agriculture, urban planning, economic management, public financial management, PPPs, and SME, among others. The Regional Hub Office in Riyadh is part of the World Bank’s Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Country Management Unit (CMU) which serves as the principal liaison between the World Bank and the six Arab States of the GCC, with additional country offices in Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. The World Bank is seeking to recruit a highly qualified candidate for the position of Driver in the Saudi Arabia Hub Office. The Driver will be based in Riyadh Country Office and will report to the Hub Manager. Roles Responsibility: • Transport Bank staff to desired destinations. Drive office vehicle(s) as requested, with due regard to time schedules, apply knowledge of driving regulations, safety requirements, traffic and conditions, and preferable routes to minimize travel time. • Ensure that highest security standards are applied by passengers as per the Bank Road Safety guidelines and that local regulations are adhered to. • Perform the routine maintenance and cleaning of the assigned vehicle, check gasoline, oil, water, battery, brakes, signal lights, tires, etc.; conduct minor repairs and maintenance. • Take suitable precautions for the security of the vehicle and its contents when left unattended. • Maintain records of trips time and duration, mileage, gasoline consumption, oil changes, and servicing. • Deliver the vehicle to the designated vehicle maintenance location and ensure maintenance execution as requested. • Make minor purchases, collection, and delivery of required goods from local suppliers as needed for the office. • Undertake other assigned tasks requested by or through the Senior Driver.

item.title: Environmental Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org. Eastern and Southern Africa (AFE) Region Home to about 700 million of Africa’s people, Eastern and Southern Africa is a geographically, culturally and economically diverse region of 26 countries stretching from the Red Sea in the North to the Cape of Good Hope in the South. Children under 18 make up almost half of the total population. The subregion boasts of some of the world’s richest human and natural resources and, apart from South Africa, the countries are predominantly raw material exporters. The subregion harbors some of Africa’s protracted conflicts, rendering many of its countries fragile, while significant gaps in education, health, and skills development continue to keep people from reaching their full potential. This creates a huge development challenge, impacts heavily on the lives and livelihoods of people, and hinders regional integration and trade. But it also creates an opportunity to work closely with country leaders, civil society, development partners, and young people to chart a brighter course for the future. The World Bank’s Eastern and Southern Africa Region, comprised of approximately 1,200 staff, mostly based in 26 country offices, has been helping countries realize their considerable development potential by focusing on the following priorities: Creating Jobs and Transforming Economies: We are working with countries across Africa to stimulate job creation and economic transformation by leveraging all sources of finance, expertise, and solutions to promote investment. Building up the Digital Economy: We are supporting Africa’s vision to ensure that every African individual, business, and government is connected by 2030 – a vision that, if realized, can boost growth by up to 2 percentage points per year, and reduce poverty by 1 percentage point per year in Sub-Saharan Africa alone. Making Institutions more Efficient and Accountable: Our support helps governments strengthen public policy processes, manage resources effectively, and reinforce fair and reliable delivery of public services. Investing in People: We are at the forefront of helping African countries accelerate human capital gains and empower women by improving their access to education and skills acquisition, sexual and reproductive health services, and employment opportunities. Supporting Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation: In the face of increasing climate-related risks, we are working with African countries to advance efforts to adopt renewable energy, climate-smart agriculture, and green infrastructure. Addressing the Drivers of Fragility, Conflict, and Violence: Given the cross-border nature of conflicts in Africa, we are employing an approach that simultaneously focuses on the drivers of fragility while also supporting well-targeted regional initiatives to create opportunities for peace and shared prosperity. Building Partnerships and Working across the African Continent: We are scaling up our work on regional integration, taking a holistic view of the continent that covers both North and Sub-Saharan Africa. Eastern and Southern Africa (AFE) Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/afr/eastern-and-southern-africa Unit Description: On October 1, 2018, the World Bank launched a new Environment and Social Framework (ESF) to help protect people and the environment in the investment projects that it finances. The effort, now about seven years under implementation, is one of several initiatives, including procurement reform, the gender strategy, and the climate change action plan, undertaken by the Bank to improve development outcomes. The ESF brings the World Bank’s environmental and social (E S) protections into closer harmony with those of other development institutions, and makes important advances in areas such as transparency, non-discrimination, social inclusion, public participation, and accountability – including expanded roles for grievance redress mechanisms. The ESF helps to ensure social inclusion, non-discrimination, and explicitly references human rights in the overarching vision statement. As the World Bank Group (WBG) advances with modernizing its ESF approach, a new organizational arrangement has been agreed involving “Makers” (responsible for preparation, implementation support, and monitoring and problem solving) and “Checkers” (responsible for monitoring and risk-based oversight and identifying and flagging challenges and problems that need to be addressed) to ensure a strengthened approach to risk management on E S matters. The new arrangements also demonstrate a commitment to promoting “One WBG” and the key role that the Environmental and Social leadership in IDA/IBRD, IFC and MIGA, will play in this effort. The Central Safeguards Unit (SAEM3) is one of the three units in AFE that manages E S risks and covers two Country Management Units (CMUs): The Ethiopia CMU comprising of Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan and Eritrea; and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) CMU comprising of DRC, Angola, Burundi and Sao Tome and Principe. The Position – Environmental Specialist This position is based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia and will focus on environmental and social risk management, including on health and safety in Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Sudan. This position will focus on implementing the World Bank’s environmental and social risk management policies (including the Safeguard Policies and the Environmental and Social Framework, or ESF) and building and strengthening national systems and capacity in this regard. All World Bank-supported investment projects must meet ambitious environmental, social, health and safety standards. SAEM3 is responsible for providing technical support and oversight into all investment projects to meet these obligations. Duties Responsibilities: The Environmental Specialist will have the following key responsibilities: • Conduct environmental and social risk management due diligence of World Bank-financed operations, including preparation of Environmental and Social Review Summaries (ESRSs), E S Section of the Project Appraisal Document (PAD), etc. • Ensure the effective integration of environment, health, and safety into the design, preparation, appraisal, and implementation of World Bank-supported projects, in line with the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), WBG EHS guidelines, IFC Performance Standards, and other good international practices. • Oversee compliance with World Bank Group EHS guidelines, IFC Performance Standards, and other relevant frameworks. • Guide and support clients and counterparts in preparing project documents, including Environmental and Social Commitment Plans (ESCPs), Labor • Management Procedure (LMP), Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), Stakeholder • Engagement Plans (SEPs), Project Implementation Manuals (PIMs), and others to meet ESF and operational policy requirements. • Support timely and accurate disclosure procedures and public consultation for all required environmental assessment and management instruments. • Provide guidance on specialized plans (e.g., biodiversity management, resource efficiency and waste management, occupational health and safety, dam safety, international waterways). • Support clients and counterparts with incident and accident management, including immediate, underlying and root cause analysis, implementation of corrective actions, reporting, and ensuring SEA/SH-sensitive confidentiality for projects with moderate environmental and social risks. • Organize and deliver needs assessments, capacity building, and technical training on environmental, health, and safety risk management for national agencies, local governments, and public/private sector practitioners. • Collaborate with other World Bank Group teams to integrate risk management capacity development into sectoral programs. • Work closely with Lead Specialist and the CMU ESF Coordinator, as well as Task Team Leaders and cross-practice teams (Procurement, Legal) to ensure quality and consistency in safeguards work and risk management across the region.

item.title: Senior Conference Assistant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit www.worldbank.org . The International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) is the world's leading institution devoted to international investment dispute settlement. ICSID administers a large and complex portfolio of cases and supports hearings, sessions, deliberations, conferences and training activities across multiple jurisdictions and time zones. The Senior Conference Assistant plays a key role in the planning, coordination, and execution of hearings and events. The position is responsible for independently managing logistical and administrative arrangements for in-person, virtual and hybrid proceedings, coordinating vendors and service providers, maintaining hearing schedules and planning tools and supporting improvements to hearing operations and related systems. The Senior Conference Assistant also contributes to institutional initiatives to enhance the efficiency, quality and consistency of hearing services. Further information about ICSID is available on its website at www.worldbank.org/icsid . Role Responsibilities: Hearing and Event Management • Independently coordinate end-to-end logistical arrangements for hearings, sessions, deliberations, meetings, conferences, seminars, training programs, and other events. • Manage multiple concurrent hearings and events, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality services and adherence to established timelines. • Schedule and coordinate in-person, virtual, and hybrid proceedings, including test sessions. • Prepare and monitor hearing and event timelines and ensure that all required arrangements are completed on schedule. • Coordinate hearing room setup, breakout rooms, catering, interpretation, court reporting, audiovisual support, security, building access, and related logistical requirements. • Support hearings and events in Washington, D.C., as well as at external venues in other locations. Vendor and Financial Coordination • Coordinate with vendors and service providers and assist with the procurement of hearing-related services in accordance with World Bank Group policies and procedures. • Obtain, review, and compare vendor proposals and cost estimates. • Maintain vendor records and support the registration of new vendors. • Support the preparation, tracking, and reconciliation of hearing- and event-related expenditures. • Monitor purchase orders and vendor tracking tools and assist with invoice processing and payment follow-up. Planning, Tracking, and Administration • Maintain hearing calendars, scheduling tools, trackers, and planning databases. • Monitor hearing schedules and promptly communicate changes to relevant stakeholders. • Maintain accurate records of hearings, events, vendors, and service providers. Process Improvement and Systems Support • Support the implementation of new systems, digital tools, and automation initiatives for hearing administration. • Assist with testing, documenting, and improving hearing management processes and internal procedures. • Contribute to institutional projects and initiatives related to hearings, conferences, and operational effectiveness. Team Support • Share knowledge and promote consistency in hearing administration practices. • Serve as a backup to the Conference Officer as needed. • Perform other duties assigned by the Conference Officer or ICSID management.

item.title: Sr. Financial Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit www.worldbank.org . About the Global Environment Facility (GEF) The Global Environment Facility (GEF) is a multilateral financial mechanism created in 1991 to provide grant and concessional financing to recipient countries for projects and programs that address biodiversity loss, climate change mitigation, degradation of international waters, land and forests, ozone depletion, elimination or reduction of persistent organic pollutants and mercury, all within the framework of sustainable development. The GEF unites 186 countries in partnership with international institutions (18 GEF Agencies), civil society organizations (CSOs), and the private sector to address global environmental issues while supporting national sustainable development initiatives. An independently operating financial organization, GEF is the designated financial mechanism for five international environmental conventions (Conventions): the Convention on Biological Diversity, the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and Minamata Convention on Mercury. GEF is also a designated financial mechanism of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification. Since 1991, the GEF has achieved a strong track record with developing countries and countries with economies in transition, providing $27 billion and mobilizing $ 155 Bn in 2,300 active projects in over 149 countries. Over three decades, GEF and its Agencies have successfully used a wide array of non-grant instruments as concessional finance such as debt, equity, and guarantees to attract private sector investment and deliver global environmental benefits beyond business as usual. The GEF-9 Programming Directions recognized the importance of blended finance and increased the blended finance global program to 10% of GEF total Pledges (currently $390 million for the 2026-2030 period). Most importantly, over this period, the GEF will focus on mainstreaming blended finance across the GEF portfolio to achieve 25% of overall GEF resources that are invested in a manner that mobilize private capital. This focus will include expanding investments from the Blended Finance Global Program and actively reaching recipient Countries that will be incentivized to use blended finance approaches in their projects and programs. The GEF will also seek to promote multi-trust fund blended finance projects within the GEF Family of Funds (which include the Special Climate Change Fund, Least Developed Countries Fund and Global Biodiversity Framework Fund). The GEF Secretariat is a Vice-Presidential Unit (VPU) within the World Bank with approximately 100 staff. The GEF Secretariat is seeking a Senior Financial Specialist in Washington, DC to support the GEF Programming Division under the Blended Finance team. Duties and Accountabilities: The Sr. Financial Specialist will work in the GEF Blended Finance team within the GEF Programming Division and will work across geographic regions and thematic focal areas, as required. The Sr. Financial Specialist will work with Regional and Focal Area Teams on functions that require cooperation and collaboration related to the programming of Blended Finance resources. S/he will also support regional and country-level engagement with clients, Agencies and stakeholders to ensure that GEF recipient countries optimize their Blended Finance investments to achieve global environmental benefits. The Sr. Financial Specialist will also support GEF family of funds professionals reviewing blended finance projects. The Sr. Financial Specialist will work under the guidance of the Blended Finance Coordinator and will report to the Manager of the Programming Division. Specific duties include the following: • Build a pipeline of viable projects with GEF Agencies and Countries for GEF Council approval. The Sr. Financial Specialist will provide guidance to Agencies, Countries and colleagues on major issues involved in the development of blended finance project proposals and assist in overall preparation of work programs to be presented to Council. • Perform and manage reviews of project proposals under the Blended Finance Global Program and project proposals submitted by Countries in accordance with the agreed project review criteria and GEF Programming Directions. • Manage the preparation of annual reflow reporting in coordination with the GEF Trustee and GEF Agencies. The Sr. Financial Specialist will be required to review the existing processes for reflow reporting and repayment and seek to make recommendations to improve existing processes and policies. Additionally, the s/he will review GEF’s portfolio of ongoing projects through implementation, monitoring, and evaluation activities with GEF Agencies and countries. • Play an important role in developing blended finance policies and guidelines and support the overall GEF Programming Division. • Provide quality inputs to the CEO and senior management on country and thematic briefings, talking points, speeches, analytical/strategic documents. • Participate in the GEF work within the Country Engagement Strategy, including participation in country dialogues, expanded constituency workshops, and other relevant forums. As required, represent the GEF at a senior level at selected international; political, business, scientific and operational forums. • Undertake additional duties as directed by the Manager of the GEF Programming Division and, as delegated, by the Blended Finance Coordinator. Expertise and Qualifications The ideal candidate would have experience as an investment officer in a Multilateral Development Bank (MDB) or International Financial Institution (IFI) with expertise in multiple financial products including debt, guarantees, equity and blended finance. Project management skills such as reflow management and reporting will also be required. The candidate will have excellent financial skills and technical expertise in assessing financial structures. Additionally, the candidate’s strong communications skills will be evaluated since a significant part of the Senior Financial Specialist work will be to build capacity both internally and externally. The candidate needs to be familiar with the dynamics of the global environmental finance arena, including international negotiations of the Conventions, the GEF serves as financial mechanism.

item.title: Program Officer
item.description: The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . The Global Environment Facility (GEF) is a multilateral financial mechanism created in 1991 to provide grant and concessional funds to recipient countries for projects and programs that address biodiversity loss, climate change mitigation and adaptation, degradation of international waters, land and forests, ozone depletion, elimination or reduction of persistent organic pollutants and mercury, all within the framework of sustainable development. The GEF unites 186 countries in partnership with international institutions, civil society organizations (CSOs), and the private sector to address global environmental issues while supporting national sustainable development initiatives. An independently operating financial organization, GEF is the designated financial mechanism for five multilateral environmental conventions: The Convention on Biological Diversity, the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), UN Convention to Combat Desertification, and Minamata Convention on Mercury. GEF was also recently designated to serve as part of the financial mechanism of the international legally binding instrument under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ). Since 1991, the GEF has achieved a strong track record with developing countries and countries with economies in transition, providing $24.7 billion in grants for over 5,700 projects in over 170 countries. The GEF Secretariat is a Vice-Presidential Unit (VPU) within the World Bank for administrative purposes and has approximately 100 professional, administrative and client support staff. The Secretariat is seeking a Program Officer to provide comprehensive assistance in the planning, organization, and execution of Council Meetings and other meetings such as the GEF Assembly and the replenishment meetings. The role requires a professional with proven track record in international event coordination, strong diplomatic skills, and experience in high-level engagements. The incumbent will play a key role in ensuring the smooth operation of Council Meetings, supporting both technical and political aspects, and maintaining high standards of organization and detail. The selected Program Officer will report to the Secretary to the GEF Council. Objective The Program Officer will provide strategic and operational leadership to the GEF Events Team, ensuring the delivery of high-quality, impactful events that meet institutional standards and effectively serve GEF's diverse stakeholder community. The role also carries a strong team development mandate, with responsibility for building both the technical and interpersonal capabilities of team members. Scope of Work The Program Officer will be responsible for the following: Events Team Coordination • Coordinate and supervise the events team in end-to-end planning, logistics, and execution of GEF international events (efficient per diem delivery, venue selection, contracting, Purchase Orders, travel logistics, interpretation, audio-visual services, travel for sponsored participants, among others). • Develop and coordinate travel guideless in line with World Bank’s policy, event budgets, timelines, work plans and roles and responsibilities of each team member, ensuring delivery within scope and on schedule. • Develop contingency plans and coordinate operations, including troubleshooting unforeseen issues in real time. • Develop post-event evaluations and produce lessons-learned reports to continuously improve event quality. • Back-fill members from the events team as needed. Team Leadership and Development • Coordinate and mentor the GEF Events Team, providing day-to-day guidance, workload coordination, and performance oversight. • Conduct regular one-on-one check-ins and team meetings to foster a collaborative, high-performing work culture. • Identify training needs and facilitate access to relevant learning opportunities for team members. • Set clear performance expectations and provide constructive feedback. Strategic and Institutional Contribution • Advise on event strategy, format innovation, and best practices in international event coordination. • Contribute to the development of standard operating procedures and events coordination guidelines. Note: This internal requisition is open to WBG and IMF staff only (including short-term and extended term consultants/ temporaries). External candidates are requested not to apply. In case an external candidate applies, their application will not be considered.

The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. Visit www.worldbank.org . About the Global Environment Facility (GEF) The Global Environment Facility (GEF) is a multilateral financial mechanism created in 1991 to provide grant and concessional funds to recipient countries for projects and programs that address biodiversity loss, climate change mitigation and adaptation, degradation of international waters, land and forests, ozone depletion, elimination or reduction of persistent organic pollutants and mercury, all within the framework of sustainable development. The GEF unites 186 countries in partnership with international institutions, civil society organizations (CSOs), and the private sector to address global environmental issues while supporting national sustainable development initiatives. An independently operating financial organization, GEF is the designated financial mechanism for five international environmental conventions: the Convention on Biological Diversity, the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and Minamata Convention on Mercury. GEF is also a designated financial mechanism of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification. The GEF Secretariat is a Vice-Presidential Unit (VPU) within the World Bank for administrative purposes and has approximately 100 professional, administrative and client support staff. The Secretariat has established an Integration and Knowledge Division (IKD) to strengthen and harness the integrated approach programming for tackling major drivers of global environmental degradation. A key focus of the integrated approach programs is to influence transformative changes in systems that drive such degradation. This includes natural, food, urban, health, and energy systems. The Secretariat is seeking a Senior Environmental Specialist to lead and coordinate thematic work on systems transformation through the integrated approach programs, focusing on all aspects of circular economy in the context of tackling drivers with links to the GEF focal areas. The successful individual will serve as Theme Lead reporting directly to the Manager of Integration and Knowledge and work closely with staff across divisions to ensure that circularity and systems thinking are embedded in GEF Programming focused on tackling drivers of global environmental degradation. Duties and Accountabilities: Under the supervision of the Manager for Integration and Knowledge, the position has the following specific responsibilities: • Lead and support programming and portfolio management on embedding circularity in targeted systems and sectoral supply chains, including guidance to GEF implementing and Executing Agencies and country counterparts on options and approaches to advance integrated solutions. • Lead the development of appropriate indicators for circular economy and systems change as they relate to the GEF core indicator targets and results monitoring framework. • Provide guidance on circular economy and integrated solutions to GEF Agencies and countries for development of GEF project proposals and programmatic approaches and for monitoring the project implementation performance. • Lead the development of impactful knowledge products to advance circularity and systems change, including documentation of best practices and lessons and contribute to the preparation of appropriate GEF policies and guidelines on integrated programming. • In coordination with the Conventions and Program Divisions, follow relevant global discourse on circular economy and support outreach to developing countries as needed. • Establish and maintain a productive dialogue with the GEF Agencies and Countries and key stakeholders, including key private sector initiatives and platforms, to leverage opportunities for GEF integrated programs. • Lead and promote regular and informed communication about GEF investments in circular economy practices. • As required, represent the GEF at a senior level at selected international political, scientific, and operational forums. • Provide quality inputs to the CEO and senior management on country and thematic briefings, talking points, speeches, analytical/strategic documents. • Undertake additional duties as required by GEF Secretariat Management, including participation in Knowledge Management, Results Based Management, Monitoring, and other related operational activities.

item.title: Senior Transport Specialist – Logistics
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org . Infrastructure Vertical The WBG Infrastructure Vertical provides public and private solutions to operational teams and clients across the WBG to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs by: (i) supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, (ii) policy environment, and (iii) enabling and mobilizing private sector capital. With 60 years of experience, the WBG is poised to support the sector becoming an engine of growth and jobs through improving policies and governance, foundational infrastructure and private sector investments. WBG lending in the sector is expected to grow substantially. The Infrastructure VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure Transport and Logistics Department Within the Infrastructure VPU, the WBG Transport and Logistics Department seeks to connect people to jobs, social services and income-generating opportunities, as well as to move goods between local, regional, and international markets, using cleaner, safer, more equitable and more resilient transport solutions, with a particular focus on private capital mobilization. The Department is composed of 3 units: (1) Policy and Regulations; (2) Solutions and Impact; and (3) Transport Trust Funds. The Senior Transport-Logistics Specialist will serve as the senior logistics lead and report to the Manager, Transport and Logistics, Policy and Regulations. The role will provide thought leadership on logistics; lead the development of high-quality knowledge products and advisory services; support regional teams across the World Bank Group in designing and implementing logistics policies, regulations, and solutions; and contribute actively to the Knowledge and Solutions Groups for Logistics, Maritime Transport and Ports. The Specialist will also advance private sector participation and private capital mobilization in logistics and supply chain management in the related transport sub-sectors (Ports, Railways, Trucking and Intermodal freight) by assessing and advising business cases and feasibility studies. The Specialist will be recognized as a go-to expert on cutting-edge developments in Logistics and Supply Chain Management, both on the public policy and private sector sides. Key responsibilities: Strategic Leadership and Flagship Research: • Serve as the World Bank Group’s senior technical lead on logistics and supply chain development, providing strategic guidance across freight transport, logistics infrastructure and services, trade facilitation, multimodal transport, and supply chain resilience. • Identify emerging and key challenges and opportunities and shape the WBG’s logistics agenda through high-quality analytics, policy advice, operational solutions, and innovative financing approaches. • Lead the development of policy, regulatory, institutional, and investment frameworks to improve logistics performance, competitiveness, sustainability, and private sector participation. • Develop and maintain practical policy and regulatory solutions that regional teams can adapt to country and sector contexts, working closely with relevant Global Leads and regional teams. • Define annual strategic priorities and implementation plans for the logistics agenda and report on progress to KIT management. • Lead analytical work on emerging trends in logistics and supply chain development and support the formulation of policy, regulatory, institutional, and investment frameworks that improve logistics competitiveness and economic growth. Operational Support and Private Sector Solutions: • Provide senior technical and quality assurance support to IFC/IBRD/MIGA regional teams across the project cycle (from upstream support on fundamental design issues to help extract lessons during the completion process), ensuring that operations and advisory engagements reflect global knowledge, sound technical judgment, and international good practice. • Ensuring that the most relevant and up-to-date global knowledge informs the design and implementation of country engagements and helps resolve technical disagreements • Advise on the planning, development, modernization, and optimization of logistics systems and infrastructure, including corridors, logistics parks and hubs, dry ports, intermodal terminals, distribution centers, free trade zones, and special economic zones. • Assess logistics business models and investment opportunities across areas such as contract logistics, freight forwarding, trucking, rail freight, maritime logistics, e-commerce and last-mile delivery, cold chain, warehousing, and multimodal supply chains. • Evaluate logistics network and growth strategies, including market demand, location and network design, fleet and warehousing requirements, operating models, technology deployment, and strategic partnerships. • Support the assessment of commercial viability, private sector participation, and private capital mobilization opportunities in logistics and related freight sectors. • Promote more efficient and sustainable logistics through digitalization, modal shift, fleet modernization and electrification, alternative fuels, and other decarbonization solutions. Technical Leadership in Logistics and Supply Chain Solutions: • Serve as the World Bank Group's lead technical expert on logistics systems and supply chain development, covering freight transport, warehousing, distribution networks, logistics infrastructure, trade facilitation, multimodal transport, and logistics services. • Lead analytical, advisory, and operational support related to the planning, development, modernization, and optimization of logistics ecosystems, including logistics corridors, logistics parks, inland logistics hubs, freight villages, dry ports, intermodal terminals, free trade zones, special economic zones, and distribution centers. Also including strategies to attract logistics operators, manufacturers, distributors, e-commerce companies, and other private sector participants. • Evaluate the growth and expansion strategies of logistics service providers by assessing geographic expansion opportunities, freight demand, customer requirements, fleet needs, warehousing requirements, network optimization opportunities, and modal alternatives. • Lead technical assessments of logistics business models across a broad range of sectors, including e-commerce fulfillment, last-mile delivery, parcel and express logistics, contract logistics, cold-chain logistics, freight forwarding, trucking operations, rail freight, maritime logistics, and integrated multimodal supply chains. • Assess clients’ proposals on logistics network design, including hub location strategies, warehouse footprints, fleet composition, service coverage, operating models, technology deployment, and partnerships with transport operators, infrastructure providers, customers, suppliers, and other strategic stakeholders. • Assess opportunities to improve logistics efficiency and sustainability through digitalization, supply chain optimization, modal shift, fleet modernization, electrification, low-carbon transport solutions, alternative fuels, and other decarbonization measures. Knowledge, Learning and Mentoring: • Lead flagship analytical and knowledge work on emerging trends and innovations in logistics and supply chain management, translating global experience into actionable solutions for clients and operational teams. • Capture and disseminate lessons from WBG operations and convene the Logistics Knowledge and Solutions Group to facilitate exchange across regions and identify emerging issues. • Assess gaps in technical skills based on business needs, and work with the KTI Management Team to internally develop these skills through formal or on-the-job training and through developing a solutions-focused learning curriculum • Support technical staff in deepening their expertise • Regularly convene staff affiliated with the Knowledge and Solutions Group for Logistics to discuss emerging issues, share experiences across regions, and identify issues for management attention, ensuring balanced participation of field-based staff along with those based in HQ • Convene field-based friendly training and dissemination events to ensure that best practice experiences are widely known and discussed within the World Bank Group • Identify and promote opportunities for South-South and North-South peer exchange among clients facing similar development challenges • Develop and deliver learning initiatives covering logistics policy, logistics infrastructure, supply chain management, freight transport, logistics technologies, free trade zones, multimodal logistics, and sustainable freight solutions. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org E urope and Central Asia (ECA) Region: The Europe and Central Asia (ECA) region comprises 30 extremely diverse, predominantly middle-income countries, with a population of nearly 500 million people. ECA countries face structural and legacy issues, including an incomplete transition to a market economy and declining productivity, weak institutional capacity, dependence on fossil fuels, limited physical and digital connectivity and, in many instances, aging populations. Recent shocks (COVID-19, Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, weather shocks and natural disaster) have further exacerbated these challenges, with significant impacts on the level, inclusiveness and sustainability of growth and overall living standards. The World Bank Group is working closely with client countries in the region to address these issues, with increasing focus on productivity growth and job creation, energy security and water management, human capital and economic inclusion, and physical and digital connectivity. The region has a strong lending pipeline and a large portfolio of projects spanning a number of sectors. In addition, knowledge is critical to the Bank’s value proposition to client countries in the ECA region. https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/eca Background and Context The World Bank’s Health, Nutrition and Population (HNP) Global Practice in the Europe and Central Asia (ECA) Region is supporting Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) in advancing health system reforms focused on financial sustainability, service delivery performance, quality of care, and resilience, in line with Universal Health Coverage (UHC) objectives. The ETC will support implementation and preparation of World Bank–financed activities in BiH, with two anchor engagements: • MDTF: “Technical Support for BiH Health Reform” (P180862) Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA), providing analytical, technical assistance, and implementation support for health sector reforms; and • Health Systems Improvement Project (HSIP, P171150), including Additional Financing, supporting investments and reforms in health financing, service delivery, digital health, and system performance. The ETC will contribute to our operational engagement in the health sector and act as a focal point between the World Bank and relevant stakeholders, at state, entity and cantonal levels, and development partners to ensure strong analytical underpinnings, smooth implementation support, and effective policy dialogue. Duties and Responsibilities: The ETC will be based in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina and report to the HNP Practice Manager and will be responsible for the following tasks and duties: • Provide day to day implementation support for ongoing projects, including health financing, strategic purchasing, service delivery reforms, digital health, and quality improvement. • Contribute to implementation support missions, preparation of Aide Memoires, management updates, and follow up on agreed actions. • Support preparation or restructuring of project documentation (Project papers, results frameworks, indicators, and progress reporting). • Assist in monitoring results, identifying implementation bottlenecks, and proposing corrective actions. • Contribute to design, preparation, and delivery of analytical and advisory activities. • Support preparation of policy notes, technical briefs, diagnostic studies, and just in time analysis on health financing, pharmaceuticals, service delivery performance, provider payment mechanisms, and system efficiency. • Compile, validate, and analyze quantitative and qualitative data from administrative sources, household surveys, and international benchmarks. • Ensure analytical outputs are policy relevant, well structured, and aligned with ongoing reforms and lending operations. • Support ongoing policy dialogue with Ministries of Health, Health Insurance Funds, Ministries of Finance, and other relevant institutions at state, entity, and cantonal levels. • Assist in organizing consultations, workshops, and technical discussions with civil society, professional associations, and donor partners, as relevant. • Contribute to communication materials, presentations, and briefing notes for senior government officials and World Bank management. • Support knowledge sharing across BiH, Western Balkans, and ECA, drawing on regional and global experience. • Monitor sector developments and reforms, keep teams informed of emerging risks and opportunities. • Undertake additional tasks related to the BiH health portfolio or beyond as requested.
