item.title: ETC DRF - Insurance and Modeling Expert
item.description: Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty on a livable planet, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . Prosperity Vice Presidency The WBG Prosperity Vice Presidency is responsible for getting the right public and private sector solutions to our operational teams and to our clients, and to produce scalable impact. It l eads the WBG’s key global engagements in support of: Growth and jobs (including supporting teams across the WBG on the jobs agenda); debt sustainability and debt management; improved domestic resource mobilization and expenditure efficiency; a resilient and inclusive financial sector; business-enabling policies and regulations; trade policy and facilitation; and transparent, effective, and accountable government institutions world-wide. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission. Financial Services Sector (FSS) I Department The FSS Global Department is comprised of two directorates: FSS I covers financial resilience and integrity, financial inclusion, capital market development and disaster risk finance, while FSS II covers SME finance, Banking, Housing, Leasing and Insurance, as well as Sustainable Finance. Disaster Risk Finance Unit The Disaster Risk Finance (DRF) team in FSS1 helps client governments strengthen financial resilience to disaster shocks. Through the Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program (DRFIP), the team delivers technical assistance, analytical work, and advisory support, drawing on the World Bank’s crisis preparedness and response toolkit and other financial instruments. It works closely with regional and country teams, government counterparts, private sector, development partners to design and implement solutions tailored to each country’s risk profile and institutional context. The DRF team also contributes to global efforts to close insurance protection gaps, including through engagement with the G7, G20, the International Association of Insurance Supervisors, and the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), among others. Against this background, the DRF team seeks an Extended Term Consultant (ETC) to provide senior-level technical advice and engagement support for the Unit’s work program on DRFI, insurance market development, and risk modeling. The position is based in Sydney, Australia and requires frequent travel. Duties and Responsibilities The ETC will be responsible for the following, mainly covering the Pacific regional program, while s/he is expected to also support other regional engagements as the needs arise. • Lead the delivery of disaster risk finance instruments and mechanisms, including sovereign risk transfer products such as parametric insurance, catastrophe bonds, and risk pooling arrangements, as well as contingent financing facilities, disaster reserve funds, and risk-based public financial management frameworks. • Provide ad hoc actuarial and quantitative analysis to support client engagement, policy dialogue, and internal decision-making, including identifying options to strengthen financial protection across risk layers undertaking value for money analysis. • Review and quality-assure technical outputs prepared by others, including diagnostic reports, strategy documents, financial models, and presentations. • Curate and share knowledge on insurance market development, including key bottlenecks, global trends, insurance technology, the integration of insurance into climate risk management, relevant case studies, and financial innovations for client countries. This may include co-authoring policy and research notes, preparing internal guidance, developing policy and industry toolkits, and organizing seminars and workshops. • Collaborate with internal stakeholders such as IFC, MIGA, Treasury, and external stakeholders, including the Insurance Development Forum (IDF). • Represent the CDRFI team in stakeholder consultations, interagency coordination forums, workshops, and donor dialogues, as needed. • Perform other duties and tasks assigned by the Unit Manager.

item.title: E T Consultant- Geospatial Data Scientist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org . Infrastructure Vertical The WBG Infrastructure Vertical provides public and private solutions to operational teams and clients across the WBG to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs by: (i) supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, (ii) policy environment, and (iii) enabling and mobilizing private sector capital. With 60 years of experience, the WBG is poised to support the sector becoming an engine of growth and jobs through improving policies and governance, foundational infrastructure and private sector investments. The WBG lending in the sector is expected to grow substantially. The Infrastructure VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure Disaster Management, Solutions Impact Unit (KIUSD) supports low and middle-income countries to understand, manage, and reduce their risks from natural hazards and climate change. Within KIUSD, the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) umbrella trust fund is a global partnership that helps low- and middle-income countries better understand and reduce their vulnerability to natural hazards and climate change. GFDRR supports analytics and technical assistance to the most vulnerable countries and communities where it will have the greatest positive impact. As a donor-funded program, GFDRR consults regularly with donors and actively strives to maintain and develop new partnerships for increased impact. For more information: https://www.gfdrr.org/en Global Program on Nature-Based Solutions for Climate Resilience Housed within IDURM is the Global Program on Nature-Based Solutions for Climate Resilience. The Global Program has the objective to increasing investment in Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) for addressing climate resilience challenges across the World Bank portfolio. The Program aims to achieve the objective through the development of targeted knowledge, tools and operational support modalities for task teams and their government clients. The Program helps task teams and their counterparts at national and city level to identify, prepare, implement and finance NBS for climate resilience purposes as stand-alone interventions or as part of wider investment, policy and analytical engagements. The Program furthermore uses its position as a Global Program to support the development and transfer of knowledge on NBS within and outside the World Bank Group. In its objectives and approach, the Program is aligned with World Bank strategies including the Climate Change Action Plan 2021-2025 and the Green, Resilient and Inclusive Development (GRID) approach. The Program is structured along three pillars: Operations, Knowledge and Partnerships. Pillar 1: Operations Under this Pillar, the Program supports World Bank Task Teams and their Government counterparts in the identification, operational assessment, implementation and financing of NBS for Climate Resilience. The Program hosts a core team of technical experts, a curated pool of firms and consultants and key operational tools to assist in the mainstreaming of NBS for Climate Resilience across Global Practices. Pillar 2: Knowledge This Pillar strengthens the Bank’s knowledge position on NBS and aims to make the Global Program a hub for NBS knowledge both internally and externally, with a focus on climate resilience at urban, coastal and river basin level. Activities include developing and consolidating knowledge products and tools; training staff and clients in preparing and implementing NBS ensuring best practices are integrated into operations; and publishing operational reports and externally facing peer-reviewed articles. All knowledge products developed to date are available on the Program’s website. Pillar 3: Partnerships Under the Partnerships pillar, the Program strengthens internal and external partnerships needed to advance NBS in the World Bank portfolio. Internally, this includes relationships with other teams across the World Bank Group, including with other Global Practices as well as with IFC. Externally, partnerships are established with key knowledge and implementation partners, donors and co-financiers, in close coordination with GFDRR donors and partnership teams. Please note this position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. Job Duties and Responsibilities The E T Consultant’s will support implementation of GPNBS, with a focus on the development and application of geospatial (and other quantitative) tools such as the NBS Opportunity Scan. Tasks include further development and automation of the urban, catchment and coastal NBS Opportunity Scans, supporting the delivery of country-level technical assistance applying the NBS Opportunity Scans, further development of cost-benefit analysis tools and their in-country application. The E T consultant will also be expected to contribute or lead knowledge products related to climate risk and NBS and support the other Pillars of the program where relevant. Additionally, the ET consultant will work on the harmonization and integration of geospatial and quantitative tools across the global disaster risk management units, including those focusing on disaster risk analytics, urban resilience and earth observation. The E T Consultant will work closely with the Task Team Leaders and core staff of the Global Program, under managerial supervision of the Practice Manager of KIUSD. Specific responsibilities and duties will include (but not be limited to) the following: • Take a leading role in the development and application of geospatial and other quantitative tools of GPNBS, including the NBSOS and BIOME. • Supporting, curating, and developing EO-data applications for longer term monitoring of NBS investments, by monitoring ecological indicators and natural capital. • Liaising with key partners inside and outside the World Bank that are managing/developing geospatial tools, EO-data, Geo-AI, VGI and other geographic information relevant to NBS, such as ESA, NASA, and many others. • With the wider NBS team, take up the role as a technical advisor supporting World Bank Task Teams on how to make effective use of EO-data and geospatial analytics when preparing, designing and implementing NBS operations. • Advance collaboration and integration of geospatial and quantitative analytics tools on risk management and resilience in KIUSD and other teams in the global urban and disaster risk management department. • Lead and/or contribute to knowledge products related to NBS analytics developed under the Knowledge pillar of the Program. • Illustrate Program advancements and contributions in the form of blogs, peer-reviewed papers, conference contributions, etc. • Contribute to programmatic outputs including results monitoring, reporting, budgeting, and branding • Deliver presentations and workshops at a variety of settings, including with Task Teams, government counterparts and at internal and external events

item.title: Investment Analyst – PPP Transaction Advisory Services
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit: https://www.ifc.org IFC’s Transaction Advisory Services department provides financial advisory services to client governments and private companies with the purpose to increase access to basic infrastructure and social services by facilitating private investments in various sectors. Specifically, the PPP team acts as transaction advisor to governments to structure and implement the following types of public-private partnership (PPP) projects: • BOT type concessions • Management and lease contracts • Restructuring and privatization of state-owned enterprises By structuring successful PPPs, infrastructure and public services may be expanded and improved in a cost-effective manner, benefiting from private sector’s expertise, management, and finance. The PPP team has an active global portfolio of over 100 PPP projects covering different sectors, of which power, transport, water, affordable housing and health are strategic priorities. IFC’s Transaction Advisory Services department also acts as transaction adviser to private companies to help them with various types of merger and acquisition type of transactions. The Corporate Finance Services (CFS) team has an active portfolio of transactions in various sectors, of which renewable energy and privatization are strategic priorities. CTA’s Europe PPP team covers the unit’s operations across the Europe Region. The team’s 11 staff are located across 6 different European offices, including in Kyiv, Ukraine. The department is looking to recruit an Investment Analyst (IA) to work with the PPP team in the Europe region. The IA will be based in Kyiv, Ukraine reporting to the Regional Manager and Head for PPP Transaction Advisory Services in Europe. The IA will support the development and implementation of various PPP and CFS projects in Ukraine and the broader Europe region in infrastructure sectors as described above. The selected candidate will be expected to perform as a core team member under the supervision of the Hub-Leader for Ukraine and Moldova and will assist the project team leaders in the origination and execution of IFC’s advisory mandates in PPPs, privatizations and private M A transactions. Duties and Accountabilities: Duties include, but are not limited to: 1. Proactively contribute to business development activities, including: • Participate in origination and marketing activities, e.g. undertake project scoping to assess feasibility of potential projects, preparation of pitchbooks and proposals and support with IFC internal governance processes. • Prepare notes and documentation for internal approval processes and procurement of consultants. • Participate in meetings with government and private clients to discuss and assess their needs and ideas to improve access to infrastructure and delivery of public services and to identify potential PPP and CFS projects for IFC transaction advisory assistance. • Understand World Bank Group’s (WBG) strategy for assigned countries and work with them to engage with clients to implement them in a coordinated manner. 2. Assist with day-to-day management of project execution to contribute to the structuring of innovative PPP and CFS projects and to the development of recommendations to clients, including: • Assist with due diligence management, data collection, review of legal, commercial and technical outputs, project structure design, and drafting of project contractual documentation. • Prepare complex financial models and perform financial analysis. • Assist with managing project marketing to potential investors, roadshows, preparing marketing documents (teaser, information memorandum), conducting prequalification and tendering (including negotiation of project agreements with bidders) up to award and commercial/financial close. • Assist with coordinating with other parts of IFC and WBG including environmental and social, legal, other advisory and investment departments as well as IBRD colleagues.

item.title: Investment Analyst, Infrastructure, Mexico
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. Infrastructure is one of IFC's strategic priorities. IFC's Infrastructure department supports the World Bank Group's aim of improving access to efficient, reliable, and affordable infrastructure for the poor in emerging markets. The team is responsible for originating and managing IFC's investment activities in the following sectors: Power Generation, Distribution and Transmission, Mining, Transport logistics, Telecommunications, Water, Waste, Privatized Public Services and other Subnational/Cities financing. IFC's focus in the sector is on: (i) increasing access to basic infrastructure services; (ii) supporting local companies while improving transparency and corporate governance; (iii) exploring new equity and debt investment opportunities and catalyzing foreign direct investments, including co-investments and mobilizing syndicated and parallel loans; (iv) introducing and developing new financial products including through Public-Private Partnerships; and (v) building long-term partnerships with strong global and regional players. The Latin America and the Caribbean Infrastructure Unit, an open and dynamic unit involved in the origination, structuring, and supervision of IFC's infrastructure investments in the region, is seeking an Investment Analyst to join our team. The appointee will be stationed in Mexico City, Mexico, reporting to IFC’s Regional Lead for the Infrastructure team in Colombia Central America and to the LAC1 Infrastructure Regional Industry Manager. Duties and Accountabilities: Specific responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Business Development: • Support in the sourcing and assessment of new opportunities; identifying bankable projects, anticipating market trends, and employing sector/country knowledge; synthesizing information into internal reports for decision-making purposes. • Create and analyze financial models; demonstrated corporate and project finance modeling experience will be a plus. • Participate in and support the structuring of new transactions. • Review and analyze historical and projected financial statements. • Conduct industry, integrity (KYC), and market research (including pricing benchmarks) and assist in IFC's business development efforts. • Elaborate pitchbooks and proposals for clients. • Review company information and prepare reports on periodic financial statements, project progress reports, and other information submitted by clients. • Prepare documentation for IFC internal processes. • Participating in and providing analytical support in investment negotiations. • Participate in the active monitoring of investments in portfolio companies, including monitoring of compliance with IFC financial, environmental, insurance, and legal requirements. • Monitor a portfolio of existing assets and prepare high quality reports identifying any potential risks, issues and mitigants.

item.title: E T Consultant (Associate Data Engineer)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) delivers digital support for global and country-specific products, supports systems aligned with the new Country Engagement model,and provides geospatial solutions for geo-tagging of projects to improve spatial visibility and impact tracking. It also drives the delivery of AI-powered business solutions to support business priorities and accelerate data-driven decision-making across the institution. The Associate Data and AI Engineer plays a critical role in the delivery of geospatial solutions and capabilities, supporting high-impact technology initiatives that serve a broad World Bank Group operational user base. To support this effort, ITSCE seeks an experienced data professional to join the Geospatial Solutions team. The position is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining scalable data pipelines that ingest, transform, validate, and publish geospatial and non-geospatial data from a wide range of internal and external sources. The role requires strong expertise in data engineering, geospatial data management, ETL/ELT frameworks, data quality assurance, and data integration practices to ensure trusted, discoverable, and reusable datasets across the platform ecosystem. Within ITSCE, the Data Engineer will support the delivery of the unit’s work program by building and optimizing data infrastructure that powers geospatial products, analytics, and operational decision-making. Working with limited supervision, the incumbent will develop and maintain automated data pipelines, streamline data acquisition processes, implement data validation and quality controls, and improve the reliability, performance, and scalability of geospatial data services. The role will collaborate closely with business stakeholders, GIS specialists, product managers, and technology teams to gather and translate data requirements into sustainable engineering solutions. Specific Responsibilities • Analyze and conduct validation and cleansing processes, ensuring the integrity and quality of geospatial and non‑geospatial data (including spatial attributes, coordinates, projections, and metadata). • Optimize the implementation of automated testing and monitoring solutions to proactively identify and resolve data quality issues, including spatial data quality checks (e.g., geometry validity, missing coordinates, topology consistency, schema drift). • Optimize data pipelines to efficiently gather, process, and store large datasets, including spatial datasets required for platform and digital twin capabilities (e.g., feature services, geo‑tagging datasets, reference layers). • Maintain the data infrastructure and data platforms, addressing issues promptly to reduce downtime and ensure reliable availability of geospatial data products and services. • Participate in agile ceremonies to align data engineering efforts with project goals. • Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, GIS specialists, and product owners to understand data requirements and deliver solutions that drive business value, including translating operational needs into geospatial data models and integration requirements. • Analyze and maintain comprehensive documentation for data processes, pipelines, and systems to facilitate knowledge sharing and compliance.

item.title: Policy Analyst
item.description: CITY is looking for an experienced, dynamic and motivated Policy Analyst to contribute to the division’s work, with specific knowledge and expertise on local environmental policy, notably concerning water and sanitation, blue and circular economy, and nature-based solutions. The selected candidate will report to Head of the Water Governance, Blue and Circular Economy Unit. Main Responsibilities Research, analysis and drafting Design and conduct innovative economic and/or policy research on challenges and opportunities related to local environmental policy at local, national and global scales. Analyse international evidence and data to inform policy analysis on the division’s topics in OECD member countries and beyond. Build and maintain databases and conduct empirical analysis as needed. Draft and edit high-quality, evidence-based assessments and tailored recommendations in policy and working papers, publications, reports, and other outputs including blogs and seminar proceedings. Organise and summarise complex materials in a clear manner for specialist and non-specialist audiences, and develop briefing materials as needed for Directors and the Office of the Secretary General . Keep abreast of new research, exploratory work and policies on local environmental policy, emanating from governments, other international organisations, non-governmental organisations, academia and the private sector. Project management and fundraising Contribute to the management of projects, including ensuring timely delivery of quality outputs. Actively support the Division’s and Unit’s fundraising efforts, including through developing and drafting project proposals and strengthening networks and engagement with potential donors as required. Supervise the work of interns, external and internal consultants, and junior staff as needed. Co-ordination, representation and liaison Support the organisation of the OECD Working Party on Urban Policy, the OECD Water Governance Initiative and networks of government officials and practitioners, as well as project-related meetings and events, such as seminars, roundtables and workshops, as needed. Establish and maintain contacts with representatives in relevant ministries and government agencies, as well as intergovernmental organisations and relevant stakeholders. Represent the OECD Secretariat at international conferences and contribute to raising the profile of, and disseminating, CITY and CFE work at local, national and international levels. Collaborate with other Divisions and Directorates and contribute to horizontal and multidisciplinary projects and outputs as needed. Other duties Provide general support to the activities of the Division as required. Carry out other tasks as assigned, in particular as requested by the Head of Division and the Director’s office.

item.title: Senior Outcomes Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . The Delivery Unit translates corporate priorities and outcome commitments into management routines that support implementation, problem-solving, accountability, and course correction. Its work connects targets, portfolio intelligence, operational evidence, delivery constraints, and leadership decisions. Core instruments include sector and regional stocktakes, target monitoring, delivery analytics, and AI-enabled tools that help teams move from storing data to steering performance. The Senior Economist / Senior Outcomes Specialist will lead major elements of this agenda. The position will devote approximately 50 percent of time to sector-focused stocktakes, 30 percent to managing the substantive work of the High-Level Council on Jobs, and 20 percent to the development, testing, evaluation, and research of AI-enabled outcomes tools. The role requires a combination of development economics, delivery-unit practice, advanced quantitative analysis, technology and product fluency, behavioral science, and senior stakeholder management. Duties and Accountabilities 1. Lead sector-focused stocktakes and delivery reviews (approximately 50 percent) • Design and manage a systematic program of sector-focused stocktakes that enables senior management to assess whether strategies, portfolios, and implementation pathways are on track to deliver agreed outcomes. • Establish the analytical architecture for each stocktake, including outcome questions, indicators, targets, baselines, benchmarks, portfolio cuts, trajectories, scenarios, and evidence standards. • Integrate operational, financial, portfolio, country, sector, evaluative, and external data to identify performance trends, delivery gaps, implementation bottlenecks, concentration risks, and opportunities to improve impact, scale, additionality, and value for money. • Apply delivery-unit methods to convert evidence into a small number of management choices, agreed actions, accountable owners, milestones, escalation points, and follow-up routines; track whether actions are implemented and whether they change performance. • Diagnose the institutional and behavioral drivers of delivery, including incentives, decision rights, coordination failures, attention constraints, risk perceptions, cognitive biases, and the routines that shape day-to-day implementation choices. • Facilitate structured problem-solving sessions with sector, regional, country, IFC, MIGA, and corporate counterparts; challenge assumptions constructively and build ownership of corrective action. • Prepare concise, decision-oriented briefs, dashboards, presentations, speaking points, decision records, and action trackers for senior management reviews. • Strengthen the stocktake methodology and its links to sector strategies, country programs, the WBG Scorecard, corporate outcome targets, Target Map, results narratives, and other institutional performance systems. • Synthesize cross-sector and cross-regional findings into operational guidance, management recommendations, and reusable institutional knowledge. 2. Deliver advanced economic, quantitative, and portfolio analytics • Apply economic, econometric, statistical, and mixed-methods analysis to understand the drivers of outcomes and distinguish implementation constraints from design, measurement, or reporting issues. • Develop and interpret benchmarks, progress-to-maturity curves, forecasts, counterfactuals where feasible, scenarios, sensitivity analyses, and risk models that enable management to judge whether delivery is on track. • Use reproducible analytical workflows to clean, link, validate, and analyze large administrative and operational datasets; document assumptions, uncertainty, limitations, and data-quality risks transparently. • Translate complex quantitative findings into clear operational implications and targeted actions for non-technical decision-makers. 3. Manage the High-Level Council on Jobs (approximately 30 percent) • Manage the Council's work program, translating strategic direction from the Chair, WBG leadership, and members into a focused analytical agenda, sequenced deliverables, and disciplined follow-through. • Coordinate substantive engagement with Council members and their offices, including consultations, agenda development, briefings, meeting preparation, records of discussion, action tracking, and implementation follow-up. • Lead preparation of analytical notes, evidence syntheses, policy options, presentations, speeches, and knowledge products on the quantity and quality of jobs and the pathways through which development interventions support them. • Connect the Council's work to WBG country and sector strategies, private-sector development, the More and Better-Paid Jobs framework, jobs measurement, corporate targets, and operational delivery. • Coordinate contributions across WBG units and external partners, reconcile different institutional perspectives, surface unresolved choices, and sustain momentum between high-level engagements. • Use behavioral insights to strengthen coalition-building, framing, uptake, and follow-through, recognizing how incentives, norms, identity, trust, and decision context influence collective action. 4. Advance AI-enabled outcomes tools, evaluation, and research (approximately 20 percent) • Support the end-to-end product cycle for AI-enabled outcomes and delivery tools: problem definition, user research, requirements, data and model design, prototyping, testing, evaluation, deployment, adoption, monitoring, and iteration. • Translate operational workflows into well-defined use cases, user stories, technical specifications, evaluation questions, acceptance criteria, and prioritized product backlogs. • Design and conduct structured user testing and product analytics with operational teams and decision-makers, assessing accuracy, usability, relevance, decision usefulness, trust, adoption, workflow integration, equity, and scalability. • Contribute to rigorous validation and evaluation, including benchmark datasets, error analysis, human-in-the-loop protocols, experiments or quasi-experimental approaches where appropriate, and comparisons against existing practice. • Apply behavioral science to product design and adoption by testing how defaults, salience, feedback, friction, choice architecture, and social norms affect use and decision quality. • Work with economists, data scientists, software and product teams, evaluators, operational specialists, and academic partners to refine methods and translate research into usable tools. • Ensure appropriate human oversight and transparency concerning data provenance, uncertainty, limitations, privacy, security, fairness, bias, and responsible AI risks. 5. Strengthen institutional learning and partnerships • Build strong working relationships across Global Practices, Regions, IFC, MIGA, OPCS, IEG, ITS, DEC, the Department for Outcomes, and external partners. • Develop methodological notes, case studies, evaluation products, executive briefs, and operational learning materials connecting stocktake findings, delivery practice, the jobs agenda, behavioral insights, and AI-enabled analytics. • Represent the work in technical discussions and selected senior-level engagements, exercising sound judgment and escalating strategic, political, reputational, data, technology, and quality risks as appropriate. Reporting and Working Relationships • The Senior Economist / Senior Outcomes Specialist will report to the Manager, Delivery, Department for Outcomes, or another designated manager within the Department. • The role will work closely with sector and regional leadership, country teams, IFC and MIGA counterparts, corporate units, jobs specialists, economists, behavioral scientists, data scientists, engineers, product teams, evaluators, and external partners. • The position requires a high degree of autonomy, discretion, responsiveness, and quality control in work prepared for WBG senior management and high-level external stakeholders.

item.title: Manager, Talent and Career Development
item.description: At the World Bank Group (WBG), your work shapes the future. With 189 member countries and a mission to end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity, WBG is one of the world’s most impactful development organizations. We rely on the strength of our people: broad representation, driven, and determined to deliver knowledge and results globally. The WBG Talent Management and Development Department, a core function within Human Resources, shapes the World Bank Group's talent strategy, building the workforce and leadership capabilities needed to deliver its mission. Through innovative talent solutions and programs, it enables performance, career growth, leadership development, and organizational effectiveness. The Manager, Talent and Career Development leads the strategy, governance, and delivery of the World Bank Group’s enterprise talent and career development agenda. The role oversees performance management, talent and succession reviews, promotions, career development, and internal mobility, ensuring these practices are integrated, fair, data-driven, and aligned with business priorities. Working closely with senior leaders, HR Business Partners, and other Centers of Excellence, the Manager will strengthen leadership pipelines, improve workforce capabilities, and enable employees to grow and contribute to their highest potential. This is an opportunity to shape enterprise talent and career practices across a complex, global institution and to build an integrated approach that strengthens performance, leadership pipelines, mobility, and employee growth at scale. The position is based in Washington, DC, reporting to the WBG Director of Talent Management and Development. Key Responsibilities Enterprise Talent and Career Strategy •Lead the design and execution of a cohesive framework that shows clear linkages between talent and performance management and their organizational and individual implications (promotions, career development, internal mobility, etc.). •Translate organizational priorities and workforce needs into simple, scalable, and future-focused talent practices. •Advise senior leaders on leadership pipelines, succession readiness, talent risks, and workforce capabilities. •Lead enterprise talent and succession reviews to strengthen leadership pipelines and succession readiness. •Lead the enterprise career development strategy, including career planning, career pathways, manager-led career conversations, and internal mobility practices that enable employees to navigate opportunities and build future-relevant capabilities. Program Governance, Analytics, and Innovation •Establish enterprise standards, governance, decision rights, metrics, and accountability for talent and career practices. •Use workforce data, employee listening, external benchmarks, and program evaluation to improve effectiveness, fairness, adoption, and business impact. •Lead the adoption of AI-enabled and digital talent solutions to enhance talent reviews, career development, internal mobility, succession planning, and employee experience while ensuring appropriate governance, transparency, fairness, and human oversight. •Monitor external trends and translate relevant practices into practical solutions for WBG. High- Performance Culture •Strengthen a culture of high performance, accountability, continuous development, mobility, and employee growth. •Ensure talent decisions and practices are transparent, evidence-based, inclusive, and consistently applied. •Partner with HR Business Partners, Leadership Development, and other Centers of Excellence to build manager and leadership capability. •Align performance, development, promotions, talent reviews, succession planning, and mobility into a coherent employee and manager experience. Leadership, Culture, and Team Management •Lead, develop, and empower a high-performing team, with clear priorities, accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning. •Lead enterprise-wide transformation and change management for new and evolving talent practices. •Build trusted partnerships across HR and the business and influence senior stakeholders through strong judgment, business acumen, and evidence-based insights. •Balance long-term strategy with disciplined execution and measurable delivery.

item.title: Senior HR Specialist - Talent Management
item.description: At the World Bank Group (WBG), your work shapes the future. With 189 member countries and a mission to end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity, WBG is one of the world’s most impactful development organizations. We rely on the strength of our people: broad representation, driven, and determined to deliver knowledge and results globally. BACKGROUND AND UNIT SUMMARY The WBG Talent Management and Development Department, a core function within Human Resources, shapes the World Bank Group's talent strategy, building the workforce and leadership capabilities needed to deliver its mission. Through innovative talent solutions and programs, it enables performance, career growth, leadership development, and organizational effectiveness. The incumbent will lead some of the enterprise-wide talent processes that help maximize the contributions of our staff and leaders at World Bank. This role will be responsible for designing, delivering, and continuously improving specific talent processes - including talent, succession planning and promotions. The incumbent will work closely with colleagues across the organization and other Centers of Expertise to ensure talent solutions are relevant, scalable, and flexible for our internationally diverse workforce. This requires in-depth expertise in the areas of talent management, career development, as well as strong client relationship management and teamwork. The position is based in Washington, DC and reports to the WBG Manager, Talent and Career Development. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: •Lead the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of talent practices, including talent reviews, succession planning, and promotions, ensuring they meet current and future business needs. •Serve as a thought partner to Talent Management leaders and senior stakeholders by providing insights, external perspectives, and practical recommendations on talent priorities. •Turn talent strategy into practical, scalable frameworks, tools, processes, and implementation plans that improve talent outcomes and the employee and manager experience. •Provide expert guidance to HR Business Partners and people leaders on talent management practices, helping convert talent decisions into meaningful development, career, mobility, and succession actions. •Lead talent programs and cross-functional initiatives from design to implementation, managing plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, and stakeholder engagement to deliver results. •Develop clear and compelling communications, presentations, and materials that support decision-making and stakeholder alignment. •Build strong partnerships across HR and the business to drive alignment, engagement, and successful execution of talent priorities. •Partner with HR Technology teams to improve talent systems and processes by leveraging data, technology, and user feedback. •Lead change management efforts for talent initiatives, equipping leaders, managers, and HR partners with the tools and guidance needed to apply talent practices effectively. •Use data, research, benchmarking, and industry trends to identify opportunities, develop recommendations, and strengthen talent programs. •Define success measures, track outcomes, and use data and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve program effectiveness, simplicity, and impact. •Demonstrate sound judgment, adaptability, and problem-solving in complex situations while supporting broader Talent Management and Development priorities and enterprise initiatives.
